The central government prescribes the standards as recommended by the ICAI, in consultation with and after examination of the recommendations made by the NFRA, and only a notified standard is authoritative under Indian law.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 1 Financial Reporting
citation.ref: Ch. Introduction to Ind AS — process of development and finalisation of Indian Accounting Standards

concepts.section: Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 101 — Previous GAAP carrying amount as deemed cost, all or nothing
concepts.statement: A first-time adopter has four ways of measuring property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and right-of-use assets in the opening Ind AS balance sheet, and they do not all behave the same way. Applying the relevant standards retrospectively, using fair value at the date of transition, and using a previous GAAP revaluation that was at its date broadly comparable to fair value or to cost or depreciated cost adjusted for a general or specific price index may each be chosen item by item, one plant retrospectively and another at fair value. The fourth is different: continuing with the previous GAAP carrying amount is available only where there is no change in functional currency, and only if it is applied to all of the asset classes and every item within them. It also extends to investment property, which is the only route to deemed cost there, since Ind AS 40 permits only the cost model and fair value as deemed cost is therefore not available for investment property. Carrying amount means the net book value on the date of transition and not the original cost, so future depreciation runs on that net book value over the remaining useful life, reviewed at least annually as Ind AS 16 requires. Different entities within a group may choose different bases in their own standalone financial statements; for the consolidated financial statements the entire group is treated as one reporting entity and different bases across its entities are not permissible.

citation.ref: Ch. Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS — deemed cost for property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and right-of-use assets, paragraphs D5 to D7AA

concepts.section: Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 101 — The mandatory exception for derecognition
concepts.statement: Ind AS 101 has two kinds of relief and they run in opposite directions. An optional exemption is an election the first-time adopter may take. A mandatory exception is a prohibition on going back, and it binds whether the entity wants it or not. For derecognition the exception is that a first-time adopter shall apply the derecognition requirements in Ind AS 109 prospectively for transactions occurring on or after the date of transition. A non-derivative financial asset or liability derecognised under previous GAAP as the result of a transaction occurring before that date is therefore not recognised again under Ind AS, even where the Ind AS 109 criteria would not have been met — an NBFC that securitised a loan portfolio to a trust before transition, and derecognised it under Indian GAAP, does not bring it back on to the balance sheet. The items return only if a later transaction or event qualifies them for recognition. One door is left open: the entity may apply the derecognition requirements retrospectively from a date of the entity's choosing, but only where the information needed to apply Ind AS 109 to those past transactions was obtained at the time of initially accounting for them, not reconstructed afterwards.

citation.ref: Ch. Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS — mandatory exceptions, derecognition of financial assets and financial liabilities

concepts.section: Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 101 — Resetting cumulative translation differences at transition
concepts.statement: Ind AS 21 accumulates the exchange differences on translating a foreign operation in a separate component of equity and reclassifies them to profit or loss when the operation is disposed of, so a first-time adopter would in principle have to rebuild that accumulated balance for every foreign operation from the day each was acquired. Ind AS 101 offers an election out of it. If the exemption is used, the first-time adopter need not recognise those translation differences in other comprehensive income from the beginning and need not reclassify the pre-transition cumulative amounts on a later disposal, and the cumulative translation differences are deemed to be zero for all foreign operations at the date of transition. It is not available for one foreign operation and refused for another. The consequence carries to the far end: the gain or loss on a subsequent disposal of a foreign operation shall exclude the translation differences that arose before the date of transition and shall include only those arising after it.

citation.ref: Ch. Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS — optional exemptions, cumulative translation differences

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — what it is, and what happens when it and an Ind AS disagree
concepts.statement: The Conceptual Framework is not a Standard. It does not override any Ind AS or any requirement inside one, and it is not part of the set of standards the standard-setter pronounces. It is written first for the standard-setter, to keep the Standards built on consistent concepts. It reaches a preparer in only two situations — developing a consistent accounting policy where no Ind AS applies to a transaction or event, and where an Ind AS allows a choice of accounting policy — and it serves everybody in a third way, as an aid to understanding and interpreting the Standards. Where the standard-setter decides that meeting the objective of financial reporting requires a Standard to depart from an aspect of the Framework, it does so deliberately and explains the departure in the Appendix to that Ind AS. So a preparer who finds an Ind AS pointing one way and the Framework's concepts pointing another has no choice to make. The Ind AS governs, and the Framework is not authority for leaving it.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the statement that the Conceptual Framework is not a Standard and does not override any Standard or any requirement in a Standard, its three purposes of assisting the standard-setter, assisting preparers where no Standard applies or where a Standard allows a choice, and assisting all parties to interpret the Standards, together with the requirement that a deliberate departure is explained in the Appendix to the relevant Ind AS

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — whom the statements are for, and the three things they cannot do
concepts.statement: The objective of general purpose financial reporting is to give financial information about the reporting entity that is useful to existing and potential investors, lenders and other creditors in deciding whether to give the entity resources. Those decisions are of three kinds — buying, selling or holding equity and debt instruments; providing or settling loans and other credit; and exercising rights to vote on or otherwise influence what management does with the entity's economic resources. The information serves two assessments at once, the prospects for future net cash inflows to the entity and management's stewardship of the entity's economic resources, and stewardship is part of the objective rather than something outside it. Three limitations sit alongside. The reports do not and cannot carry everything those users need, who must also read economic conditions, political events and industry outlooks elsewhere. They are not designed to show the value of the reporting entity, only to help users estimate it. And they are not primarily directed at other parties — regulators and members of the public are not the primary users, however much they read them.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the objective of general purpose financial reporting and the three classes of decision it serves, the inclusion of management's stewardship of the entity's economic resources, and the three stated limitations that general purpose financial reports cannot provide all the information users need, are not designed to show the value of the reporting entity, and are not primarily directed to parties other than investors, lenders and other creditors

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — relevance, and why materiality has no fixed percentage
concepts.statement: Information is relevant if it is capable of making a difference to the decisions users take, and it does that through predictive value, confirmatory value, or both. Predictive value does not mean the information is a forecast — it means users can feed it into their own predictions, so this year's revenue analysis has predictive value while being entirely historical. The same information usually has confirmatory value too, because it lets a user check the predictions made last year and mend the process that produced them. Materiality is not a separate characteristic sitting beside relevance; it is the entity-specific aspect of relevance. Information is material if omitting it, misstating it or obscuring it could reasonably be expected to influence the decisions primary users make on the basis of that entity's reports, and the test runs on the nature of the item or its magnitude or both, judged in the context of that individual entity. That is exactly why the standard-setter cannot lay down a uniform quantitative threshold or decide in advance what will be material — a percentage of profit imported from a group manual is a starting point for an auditor, never the answer to the question the Framework asks.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the definition of relevance through predictive value and confirmatory value, the statement that information need not be a prediction or forecast to have predictive value, and the treatment of materiality as an entity-specific aspect of relevance based on the nature or magnitude or both of the items concerned, on which no uniform quantitative threshold can be specified in advance

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — faithful representation, and the word the Framework does not use
concepts.statement: To be useful, information must faithfully represent the substance of what it purports to represent. Where substance and legal form are the same, reporting the form is enough; where they differ, reporting only the form does not faithfully represent the transaction. A perfectly faithful depiction has three characteristics. Complete — all the descriptions and explanations a user needs to understand the item, including how a figure was arrived at. Neutral — no bias in what is selected or how it is presented, nothing slanted, weighted, emphasised, de-emphasised or otherwise manipulated to make the information land favourably or unfavourably. Free from error — no errors or omissions in the description and no errors in selecting and applying the process that produced the figure. Free from error does not mean accurate. An estimate of an unobservable value cannot be called accurate or inaccurate at all, and it is still a faithful representation if it is clearly described as an estimate, the nature and limits of the estimating process are explained, and the process was chosen and run without error. The outcome differing from the estimate does not make the estimate wrong. And note the word that is absent — the Framework's two fundamental characteristics are relevance and faithful representation, and reliability is not one of them. Ind AS 8 still uses "reliable" when it tells management how to develop a policy, and there faithful representation is only one of five limbs of reliability, alongside substance over form, neutrality, prudence and completeness.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the requirement that information faithfully represent the substance of the phenomenon rather than its legal form, the three characteristics of a perfectly faithful depiction as complete, neutral and free from error, and the statement that free from error does not mean perfectly accurate in all respects; read against Ind AS 8, which frames the same ground as relevance and reliability with faithful representation as one limb of reliability

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — prudence is caution, and it cuts both ways
concepts.statement: Neutrality is supported by the exercise of prudence, and prudence in the Framework means one thing only — the exercise of caution when making judgements under conditions of uncertainty. It is not conservatism and it is not a licence for a cushion. The rule is stated in both directions and the second direction is the one that gets forgotten. Exercising prudence means assets and income are not overstated and liabilities and expenses are not understated; equally, it does not allow assets or income to be understated or liabilities or expenses to be overstated. So an adjustment that deliberately pushes a provision above the best estimate, or an asset below it, fails prudence rather than satisfying it, and it fails neutrality too, because a depiction weighted to be received unfavourably is as far from neutral as one weighted the other way. Prudence is not itself a qualitative characteristic in the Framework's list — it supports neutrality, which is one of the three limbs of faithful representation.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the statement that neutrality is supported by the exercise of prudence, the definition of prudence as the exercise of caution when making judgements under conditions of uncertainty, and the paired requirements that prudence means assets and income are not overstated and liabilities and expenses are not understated, and equally does not allow the understatement of assets or income or the overstatement of liabilities or expenses

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — the four enhancing characteristics and what they cannot rescue
concepts.statement: Comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability enhance the usefulness of information that is already relevant and already a faithful representation. Singly or together they cannot make information useful if it is irrelevant or does not faithfully represent what it purports to. Comparability is the goal and consistency is the means of reaching it — using the same methods for the same items, period to period and entity to entity — and neither is uniformity, which would make unlike things look alike. Verifiability means different knowledgeable and independent observers could reach consensus, though not necessarily complete agreement, that a depiction is faithful; it is direct where an amount is observed, such as by counting cash, and indirect where the inputs to a model are checked and the output recalculated on the same method. Timeliness is having the information in time to influence a decision, and older information is generally less useful though it can stay useful for spotting trends. Understandability is achieved by classifying, characterising and presenting clearly — but some phenomena are inherently complex, and leaving them out to make the report easier would make it incomplete and possibly misleading. The reports are written for users with a reasonable knowledge of business who review and analyse diligently, and even they may need an adviser. Applying these four is iterative with no prescribed order, and one may be deliberately reduced to maximise another. Over the whole exercise sits the cost constraint — the benefit of reporting information must justify the cost of providing and using it.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the four enhancing qualitative characteristics and the requirement that they cannot make irrelevant or unfaithfully represented information useful, the distinction between comparability as the goal, consistency as the means and uniformity as neither, the direct and indirect forms of verification, the statement that excluding inherently complex information would make reports incomplete and possibly misleading, and the cost constraint on useful financial information

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — a reporting entity need not be a legal entity
concepts.statement: A reporting entity is an entity that is required, or chooses, to prepare financial statements. It can be a single entity, a portion of an entity, or more than one entity, and it is not necessarily a legal entity. Where it comprises a parent and its subsidiaries the statements are consolidated; where it is the parent alone they are separate or standalone; where it comprises two or more entities not all linked by a parent-subsidiary relationship they are combined financial statements. When the boundary is not settled by legal form, it is drawn from the information needs of the primary users, and faithful representation puts three requirements on it — the set of economic activities inside must not be arbitrary or incomplete, including that set must produce neutral information, and the statements must describe how the boundary was determined and what the reporting entity consists of. Consolidated statements are not designed to give information about any particular subsidiary, which is what that subsidiary's own statements are for. And unconsolidated statements, however useful to a parent's own creditors, are typically not enough for them, so where consolidated statements are required the unconsolidated ones cannot be put in their place.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the definition of a reporting entity as one required or choosing to prepare financial statements, which may be a single entity, a portion of an entity or more than one entity and need not be a legal entity, the naming of consolidated, separate and combined financial statements, the three faithful representation requirements on determining a boundary that is not set by legal form, and the statement that unconsolidated financial statements cannot serve as a substitute where consolidated financial statements are required

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — an asset is a present right, not an expected inflow
concepts.statement: An asset is a present economic resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events, and an economic resource is a right that has the potential to produce economic benefits. There are three aspects to work through — a right, the potential to produce benefits, and control — and the middle one is where the definition parts company with the older wording. For the potential to exist it need not be certain or even likely that the right will produce anything. It is enough that the right already exists and that in at least one circumstance it would produce benefits for this entity beyond those available to everybody else. So a right whose probability of paying is low is still an asset, and the low probability moves to the separate questions of whether the asset is recognised and how it is measured. That is a lower bar than the older definition still carried in Ind AS 38, which asks for a resource from which future economic benefits are expected to flow and then adds a probability criterion on top before anything may be recognised. Two further traps. The economic resource is the present right, not the future benefits the right may produce — the resource in a purchased option is the right to exercise it, not the money that exercising it might bring. And expenditure is evidence that the entity sought benefits, never proof that it obtained an asset, while the absence of expenditure proves nothing either way, since a right granted free by a government or donated by somebody else is as much an asset as a purchased one.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the definition of an asset as a present economic resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events and of an economic resource as a right that has the potential to produce economic benefits, the statement that the potential need not be certain or even likely and that a right can be an asset even where the probability of economic benefits is low, the role of timing under which the resource is the present right rather than the future benefits, and the role of expenditure under which incurring expenditure is not conclusive proof of an asset and its absence does not preclude one; read against the definition and probability recognition criterion in Ind AS 38

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — control, the agent, and the right an entity cannot hold against itself
concepts.statement: Control links an economic resource to an entity, and it is what identifies which resource the entity accounts for — an entity controlling a proportionate share of a property has that share as its asset, not the rights over the whole. An entity controls a resource if it has the present ability to direct its use, meaning to deploy it in the entity's own activities or let another party deploy it, and to obtain the economic benefits that may flow from it. Control includes the ability to prevent others from doing either, and it follows that if one party controls a resource no other party does. It usually rests on enforceable legal rights but need not — know-how kept out of the public domain can be controlled by an entity with access to it and the ability to keep it secret, with no patent anywhere. Exposure to significant variation in the benefits a resource produces may indicate control, but it is one factor in an overall assessment rather than the test. Two limits complete the picture. Where a principal engages an agent, a resource in the agent's custody that the principal controls is not the agent's asset, and the agent's duty to hand it to a third party is not the agent's liability, because the resource to be transferred is the principal's. And an entity cannot hold a right to obtain benefits from itself, so its own shares bought back and held are not its economic resources, and instruments issued by one member of a group and held by another are not the group's.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the two limbs of control as the present ability to direct the use of the economic resource and to obtain the economic benefits that may flow from it, the statement that if one party controls a resource no other party controls it, the treatment of a principal and agent under which a resource in the agent's custody controlled by the principal is not the agent's asset, and the statement that an entity cannot have a right to obtain economic benefits from itself so that repurchased own instruments and intragroup instruments are not economic resources

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — a liability turns on what the entity cannot practically avoid
concepts.statement: A liability is a present obligation of the entity to transfer an economic resource as a result of past events, and all three criteria must hold. An obligation is a duty or responsibility the entity has no practical ability to avoid, always owed to another party, though the identity of that party need not be known. Many obligations come from contract or legislation; others arise from an entity's customary practices, published policies or specific statements where it has no practical ability to act inconsistently with them, and those are constructive obligations. Where a transfer is conditional on an action the entity may itself choose to take, there is an obligation only if it has no practical ability to avoid taking that action — and a conclusion that the going concern basis is appropriate is itself a conclusion that the entity cannot avoid a transfer escapable only by liquidating or ceasing to trade. Neither an intention to make a transfer nor a high likelihood of one is enough on its own. The transfer criterion is deliberately weak — it need not be certain or even likely that a transfer will be required, only that in at least one circumstance the obligation would require one, so an obligation with a low probability of transfer still meets the definition. The past event criterion is the strict one. A present obligation exists only if the entity has already obtained economic benefits or already taken an action, and as a consequence will or may have to transfer a resource it would not otherwise have had to transfer. Timing of enforcement is irrelevant to this — a liability to pay cash next year exists now.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the three criteria for a liability, the definition of an obligation as a duty or responsibility the entity has no practical ability to avoid, the treatment of constructive obligations arising from customary practices, published policies or specific statements, the statement that a conclusion that the going concern basis is appropriate implies a conclusion that the entity has no practical ability to avoid a transfer that could be avoided only by liquidating or ceasing to trade, the statement that neither an intention nor a high likelihood of a transfer is sufficient, and the requirement that a present obligation arises from a past event only where the entity has already obtained economic benefits or taken an action

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — choosing the thing the criteria are applied to
concepts.statement: The unit of account is the right or group of rights, the obligation or group of obligations, or the group of rights and obligations, to which the recognition criteria and the measurement concepts are applied. It is selected to provide useful information, which means the information about the item and about the income and expenses it produces must be relevant and must faithfully represent the substance of what gave rise to them. It need not be the same choice throughout — one unit of account may be selected for recognition and a different one for measurement, so contracts can be recognised individually and measured as a portfolio, and for presentation items may be aggregated or split again. In principle each right is a separate asset, but related rights are usually treated as one: ownership of land carries rights to use it, to sell rights over it, to pledge it and more, and calling the bundle a single asset is normally the most concise faithful representation of them. Where rights and obligations arise from the same source and are interdependent so that they cannot be separated, they are a single inseparable asset or liability; where they are separable it may be right to group them apart. A group or series of contracts designed to achieve one overall commercial effect may have to be treated as a single unit of account — if one contract nullifies the rights and obligations in another entered into at the same time with the same counterparty, together they create nothing at all. And a single contract creating two sets of rights that could have been two contracts may need to be accounted for as if it were. Offsetting is a different operation and is generally not appropriate: it takes an asset and a liability that are separate units of account and groups them into one net figure in the balance sheet, which classifies dissimilar things together.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the definition of the unit of account as the right or group of rights, obligation or group of obligations, or group of rights and obligations to which recognition criteria and measurement concepts are applied, the statement that one unit of account may be selected for recognition and a different one for measurement, the treatment of interdependent rights and obligations from the same source as a single inseparable asset or liability, the requirement to report the substance of a group or series of contracts achieving an overall commercial effect, and the statement that offsetting differs from treating a set of rights and obligations as a single unit of account

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — the contract neither side has performed
concepts.statement: An executory contract, or a portion of a contract, is one that is equally unperformed — neither party has fulfilled any of its obligations, or both have partially fulfilled to an equal extent. It establishes a combined right and obligation to exchange economic resources, and because the two are interdependent and cannot be separated they are a single asset or a single liability rather than a right on one side and an obligation on the other. Which of the two it is depends on the terms as they stand now — the entity has an asset if the terms of the exchange are currently favourable to it and a liability if they are currently unfavourable, and a contract can move from one to the other as prices move. Whether that asset or liability appears in the financial statements is a separate question, and the definition does not answer it: that turns on the recognition criteria and on the measurement basis selected, including any test for whether the contract has become onerous. And a contract stops being executory to the extent one side performs. An employment contract creates no present obligation to pay salary until the services have been received, because until then the entity holds a combined right to future services and obligation to pay for them.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the definition of an executory contract as a contract or portion of a contract that is equally unperformed, the treatment of the combined right and obligation as a single inseparable asset or liability, the test that the entity has an asset where the terms of the exchange are currently favourable and a liability where they are currently unfavourable, and the statement that whether the asset or liability is included in the financial statements depends on the recognition criteria and the measurement basis selected including any onerous test

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — meeting a definition is necessary and not sufficient
concepts.statement: Recognition is the process of capturing an item that meets the definition of an element for inclusion in the balance sheet or the statement of profit and loss, at an amount called its carrying amount. Only items meeting a definition may be recognised — but not every item meeting a definition is recognised. An asset or liability is recognised only where recognition gives users of the financial statements information that is useful, which means both relevant and a faithful representation of the item and of any income, expenses or changes in equity it produces. Relevance can fail in two ways, neither of them automatic and neither of them decisive alone: where it is uncertain whether the asset or liability exists, and where it exists but the probability of an inflow or outflow is low. Faithful representation can fail where the level of measurement uncertainty is so high that no available measure would be useful — a range of outcomes that is exceptionally wide, a measure exceptionally sensitive to small changes in probabilities, or an allocation of cash flows that is exceptionally subjective — and in those limited circumstances the item is not recognised. Not recognising does not end the entity's duty: information about the item may still be needed in the notes, made visible enough to compensate for its absence from the balance sheet. Two things the Framework does not contain are worth naming. There is no probability threshold and no separate "can be measured reliably" criterion, which is why Ind AS 38's probable-benefits-and-reliable-cost test is a narrower gate than the Framework's. And matching costs with income is not an objective of the Framework — the simultaneous recognition of income and related expenses is a consequence of the balance sheet entries, not a reason to park in the balance sheet something that is not an asset, a liability or equity.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the definition of recognition and of the carrying amount, the two recognition criteria of relevant information and faithful representation, the treatment of existence uncertainty and a low probability of an inflow or outflow as factors that may but do not automatically defeat relevance, the limited circumstances in which measurement uncertainty is so high that the item is not recognised, the requirement to consider information in the notes for an unrecognised item, and the statement that matching of costs with income is not an objective of the Conceptual Framework and does not permit the recognition of items failing the definitions

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — taking it off, and what is left behind
concepts.statement: Derecognition is the removal of all or part of a recognised asset or liability from the balance sheet, and it normally happens when the item stops meeting the definition — for an asset, when the entity loses control of all or part of it; for a liability, when it no longer has a present obligation for all or part of it. The mechanics have three limbs. Derecognise the transferred component, meaning whatever has expired, been consumed, collected, fulfilled or transferred, and recognise the income and expenses that result. Continue to recognise the retained component, which now becomes a unit of account separate from the transferred component — and because it is a separate unit, no income or expense is recognised on it merely because the other part went, unless the derecognition changes the measurement requirements that apply to it, as happens when a parent loses control of a subsidiary and must remeasure the holding it keeps to fair value. Then present the retained component separately, present separately the income and expenses arising on the transferred component, and explain. The trap is that an apparent transfer is not always a derecognition. Where the entity has seemingly transferred an asset but keeps exposure to significant positive or negative variation in the benefits that asset may produce, that sometimes indicates it still controls it; and where the transferee holds the asset as the entity's agent, the transferor controls it still.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the definition of derecognition and the statement that it normally occurs when an asset's control is lost or a liability's present obligation ceases, the requirements to derecognise the transferred component and recognise the resulting income and expenses, to continue recognising the retained component as a separate unit of account with no income or expenses arising on it unless the measurement requirements change, and the statements that retained exposure to significant variations in the benefits may indicate continuing control and that a transferee holding an asset as agent leaves control with the transferor

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — historical cost against the three current values, and how one is chosen
concepts.statement: A measurement basis is an identified feature of the item being measured, and applying one creates a measure for the item and for the related income and expenses. There are four to tell apart. Historical cost, derived from the price of the transaction that gave rise to the item and updated only for consumption, collection or fulfilment, for impairment or onerousness, and for the accrual of interest on any financing component — it does not reflect changes in value. And three current values, all updated to conditions at the measurement date. Fair value, the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants — a market participant's perspective, an exit value, measured without deducting the transaction costs of disposal and taking no account of the costs of acquisition either. Value in use for an asset and fulfilment value for a liability, the present value of the cash flows the entity expects to derive from using and finally disposing of the asset, or expects to be obliged to transfer in fulfilling the liability — entity-specific assumptions, not observable directly, estimated with cash-flow techniques, ignoring the costs on initial recognition but including the present value of the costs to be incurred on disposal or settlement. And current cost, which like historical cost is an entry value made of consideration and transaction costs, but determined at each measurement date rather than fixed at acquisition. Choosing between them is judgement, not preference. Where resources produce cash flows indirectly by being used in combination, as plant and inventory are, historical cost or current cost is likely to be the relevant basis; where an asset produces cash flows directly and can be sold independently without significant penalty, a current value is likely to be. Using different bases for assets and liabilities whose cash flows are directly linked creates an accounting mismatch and can defeat faithful representation. So Ind AS is deliberately a mixed measurement system rather than a fair value system, and mixed does not mean inconsistent.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — the two concepts of capital, and the profit each one leaves
concepts.statement: An entity chooses a concept of capital from what its users care about. Where they care about maintaining the nominal amount of money invested or its purchasing power, the financial concept applies and capital is net assets or equity. Where they care about the entity's operating capability, the physical concept applies and capital is productive capacity. The choice is not cosmetic, because the concept of capital maintenance is what fixes the point of reference for profit — an entity has made a profit only to the extent it ends the period with more capital than it began with, after excluding distributions to and contributions from owners. Under financial capital maintenance a profit arises only where the money amount of net assets at the end exceeds the money amount at the beginning, and that can be measured in nominal monetary units or in units of constant purchasing power. Under physical capital maintenance a profit arises only where the physical productive capacity at the end exceeds that at the beginning. The principal difference between the two is how they treat changes in the prices of the entity's assets and liabilities, and it produces three different answers to one set of facts. In nominal monetary units, holding gains on assets held over the period are conceptually profits, though they may not be recognised as such until the assets are disposed of in an exchange transaction. In units of constant purchasing power, only the part of a price increase that exceeds the rise in the general price level is profit and the rest is a capital maintenance adjustment in equity. Under the physical concept, every price change affecting the entity's assets and liabilities is treated as a change in the measure of its productive capacity, so the whole of it is a capital maintenance adjustment in equity and none of it is profit.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: the financial and physical concepts of capital and the basis on which an entity selects between them, the definitions of financial capital maintenance in nominal monetary units and in units of constant purchasing power and of physical capital maintenance, the exclusion of distributions to and contributions from owners in each, and the statements that holding gains are conceptually profits under nominal financial capital maintenance, that only the increase exceeding the general level of prices is profit under constant purchasing power with the rest treated as a capital maintenance adjustment in equity, and that under physical capital maintenance all price changes are capital maintenance adjustments that are part of equity

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: Revenue is recognised when (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control of the promised good or service to the customer. Transfer of control, not transfer of risks and rewards, is the recognition trigger.

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 2 — Inventories
concepts.statement: Inventories of items that are not ordinarily interchangeable are costed by specific identification. For the rest, FIFO or weighted average is used. LIFO is not permitted.

citation.ref: para 23 to 25

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Consolidated Financial Statements
concepts.statement: An investor controls an investee only when it has all three elements together — power over the investee, exposure or rights to variable returns, and the ability to use its power to affect those returns. Control does not require a majority shareholding.

citation.ref: para 7

concepts.section: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Financial Instruments
concepts.statement: Loss allowances are measured on an expected credit loss basis, recognised from initial recognition without waiting for a default. For trade receivables the simplified approach applies, and the allowance is always lifetime expected credit losses.

citation.ref: para 5.5.15

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Business Combinations
concepts.statement: Under the Indian carve-out, a gain on a bargain purchase is recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in capital reserve, not in profit or loss — unlike IFRS 3, which takes it to profit or loss.

citation.ref: para 34 and 36

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: A performance obligation is satisfied over time only when one of three criteria is met — the customer consumes the benefit as the entity performs, the customer controls the asset as it is created, or the asset has no alternative use and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance to date. Otherwise control passes at a point in time.

citation.ref: para 35

concepts.section: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
concepts.statement: A provision is recognised only when all three conditions hold — a present obligation, legal or constructive, from a past event; a probable outflow of resources; and a reliable estimate. For a restructuring, the obligating event is announcing the plan to those affected or beginning to implement it, never the board decision alone.

citation.ref: para 14 and 72

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 16 — Property, Plant and Equipment
concepts.statement: The cost of a major inspection or overhaul that is a condition of continuing to operate an asset is capitalised into the asset's carrying amount when incurred, and any remaining carrying amount of the previous inspection is derecognised — even if the previous inspection's cost was never separately identified.

citation.ref: para 13 and 14

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 21 — The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
concepts.statement: At each reporting date, foreign currency monetary items are translated at the closing rate, with exchange differences to profit or loss. Non-monetary items carried at historical cost stay at the transaction-date rate. Whether an item is money fixes which rate it gets.

citation.ref: para 23

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 38 — Intangible Assets
concepts.statement: Internally generated goodwill is never recognised as an asset, and internally generated brands, mastheads, customer lists and similar items are barred with it. Development costs are the exception, capitalised only from the day all six conditions are demonstrated; research is always expensed.

citation.ref: para 48, 54 and 63

concepts.section: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 108 — Operating Segments
concepts.statement: An operating segment is separately reportable if it crosses ten per cent of combined revenue (internal plus external), of the greater of combined profits or combined losses, or of combined assets — and reportable segments must together cover seventy-five per cent of external revenue, adding segments until they do.

citation.ref: para 13 and 15

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 1 — Presentation of Financial Statements
concepts.statement: A liability is current when the entity lacks, at the reporting date, the right to defer settlement for at least twelve months. A covenant breached by the year end makes the loan payable on demand and therefore current — unless the lender agreed, on or before the reporting date, not to demand payment; a waiver arriving after the year end comes too late to change the classification.

citation.ref: para 74 and 75

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Statement of Cash Flows
concepts.statement: Under the Indian carve-out, an entity other than a financial institution classifies interest paid as a financing cash flow and interest and dividends received as investing — the options IFRS offers are removed. A bank classifies all of them as operating, because lending is its business.

citation.ref: para 33

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Leases
concepts.statement: A lessee recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for every lease, with two elections out — leases of twelve months or less with no purchase option, and leases of low-value assets. The exemptions are elections about recognition, not about whether the contract is a lease.

citation.ref: para 5 and 6

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 36 — Impairment of Assets
concepts.statement: An asset is impaired when its carrying amount exceeds its recoverable amount, and recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use. Higher — the entity keeps the better of selling and using, so either measure alone can clear the asset of impairment.

citation.ref: para 6

concepts.section: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 10 — Events after the Reporting Period
concepts.statement: An event after the reporting period adjusts the financial statements only when it evidences a condition that existed at the reporting date; a condition that arose afterwards is disclosed, not adjusted. Dividends declared after the reporting period are the standard's own worked example — no liability at the reporting date, however certain the declaration.

citation.ref: para 3 and 12

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 105 — Non-current Assets Held for Sale
concepts.statement: Held-for-sale classification needs the asset available for immediate sale in its present condition and the sale highly probable — management committed to a plan, an active programme to find a buyer, active marketing at a reasonable price, and completion expected within a year. Once classified, the asset is measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, and depreciation stops.

citation.ref: para 6-8

concepts.section: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 8 — Policies, Estimates and Errors
concepts.statement: A change in accounting policy is applied retrospectively, restating comparatives as if the new policy had always applied; a change in accounting estimate is recognised prospectively, in the period of change and the future. Where the two are hard to tell apart, the standard itself says treat the change as an estimate. Depreciation method and useful life are estimates; measurement basis is policy.

citation.ref: para 19 and 36

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 23 — Borrowing Costs
concepts.statement: Borrowing costs directly attributable to acquiring, constructing or producing a qualifying asset — one that necessarily takes a substantial period to get ready for its intended use or sale — are capitalised as part of the asset's cost; all other borrowing costs are expensed. Capitalisation is suspended during extended periods when active development pauses, and ends when the asset is substantially ready.

citation.ref: para 8

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 40 — Investment Property
concepts.statement: Ind AS 40 permits only the cost model for investment property — the Indian carve-out removed IAS 40's fair value model. Fair value is still measured and disclosed in the notes, but the balance sheet carries cost less depreciation and impairment. Property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation, not for use in production or administration, is what the standard covers.

concepts.section: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 113 — Fair Value Measurement
concepts.statement: The fair value hierarchy ranks inputs, not techniques: Level 1 is unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical items; Level 2 is other observable inputs — quoted prices for similar items, or corroborated market data; Level 3 is unobservable inputs. A measurement sits at the lowest level of any input significant to it, and Level 1 prices are used unadjusted where available.

citation.ref: para 76, 81 and 86

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 102 — Share-based Payment
concepts.statement: For equity-settled awards to employees, the expense is measured at the fair value of the equity instruments at grant date — and that value is never remeasured, however the share price moves. What does move is the number of awards expected to vest under service and non-market conditions, trued up each period until vesting. Market conditions are priced into grant-date value once and never trued up.

citation.ref: para 10-11

concepts.section: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 19 — Employee Benefits
concepts.statement: Defined benefit cost splits three ways: service cost and net interest go to profit or loss; remeasurements — actuarial gains and losses, and the return on plan assets beyond the amount already in net interest — go to other comprehensive income, and once there they are never reclassified to profit or loss. The split keeps the operating result clear of actuarial volatility without hiding it.

citation.ref: para 120 and 122

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Investments in Associates
concepts.statement: Twenty per cent or more of voting power presumes significant influence — the power to participate in financial and operating policy decisions — and less than twenty presumes its absence; both presumptions yield to clear demonstration otherwise. Board representation, policy participation, material transactions, interchange of personnel or essential technical dependence can evidence influence below the line. An associate is equity accounted, not consolidated.

citation.ref: para 5-6

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — Income Taxes
concepts.statement: A deferred tax asset on unused tax losses is recognised only to the extent future taxable profit is probable — and a history of recent losses is itself evidence against that. A loss-making entity records the asset only to the extent of taxable temporary differences or convincing other evidence of future profit, such as a firm order book from a cause that has demonstrably ended.

citation.ref: para 34-35

concepts.section: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Classification of financial assets
concepts.statement: A financial asset is carried at amortised cost only when both tests pass: the business model is to hold and collect contractual cash flows, and those cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest. Held-to-collect with equity-linked returns fails the second; plain-interest bonds bought for trading fail the first. Failures land in fair value categories.

citation.ref: para 4.1.2

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Non-controlling interest at acquisition
concepts.statement: For each business combination, the acquirer measures qualifying non-controlling interest at either full fair value or the proportionate share of the acquiree's identifiable net assets — a choice made combination by combination, not as a standing policy. The choice sets goodwill: fair value NCI produces full goodwill including the minority's share; the proportionate route recognises only the acquirer's goodwill.

citation.ref: para 19

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Lessor accounting
concepts.statement: Lessors still classify: a lease that transfers substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership is a finance lease — derecognise the asset, recognise a receivable; otherwise it is an operating lease — keep the asset, book income over the term. Indicators include ownership transfer, a bargain purchase option, the term covering the major part of economic life, and present value of payments amounting to substantially all the fair value. Lessee accounting became single-model; lessor accounting did not.

concepts.section: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 32 — Liability or equity
concepts.statement: An instrument is classified by substance against the definitions, not by its legal name: a contractual obligation to deliver cash — mandatory redemption, compulsory dividends — makes a financial liability, however the instrument is titled. Preference shares redeemable at the holder's option or on a fixed date are debt; pure discretion over both dividends and redemption keeps an instrument in equity. Classification happens once, at issue.

citation.ref: para 11 and 15

concepts.section: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 33 — EPS and bonus issues
concepts.statement: A bonus issue, split or similar event changes the share count without changing resources, so EPS treats the new count as if it had existed from the beginning of the earliest period presented — restating the comparative EPS too. A fresh issue for cash, by contrast, enters the weighted average only from its date, because new resources arrived then.

citation.ref: para 27-28

concepts.section: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 24 — Related Party Disclosures
concepts.statement: Key management personnel compensation is disclosed in total and by category — short-term, post-employment, other long-term, termination, share-based. Related party disclosure is about relationships and transactions, not approval: arm's length terms may be claimed only if they can be substantiated, and a government-related entity gets a partial exemption for dealings with its government and its sister entities, disclosing the nature and extent instead of every transaction.

citation.ref: para 17

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 34 — Interim Financial Reporting
concepts.statement: Interim statements apply the same accounting policies as the annual ones — a quarter is not a licence for different measurement — and reporting frequency must not change the annual result: measurements run year-to-date, so a third-quarter estimate correction adjusts the year-to-date figures rather than fabricating a standalone quarter. Costs that fail asset definitions at year-end fail them equally at a quarter's end.

citation.ref: para 28

concepts.section: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Onerous contracts
concepts.statement: A contract whose unavoidable costs of fulfilment exceed the benefits expected under it is onerous, and the present obligation is provided for at once — the unavoidable cost being the lower of the cost of fulfilling and the penalty of exiting. Routine cancellable purchase orders create no obligation, and expected future operating losses of the business generally are never provided for; the onerous contract is the exception because the loss is contracted, not merely forecast.

citation.ref: para 66-68

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 111 — Joint operations and joint ventures
concepts.statement: Joint control is contractually agreed sharing of control where the relevant decisions need unanimous consent. The arrangement's type decides the accounting: joint operators have rights to the assets and obligations for the liabilities and record their share of each, line by line; joint venturers have rights only to the net assets and equity-account the investment. Structure through a separate vehicle starts, not ends, the classification.

citation.ref: para 7 and 15-16

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 20 — Government grants
concepts.statement: A government grant is recognised only when there is reasonable assurance the entity will comply with its conditions and the grant will be received. Since the 2018 amendment, a grant related to an asset may be presented either as deferred income released over the asset's life, or by deducting it from the asset's carrying amount — the pre-2018 Indian text had removed the deduction option, and stale materials still teach that removal.

citation.ref: para 7 and 24 (as amended 2018)

concepts.section: Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 101 — First-time adoption
concepts.statement: A first-time adopter may elect deemed cost for property, plant and equipment at the transition date: fair value at that date, or the previous GAAP carrying amount where eligible — instead of rebuilding depreciated cost as if Ind AS had always applied. The elections are optional exemptions from full retrospective application; the general rule remains retrospective, and mandatory exceptions forbid hindsight in estimates.

citation.ref: deemed cost exemption for PPE at transition

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Principal versus agent
concepts.statement: An entity is a principal when it controls the promised good or service before transfer to the customer, reporting gross revenue; an agent arranges for another to provide it, reporting only its fee or commission. Momentary legal title on the way through does not make a principal; inventory risk, primary responsibility for fulfilment and discretion in setting prices indicate control. The revenue difference is presentation, not profit.

citation.ref: para B34-B35

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Loss of control
concepts.statement: When a parent loses control of a subsidiary it derecognises the subsidiary's assets, liabilities and NCI, recognises the consideration received, and measures any retained interest at fair value at that date — that fair value becomes the cost of the new associate or investment. The gain or loss in profit or loss thus includes a remeasurement of the stake kept, not only the stake sold; control is an all-or-nothing line.

citation.ref: para 25

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 16 — Revaluation model
concepts.statement: Under the revaluation model an upward revaluation goes to other comprehensive income and accumulates in equity as revaluation surplus — except to the extent it reverses a decrease earlier charged to profit or loss. A downward revaluation charges profit or loss — except to the extent a surplus for that same asset exists to absorb it. The surplus never passes through profit or loss: on disposal it transfers directly to retained earnings.

citation.ref: para 39-40

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 2 — NRV and the raw materials exception
concepts.statement: Inventories are carried at the lower of cost and net realisable value, item by item — but raw materials are not written down below cost while the finished products they will enter are expected to sell at or above cost. Only when the materials' price decline signals that the finished product's cost exceeds its NRV do the materials write down, with replacement cost as their best available measure.

citation.ref: para 32

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 41 — Agriculture
concepts.statement: Biological assets are measured at each reporting date at fair value less costs to sell, with changes through profit or loss — cost models yield to the market's verdict on living, growing assets. Bearer plants — the tea bush, not the tea leaf — are carved out to Ind AS 16 as plant-like assets, while the produce growing on them stays in Ind AS 41 until harvest, when it moves to Ind AS 2 at its harvest-date fair value as deemed cost.

citation.ref: para 12-13 and scope

concepts.subsection: Schedule III — Mandated ratios and disclosures
concepts.statement: Division II of Schedule III requires eleven named ratios in the notes — current ratio, debt-equity, debt service coverage, return on equity, inventory and receivables and payables turnover, net capital turnover, net profit, return on capital employed, return on investment — with the elements of each computation and an explanation wherever a ratio moved more than twenty-five per cent from the prior year. The amendments also demand disclosure of benami proceedings, undisclosed income surrendered, and crypto holdings.

citation.ref: Schedule III Division II (2021 amendments)

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Sharing an associate's losses
concepts.statement: Equity accounting absorbs an associate's losses only down to zero: once the investor's share of losses equals its interest — the equity-method carrying amount plus long-term interests that are in substance part of the net investment — recognition of further losses stops, resuming only after future profits rebuild the base. Losses beyond zero are provided only where the investor has legal or constructive obligations or made payments for the associate.

citation.ref: para 38-39

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Constraining variable consideration
concepts.statement: Variable consideration — bonuses, penalties, volume rebates, royalties — enters the transaction price only to the extent it is highly probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue will not occur when the uncertainty resolves. Estimation uses the expected value or the most likely amount, whichever predicts better; the constraint then trims the estimate. Booking the hopeful number and reversing later is the pattern the rule exists to stop.

citation.ref: para 56

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Cash and cash equivalents
concepts.statement: Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments readily convertible to known amounts of cash with insignificant risk of value change — normally maturing within about three months of acquisition. Equity investments are excluded save in-substance equivalents. Bank overdrafts repayable on demand that form an integral part of cash management join cash and cash equivalents, turning the statement's bottom line negative-capable.

citation.ref: para 7-8

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Consolidation procedures
concepts.statement: Consolidation combines like items line by line, eliminates the parent's investment against its share of each subsidiary's equity, and eliminates intragroup balances, transactions and unrealised profits in full — not merely the parent's share. The group reports as one economic entity under uniform accounting policies for like transactions, restating a subsidiary's numbers where its policies differ.

citation.ref: para 19 and B86

concepts.subsection: Chapter 6 of the FTP — Who may be an EOU, and the net foreign exchange test
concepts.statement: An Export Oriented Unit undertakes to export its entire production of goods and services, apart from the sales into the domestic tariff area that Chapter 6 itself permits, and it may be set up for manufacture, for repair, remaking, reconditioning and re-engineering, for services and software, and for agriculture, aquaculture, animal husbandry, floriculture, horticulture, poultry and sericulture. Trading units are outside the scheme altogether — the schemes buy export production, not export trading. Only a project with a minimum investment of one crore rupees in plant and machinery is considered for establishment as an EOU, and that floor does not apply to existing units, to units in an EHTP, STP or BTP, or to EOUs in handicrafts, agriculture, floriculture, aquaculture, animal husbandry, information technology, services, brass hardware and handmade jewellery; the Board of Approval may allow a lower floor besides. The obligation the whole scheme turns on is not a fixed export figure. The unit shall be a positive net foreign exchange earner, and the earning is computed cumulatively in blocks of five years beginning from the commencement of production, so a bad year is answered by the rest of its block rather than by a default. Where a product in the letter of permission is prohibited or restricted for export, the Board of Approval may extend that five year block; where the unit is in genuine hardship or an adverse market, it may extend it by up to one year, case by case. The unit executes a legal undertaking with the Development Commissioner, and failure to earn positive net foreign exchange or to keep the terms of the letter of permission exposes it to penal action under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act and to cancellation of that letter.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 6.00(a), 6.04, 6.05(c) and 6.06 of Chapter 6, read with Appendix 6B for the sector-specific value addition

concepts.subsection: Paragraph 6.07 — What an EOU may sell at home, and the four different conditions
concepts.statement: The rule is that the entire production of an EOU shall be exported; every domestic sale is an exception Chapter 6 grants, and the exceptions do not share one condition. Finished goods specified in the letter of permission, and the by-products, rejects, waste and scrap thrown off in making them, may be sold into the domestic tariff area only if they are freely importable under the policy and only on fulfilment of positive net foreign exchange, on payment of goods and services tax and compensation cess together with reversal of the customs duties that were availed as exemption on the inputs used in them, the reversal following the standard input output norms; an amount equal to the anti-dumping duty leviable at import is payable besides on those inputs, and pepper and pepper products and marble may not be sold domestically at all. For services, including software, the sale is capped instead of conditioned on the whole: up to fifty per cent of the free-on-board value of exports or fifty per cent of the foreign exchange earned. A gems and jewellery unit may sell up to ten per cent of the previous year's free-on-board value of exports, again on positive net foreign exchange. And two categories escape the net foreign exchange test entirely — sale of rejects up to five per cent of the free-on-board value of exports, and scrap, waste and remnants arising out of the production process, which are sold on the notified norms and applicable duties whatever the unit's net foreign exchange position. Reading one condition across all four is the mistake the paragraph is built to catch.

citation.ref: Paragraph 6.07(a) to (f) of Chapter 6

concepts.subsection: Paragraph 6.17 — Leaving the EOU scheme, and what the exit costs
concepts.statement: A unit may opt out of the scheme with the approval of the Development Commissioner, and the exit is priced: applicable excise and customs duties, and the integrated, central, State or union territory tax and compensation cess, all fall due, under the industrial policy in force. A unit that has not achieved its obligations is also liable to penalty at the time of exit — the duty is the price of the goods, the penalty is the price of the broken undertaking, and they are separate. The sequence matters as much as the sum. The unit intimates the Development Commissioner and the customs authorities in writing and assesses its own duty liability; customs confirm it on priority, on the condition that the unit has achieved positive net foreign exchange after taking the depreciation into account — which is also the only circumstance in which the depreciation benefit is available on capital goods disposed of into the domestic tariff area. The unit then obtains a No Dues Certificate, applies for final exit, and the Development Commissioner issues the final exit order within seven working days where nothing is pending under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act. In the gap between the No Dues Certificate and the final exit order the unit may claim no exemption for procuring capital goods or inputs, though an advance authorisation, a duty free import authorisation or duty drawback remain open to it on their own eligibility. Two conversions carry no duty on the way out: capital goods that a unit bought duty-paid as a domestic unit before converting into an EOU, and capital goods imported under EPCG whose export obligation was fully discharged before conversion.

citation.ref: Paragraph 6.17(a), (b), (d), (e) and (f) of Chapter 6, read with paragraph 6.14(b) on depreciation

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 4.24 to 4.28 — Duty Free Import Authorisation, and how it is not an advance authorisation
concepts.statement: A Duty Free Import Authorisation lets an exporter import the inputs that went into goods he has already exported, and every one of its terms separates it from the advance authorisation it sits beside. It is issued on a post-export basis, and only for products for which standard input output norms have been notified, so there is no room for a self-declared norm. It exempts basic customs duty and nothing else — where an advance authorisation reaches the whole family of duties, this one reaches one of them, and the integrated tax and compensation cess are paid. Its minimum value addition is twenty per cent, against fifteen for an advance authorisation. It is transferable, and that is the sharpest difference of all: an advance authorisation and the material imported under it carry the actual user condition and cannot be transferred even after the export obligation is discharged, while the Regional Authority issues a transferable duty free import authorisation with a validity of twelve months from the date of issue, which will not be revalidated. The exports themselves must be completed within twelve months of filing the online application and generating the file number, a separate authorisation is issued for each set of norms, and no authorisation issues at all for an input carrying a pre-import condition or one for which the norms prescribe actual user. Import of tyres under the scheme is not allowed.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 4.24 to 4.28 of Chapter 4, read against paragraphs 4.09 and 4.16 for the advance authorisation comparison

concepts.subsection: Chapter 7 of the FTP — Deemed exports under the policy, which is not the GST list
concepts.statement: One phrase, two lists, in the same paper. For the Foreign Trade Policy, a deemed export is a transaction in which the goods do not leave the country, payment is received in Indian rupees or in free foreign exchange, and — the condition that does most of the work — the goods are manufactured in India. For the goods and services tax, Chapter 7 says in its own words that deemed exports mean only the supplies notified under section 147, on the Council's recommendation, with their own benefits and their own conditions. So a supply can be a deemed export for one of them and not the other, and answering a policy question out of section 147 is the trap. The policy's own categories are seven. A manufacturer's supply of goods against an advance authorisation or a duty free import authorisation; his supply to an EOU, STP, EHTP or BTP; and his supply of capital goods against an EPCG authorisation. And by a main or sub-contractor: supplies to projects funded by notified multilateral or bilateral agencies under international competitive bidding; supplies to projects the customs notification lets in at zero basic customs duty, again under such bidding, with mega power projects on their own terms; supplies to the United Nations or an approved international organisation; and supplies to a nuclear power project of 440 MW or more certified by a Joint Secretary in the Department of Atomic Energy and tendered competitively. The benefits are three, and only three: an advance authorisation or duty free import authorisation, deemed export drawback, and refund of terminal excise duty on the goods still in Schedule 4 of the Central Excise Act where the supply is eligible and no exemption already applies.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 7.01, 7.02 and 7.03 of Chapter 7, read with section 147 of the CGST Act, 2017 for the contrast the policy itself draws

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 5.04(d), 5.09, 5.10 and 5.11 — Four ways to cut the export obligation, and why only one of them counts
concepts.statement: The specific export obligation is six times the duties, taxes and cess saved, and Chapter 5 offers four separate ways of cutting it. Where the capital goods are sourced from a domestic manufacturer the specific obligation is twenty-five per cent LESS. For an exporter of green technology products the specific obligation is seventy-five per cent OF the figure paragraph 5.01(b) gives. For a manufacturing unit in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir or Ladakh it is twenty-five per cent OF that figure, which is the largest cut of the four by a wide margin. And where the holder has fulfilled seventy-five per cent or more of the specific obligation together with the whole of the average obligation to date, in half or less than half the original period, the balance is condoned and the authorisation redeemed. Two things decide almost every question on this. First, the difference between twenty-five per cent less and twenty-five per cent of — one leaves three quarters standing and the other leaves a quarter. Second, paragraph 5.04(l): only ONE of these four benefits is admissible, so they are alternatives to choose between and never a stack to multiply together. None of the four touches the average export obligation, which each paragraph says in the same breath in which it grants the relief.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 5.04(d), 5.04(l), 5.09, 5.10 and 5.11 of Chapter 5, read with paragraph 5.01(b)

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 5.04(c) and 5.12 — The average export obligation, which is a second obligation and not part of the first
concepts.statement: An EPCG holder carries two obligations at once and they are counted differently. The specific obligation is six times the duty saved over six years. The average export obligation is the arithmetic mean of what he exported of the same and similar products in the three preceding licensing years, and it must be met EVERY financial year until the specific obligation is complete, not once across the period. The two meet at one point that decides most questions: exports over and above the average are the only ones considered for fulfilment of the specific obligation, so a year that merely matches the past contributes nothing at all. Thirteen kinds of export are relieved of maintaining an average altogether — handicrafts, handlooms, industries covered by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, agriculture, aquaculture including fisheries and pisciculture, animal husbandry and dairying, floriculture and horticulture, poultry, viticulture, sericulture, carpets, coir and jute. That relief is withdrawn for the import of fishing trawlers, boats, ships and similar items, so it turns on the item as well as on the sector. And goods other than tools imported by those sectors may not be transferred for five years from the date of import even where the export obligation has been fulfilled, which is a restriction that outlives the obligation it came with.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 5.04(c) and 5.12(a), (b) and (c) of Chapter 5

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 5.01(d), 5.03 and 5.08 — How long the authorisation lives, and how long the condition on the machine does
concepts.statement: Three periods run at once under an EPCG authorisation and confusing them is the usual mistake.
