And a conclusion that an act is or is not non-compliance is ultimately a matter for legal determination by a court, which is not a conclusion an auditor may express in his report.
keywords: cannot be expected to detect non-compliance with all laws

citation.ref: the responsibility of management with the oversight of those charged with governance, the limits on the auditor's responsibility, and the point that non-compliance is ultimately a matter for legal determination by a court, read with the two categories of law at para 6

items.scenario: The representation letter your client has signed includes the sentence "the company has complied with all applicable laws and regulations". At the closing meeting the audit committee asks you to add a line to your report stating that the company is fully compliant with all applicable laws, saying the representation and the company secretary's quarterly compliance certificate together support it.

items.stem: What does SA 260 (Revised) say about each?

options.text: Both are right as they stand — telling management is telling those charged with governance wherever the same people hold both roles, and the audit committee chair speaks for the board
options.misconception: drops the two conditions the standard attaches, so the relief becomes a general rule and the subgroup becomes the whole body
options.why: Two limits are missing. The auditor must still satisfy himself that communicating with those persons adequately informs all of those with whom he would otherwise communicate in their governance capacity. And where he communicates with a subgroup he determines whether he also needs to communicate with the governing body, which is a decision to be made, not an assumption.

options.text: Both are wrong — every communication required by SA 260 must reach the full board of directors in every case
options.misconception: fixes one recipient for every entity, when the standard has the auditor determine the appropriate persons within the governance structure
options.why: The standard does not name a recipient; it makes the auditor determine the appropriate person or persons within the entity's governance structure with whom to communicate. Forcing every matter through the full board would make the relief for a company whose directors are all managers meaningless, and it is written into the standard.

options.text: In the first, where all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity, matters already communicated with those persons as management need not be communicated again with the same persons in their governance role; in the second, where the auditor communicates with a subgroup, he determines whether he also needs to communicate with the governing body
options.why: SA 260 (Revised) gives express relief where all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity: matters communicated with persons who have management responsibilities and who also have governance responsibilities need not be communicated again with those same persons in their governance capacity. Where the auditor communicates with a subgroup, such as an audit committee, the standard makes him determine whether he also needs to communicate with the governing body — the subgroup is a channel, not automatically the end of the line.
keywords: all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity

options.text: The first is wrong and the second right, since a matter raised in a management meeting is never a communication with those charged with governance, whoever happens to attend
options.misconception: applies the general rule that communicating with management does not relieve the auditor, to the one case the standard carves out of it
options.why: The general rule is right and there is an express exception to it. Communication with management does not ordinarily relieve the auditor of communicating with those charged with governance, but where all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity the standard says the matters need not be communicated again with those same persons.
keywords: all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity

citation.ref: the communication with a subgroup and the determination whether the governing body must also be communicated with, and the relief where all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity, read with para 15 and para 16

items.scenario: You audit two companies. The first is a private company with three directors; all three are executive, all three run the business daily, and there is no other director. Your manager has scheduled a separate governance meeting to repeat to those same three men everything already discussed with them as management. The second is a listed company where the team communicates only with the chair of the audit committee and has never communicated with the board.

items.stem: What does SA 300 require at the beginning of the current audit engagement?

options.text: Nothing beyond updating the strategy — those activities belong to an initial audit engagement, and a recurring audit builds on the previous year's file
options.misconception: reads the preliminary engagement activities as acceptance activities, when the standard sets them at the beginning of the current engagement whether or not it is the first
options.why: There is a separate list for an initial audit engagement, and this is not it. The preliminary engagement activities are required at the beginning of the current audit engagement, and continuance is a question that only exists in a recurring audit — a firm cannot continue a relationship it has not yet had.

options.text: All three preliminary engagement activities, every year — the SA 220 procedures on continuance of the client relationship and the specific audit engagement, an evaluation of compliance with relevant ethical requirements including independence, and establishing an understanding of the terms of the engagement
options.why: SA 300 sets the preliminary engagement activities at the beginning of the current audit engagement, not at the beginning of the relationship. They are performing the procedures required by SA 220 regarding the continuance of the client relationship and the specific audit engagement, evaluating compliance with relevant ethical requirements, including independence, and establishing an understanding of the terms of the engagement. A valuation assignment taken on during the year is exactly what the second is for, and it is invisible to a strategy copied forward.

options.text: Only the terms need attention — SA 210 requires the auditor to assess whether circumstances require the terms of the engagement to be revised in a recurring audit
options.misconception: takes the SA 210 recurring-engagement requirement as the whole of the work SA 300 sets at the start of the year
options.why: SA 210 does require that assessment in a recurring audit, and it is one of the three preliminary engagement activities, not all of them. Leaving out continuance and the evaluation of compliance with relevant ethical requirements, including independence, leaves out the two that would have caught the valuation assignment.

options.text: Communicate with the predecessor auditor before starting, in compliance with relevant ethical requirements
options.misconception: applies an activity required prior to starting an initial audit engagement to a recurring one where there is no predecessor
options.why: Communicating with the predecessor auditor is an additional activity required prior to starting an initial audit engagement where there has been a change of auditors. In the seventh year of the same appointment there is no predecessor to communicate with, and the three activities that are required have all been skipped.

citation.ref: the preliminary engagement activities at the beginning of the current audit engagement, and the additional activities required prior to starting an initial audit engagement

items.scenario: A firm is starting the seventh year of an audit. The manager copies last year's overall audit strategy forward, changes the year, and begins fieldwork. Nothing is done about client continuance, nobody evaluates whether the firm's independence survived a valuation assignment the tax department took on during the year, and the engagement letter signed in year one is left on file untouched.

items.stem: What has gone wrong under SA 315 (Revised)?

options.text: Two things — inquiry alone does not establish that a control has been implemented, since the auditor evaluates the design of identified controls and determines whether they have been implemented by performing procedures in addition to inquiry of the entity's personnel; and neither design nor implementation is a conclusion about operating effectiveness, which is tested under SA 330 before any reliance reduces substantive work
options.why: SA 315 (Revised) is explicit that the auditor evaluates the design of the controls he identifies and determines whether they have been implemented, by performing procedures in addition to inquiry of the entity's personnel — inspecting a document, observing the control being applied, tracing a transaction. A description of how a control is meant to work is not evidence that it exists and is being used. And design and implementation say nothing about operating effectiveness throughout the period, which is a response under SA 330 and the only thing that could justify reducing substantive testing.

options.text: Nothing — inquiry is a risk assessment procedure, and the components of the entity's system of internal control are understood by inquiry of management
options.misconception: stops at inquiry, when the standard requires procedures in addition to it for evaluating design and determining implementation
options.why: Inquiry is a risk assessment procedure and it is not sufficient on its own. The standard asks for procedures in addition to inquiry of the entity's personnel, and it says separately that risk assessment procedures by themselves do not provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the audit opinion.

options.text: The senior should have tested the operating effectiveness of every control he identified while obtaining his understanding
options.misconception: raises the understanding requirement to a test of controls for every control, when the standard asks only for design and implementation at this stage
options.why: Obtaining an understanding requires evaluating design and determining implementation, not a test of operating effectiveness. Operating effectiveness is tested where the auditor intends to rely on the controls, or where substantive procedures alone cannot provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence at the assertion level — a decision made under SA 330, on the controls that matter.

options.text: The only error is cutting the substantive testing; the understanding itself, built from a questionnaire and one conversation, is adequate
options.misconception: accepts an understanding obtained by inquiry alone and objects only to the response built on it
options.why: The response is wrong because the understanding was. A questionnaire completed from a single conversation is inquiry, and the requirement is to evaluate design and determine implementation by procedures in addition to inquiry. Fixing only the substantive testing leaves a file that still records controls nobody has seen operate once.

citation.ref: the requirement to evaluate the design of identified controls and determine whether they have been implemented by performing procedures in addition to inquiry of the entity's personnel, read with the significant risk definition at para 12(l)

items.scenario: A senior documents the entity's controls over purchases by working through a standard questionnaire in one conversation with the accounts manager, who describes how the three-way match, the approval limits and the vendor master change process are meant to work. The senior ticks every box, writes "controls appear effective", and cuts the planned substantive testing of purchases by half.

items.stem: What does SA 320 require?

options.text: Revise materiality but leave performance materiality where it is, since performance materiality is a fixed percentage of materiality set by firm policy
options.misconception: treats performance materiality as an arithmetic by-product rather than a judgement the standard requires to be revisited on a revision
options.why: A firm may start from a percentage, but performance materiality is a judgement about the probability that uncorrected and undetected misstatements aggregate above materiality, and SA 320 requires the auditor to determine whether it is necessary to revise it when materiality is revised downwards. Carrying it forward unchanged is a decision made by a spreadsheet.

options.text: Keep the planning figure and reassess materiality at the end, before evaluating the effect of uncorrected misstatements, as SA 450 requires
options.misconception: uses SA 450's end-of-audit reassessment to displace SA 320's duty to revise the moment the information arrives
options.why: SA 450 does require the auditor to reassess materiality prior to evaluating the effect of uncorrected misstatements, and that is a confirmation at the end. It comes too late to change any work. SA 320's revision is triggered by becoming aware of information during the audit, and leaving the planning figure in place for a quarter means every procedure in that quarter was scoped against a number already known to be wrong.

options.text: Revise materiality now, and — the revised figure being lower — determine whether it is necessary to revise performance materiality and whether the nature, timing and extent of the further audit procedures remain appropriate
options.why: SA 320 has the auditor revise materiality for the financial statements as a whole in the event of becoming aware of information during the audit that would have caused him to have determined a different amount initially, and a collapse in the benchmark the figure was built on is that information. Where he concludes a lower materiality is appropriate, he then determines whether it is necessary to revise performance materiality and whether the nature, timing and extent of the further audit procedures remain appropriate. Work already done against the old figure is a consequence to be dealt with, not a reason to leave the figure alone.
keywords: nature, timing and extent of the further audit procedures

options.text: Raise materiality instead — a company in loss has a smaller base, and a smaller figure would make the audit disproportionate to the fee
options.misconception: lets the cost of the audit set the materiality figure, which is a judgement about the decisions of users of the financial statements
options.why: Materiality is a judgement about the misstatements that could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of the financial statements. Nothing in it responds to the fee. A benchmark that has become unrepresentative is a reason to change the benchmark, not a reason to move the figure in whichever direction is convenient.
keywords: influence the economic decisions of users

citation.ref: para 12 and para 13, read with para 9 and para 11

items.scenario: Materiality for the financial statements as a whole was determined during planning on budgeted profit before tax. By the third quarter the company has lost its largest customer and sold a division at a loss; profit before tax will be a small fraction of budget. The manager decides to keep the planning figure, saying that changing it now would invalidate the sample sizes already used, and that materiality will be looked at again at the end when the uncorrected misstatements are evaluated.

items.stem: What does SA 501 require, and what does it not?

options.text: Confine the work to agreeing the segment totals to the statement of profit and loss, the segment note being a disclosure rather than a primary statement
options.misconception: reduces the requirement to a footing check, when the standard asks about the methods used and their application
options.why: Totals that agree tell you the allocation added up, not that it was made on a basis the applicable financial reporting framework permits. A change in the allocation of head office costs moves profit between segments without moving the total by a rupee, which is why SA 501 asks about the methods used by management and about testing their application.

options.text: Treat the segment note as other information under SA 720, since segment results are presented outside the primary financial statements
options.misconception: moves a disclosure that forms part of the financial statements into the other information regime, where the auditor expresses no opinion
options.why: Other information is information other than the financial statements and the auditor's report thereon, included in the entity's annual report. A note forming part of the financial statements is covered by the opinion, and SA 501 gives it a requirement of its own.

options.text: Perform enough work to express an opinion on each segment separately, since the segments are presented separately in the note
options.misconception: turns a disclosure within the financial statements into a separate opinion the standard expressly does not require
options.why: SA 501 says in terms that the auditor is not required to perform the audit procedures that would be necessary to express an opinion on the segment information presented on a standalone basis. The opinion is on the financial statements as a whole, and the segment note is a disclosure within them.

options.text: Understand the methods management used — including the elimination of inter-segment amounts and the allocation of assets and costs among segments — evaluate whether those methods are likely to result in disclosure in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework, test their application where appropriate, and perform analytical procedures; but the auditor is not required to perform the procedures necessary to express an opinion on the segment information presented on a standalone basis
options.why: SA 501 has the auditor obtain evidence about the presentation and disclosure of segment information by obtaining an understanding of the methods used by management in determining it, evaluating whether those methods are likely to result in disclosure in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework, testing the application of those methods where appropriate, and performing analytical procedures or other procedures appropriate in the circumstances. Inter-segment eliminations and the allocation of assets and costs among segments are exactly the methods it names. The standard also says what is not required: the procedures necessary to express an opinion on the segment information presented on a standalone basis.
keywords: allocation of assets and costs among segments

citation.ref: para 13, read with the litigation and claims requirements at para 9 to para 11

items.scenario: A manufacturer discloses three reportable segments. Inter-segment sales are eliminated by a spreadsheet the group accountant maintains and nobody has re-performed; the basis on which head office costs are allocated to segments was changed this year with no explanation in the file; and the segment note foots to the totals in the statement of profit and loss. The client asks you to state in your report that each segment's result is fairly stated.

items.stem: What does SA 530 say about that sample?

options.text: It is acceptable — haphazard selection avoids conscious bias, and taking whichever file is closest to hand is haphazard selection
options.misconception: calls a convenience selection haphazard, when haphazard selection still leaves every sampling unit able to be selected
options.why: Haphazard selection means selecting without following a structured technique while still avoiding conscious bias or predictability, and it is drawn from the whole population. Taking the file that saves a day of pulling records is a choice made about the population, not within it, and it removes most of the population from reach.

options.text: It is acceptable provided twenty is a sample size sufficient to reduce sampling risk to an acceptably low level for this control
options.misconception: lets sample size cure a selection method that left most of the population unable to be selected
options.why: Sample size and selection are separate requirements and both must hold. A sample size sufficient to reduce sampling risk to an acceptably low level is computed for a population the sample is actually drawn from; it says nothing about eleven months that were never in the frame.

options.text: It fails on selection and on population — block selection of contiguous items is ordinarily not an appropriate method because items in a sequence tend to share characteristics, the requirement is that each sampling unit in the population has a chance of selection, and a population of one month is not complete for a control that operated all year
options.why: SA 530 requires the auditor to select items in such a way that each sampling unit in the population has a chance of selection. Twenty consecutive vouchers from one month gives no chance at all to eleven months of the population, and block selection is ordinarily not an appropriate selection method precisely because most populations are structured so that items in a sequence share characteristics with each other. Design comes first as well: the population has to be appropriate for the purpose of the procedure and it has to be complete, and for a control that operated throughout the year one month is neither.
keywords: each sampling unit in the population has a chance of selection

options.text: It is acceptable because any deviation found in a single month's block would be an anomaly and could be left out when projecting to the population
options.misconception: reaches for the anomaly label, which is available only in extremely rare circumstances and only on a high degree of certainty obtained by additional procedures
options.why: An anomaly is a deviation demonstrably not representative of the population, and the label is available only in extremely rare circumstances where the auditor has obtained a high degree of certainty by performing additional audit procedures. A deviation found in the month it was most likely to occur is the opposite of unrepresentative.

citation.ref: para 6, para 7 and para 8, read with para 13 and para 14

items.scenario: To test whether purchase orders were authorised in accordance with the delegation of authority, which operated for the whole year, a senior takes twenty consecutively numbered vouchers from the March file. He explains that pulling files from twelve different months would take a day, that March is the busiest month so it is the toughest test, and that twenty is the sample size the firm's manual gives for this control.

items.stem: What does SA 550 require of the auditor?

options.text: Accept the disclosure — whether terms were at arm's length is a management judgement, and the auditor's responsibility is limited to checking that the related party transaction has been disclosed
options.misconception: confuses management's responsibility for making the assertion with the auditor's responsibility to obtain evidence about it
options.why: Management makes the assertion; the auditor audits it. SA 550 creates a specific requirement to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about an assertion that a transaction was on terms equivalent to an arm's length transaction, which would be pointless if disclosure were the whole of the auditor's interest.

options.text: Obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the assertion — comparing the terms with an identical or similar transaction with unrelated parties or with known market terms, evaluating the appropriateness of management's process for supporting the assertion, and verifying the source of the supporting data and testing it for accuracy, completeness and relevance
options.why: Where management asserts in the financial statements that a related party transaction was conducted on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction, SA 550 requires the auditor to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the assertion. The procedures available are comparing the terms with an identical or similar transaction with one or more unrelated parties or with known market terms, evaluating the appropriateness of management's process for supporting the assertion, and verifying the source of the internal or external data supporting it and testing that data for accuracy, completeness and relevance. A minute recording the directors' opinion and a valuation produced by the counterparty answer none of the three.
keywords: management's process for supporting the assertion

options.text: Treat the sale as a significant related party transaction outside the entity's normal course of business, inspect the underlying contracts and evaluate the business rationale — and stop there
options.misconception: stops at the significant risk a different paragraph of SA 550 creates, leaving the arm's length assertion itself untested
options.why: That is a real requirement and it is a different one. A significant related party transaction outside the entity's normal course of business gives rise to a significant risk and calls for inspection of the contracts and evaluation of the business rationale. The assertion that the terms were equivalent to an arm's length transaction is a separate statement in the financial statements and carries its own evidence requirement.
keywords: outside the entity's normal course of business

options.text: Require the assertion to be deleted, since terms equivalent to an arm's length transaction can never be supported where the asset has no market equivalent
options.misconception: turns the difficulty of supporting the assertion into a rule that it may never be made
options.why: The absence of a directly comparable transaction makes the evidence harder to find, not impossible. Known market terms for broadly similar transactions, and an evaluation of the appropriateness of management's process for supporting the assertion, remain open. What the auditor may not do is accept the assertion because nothing better was offered.
keywords: management's process for supporting the assertion

citation.ref: para 24, read with para 23

items.scenario: A company sells a purpose-built plant to its holding company and the notes state that the transaction was conducted on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction. The only support on file is a board minute recording the directors' view that the price was fair, and a valuation prepared by the holding company's own finance team. There is no comparable sale of a similar plant to any unrelated party.

items.stem: What does SA 610 (Revised) require you to do?

options.text: Use both bodies of work — the function is competent and applies a systematic and disciplined approach, and objectivity is a matter for internal audit's own charter rather than for the external auditor
options.misconception: treats competence and a systematic and disciplined approach as sufficient, when objectivity is a separate and equally binding condition
options.why: The three conditions are cumulative. The external auditor shall not use the work of the function where its organisational status and relevant policies and procedures do not adequately support the objectivity of internal auditors, even where the function is competent and applies a systematic and disciplined approach. Objectivity is the external auditor's own evaluation, not something a charter settles for him.

options.text: Use neither — SA 610 (Revised) does not permit the external auditor to use the work of an internal audit function at all, and permits only direct assistance under his direction
options.misconception: inverts the standard, which permits both the use of the function's work and, separately and on stricter conditions, direct assistance
options.why: SA 610 (Revised) deals with both. It permits the external auditor to use the work of the internal audit function where the three conditions are met, and it separately permits internal auditors to provide direct assistance under the external auditor's direction, supervision and review, on its own stricter conditions including written agreements. Neither is prohibited outright.

options.text: Use both, provided you first obtain written agreement from the entity that the internal auditors will not be interfered with and from the internal auditors that they will keep matters confidential
options.misconception: imports the written agreements that condition direct assistance into the different question whether the function's work may be used
options.why: Those written agreements belong to direct assistance, where an internal auditor performs audit procedures for the external auditor. Using the work the function has already done for its own purposes is a different route with its own gate, and a written agreement cannot supply an objectivity the organisational status does not support.

options.text: Evaluate the organisational status and relevant policies and procedures, the level of competence, and whether a systematic and disciplined approach is applied — reporting to the CFO does not adequately support the objectivity of internal auditors over work on the CFO's own approvals, so that work cannot be used, and for anything that can be used you determine the areas and extent by reference to the judgement involved and the assessed risk of material misstatement, still making all significant judgements yourself
options.why: The determination whether the work of the internal audit function can be used is made by evaluating three things, and the organisational status and relevant policies and procedures that support the objectivity of internal auditors is the one that fails here for the capital expenditure work — a function reporting to the CFO cannot be objective about the CFO's own approvals, whatever its competence. Where work can be used, the external auditor determines the areas and the extent by reference to the amount of judgement involved and the assessed risk of material misstatement, and plans so that all significant judgements in the audit are made by him.

citation.ref: the determination whether the work of the internal audit function can be used by evaluating organisational status and relevant policies and procedures supporting objectivity, the level of competence and whether a systematic and disciplined approach is applied, read with the direct assistance conditions at para 28, para 30 and para 33

items.scenario: The internal audit head reports to the chief financial officer and his appraisal and bonus are set by the CFO. The function is well staffed with qualified people, its methodology is documented and its files are reviewed internally. Your team plans to use two bodies of its work — the inventory counts at four depots, and its testing of the approvals the CFO himself gives for capital expenditure.

items.stem: What does SA 620 require to have been agreed before the work began?

options.text: An agreement was needed, but not on confidentiality — an auditor's expert is bound by the auditor's own professional duty of confidentiality by virtue of being engaged by him
options.misconception: assumes a duty the standard names as a matter to be agreed precisely because it does not arise on its own
options.why: An auditor's external expert is not a member of the firm and is not bound by the auditor's professional duty of confidentiality merely by being engaged. That is why the need for the auditor's expert to observe confidentiality requirements is one of the four matters SA 620 names for agreement, and why writing is appropriate where he has access to sensitive or confidential entity information.

options.text: Four matters, in writing where appropriate — the nature, scope and objectives of the expert's work; the respective roles and responsibilities of the auditor and the expert; the nature, timing and extent of communication including the form of any report to be provided by the expert; and the need for the expert to observe confidentiality requirements
options.why: SA 620 has the auditor agree these four matters with the auditor's expert, in writing when appropriate, and writing is appropriate here because the expert is an external expert who was given access to sensitive and confidential entity information. The nature, scope and objectives would have set what the valuation was for and on what basis; the roles and responsibilities would have said who obtains what; the form of any report would have stopped a one-page certificate with no method arriving; and the need to observe confidentiality requirements matters most where the expert also acts for a competitor.

options.text: Only the fee and the delivery date — agreeing the technical content of the work would compromise the expert's independence and make his conclusion the auditor's
options.misconception: reads agreeing the scope of the work as directing the expert's judgement
options.why: Agreeing the nature, scope and objectives of the work fixes the question the expert is asked, not the answer he gives. Without it the auditor cannot later evaluate the adequacy of the expert's work for his purposes, because there is nothing recorded to evaluate it against.

options.text: Nothing needed to be agreed in advance — SA 620 works by evaluating the relevance and reasonableness of the expert's findings after the work is done
options.misconception: keeps the evaluation requirement and drops the agreement that comes before it
options.why: The evaluation is real and it is not the whole standard. SA 620 requires the auditor to agree the four matters with the expert before the work, to satisfy himself about the expert's competence, capabilities and objectivity, and to obtain a sufficient understanding of the expert's field — and only then to evaluate the relevance and reasonableness of the findings.

citation.ref: para 11, read with para 12 and para 13

items.scenario: You engage an external valuer to value an unquoted investment. The engagement is arranged over the telephone; the valuer is told only to "value the investment as at 31 March". Your team gives him the board papers and the customer contracts so he can see the investee's order book. What comes back is a one-page certificate carrying a figure and no method. In conversation the valuer mentions that the investee's largest competitor is also a client of his.

items.stem: What is wrong under SA 700 (Revised)?

options.text: Only the partner's name is missing — 5 May is the right date, being the date the auditor's work was complete
options.misconception: dates the report from the end of the auditor's work rather than from the evidence, which includes the financial statements having been prepared and responsibility taken for them
options.why: The date is fixed by the evidence, not by the fieldwork calendar. Among the evidence the standard names is that those with the recognised authority have asserted that they have taken responsibility for the financial statements, and on 5 May they had not. A report dated before the accounts exist in approved form reports on something nobody had yet adopted.

options.text: Three things — the report cannot be dated before those with the recognised authority asserted that they had taken responsibility for the financial statements, which was 11 May; the place of signature must be stated; and for a listed entity the name of the engagement partner is included unless disclosure is reasonably expected to lead to a significant personal security threat
options.why: SA 700 (Revised) dates the report no earlier than the date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, including evidence that all the statements comprising the financial statements have been prepared and that those with the recognised authority have asserted that they have taken responsibility for them — so 5 May is impossible where the board approved on 11 May. The report also names the place of signature. And for audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of listed entities the name of the engagement partner is included, unless in rare circumstances that disclosure is reasonably expected to lead to a significant personal security threat.

options.text: Only the date — a firm is appointed and a firm signs, so no individual's name is required, and naming the place of signature is a matter of local practice
options.misconception: drops two express requirements of the standard on the ground that the firm rather than the individual holds the appointment
options.why: Who is appointed and what the report must contain are different questions. SA 700 (Revised) requires the report to name the place of signature, and requires the name of the engagement partner for a listed entity's complete set of general purpose financial statements. Neither requirement asks who the client contracted with.

options.text: Nothing — dual dating permits a report to carry one date for the audit work and a later date for the signature
options.misconception: reaches for dual dating, which deals with an amendment made for a subsequent event after the original report date, not with a report dated before the accounts were approved
options.why: Dual dating arises where the auditor amends a report already issued for a subsequent event and dates the amendment for that matter alone, leaving the original date for everything else. It has nothing to say about a first report dated before those with the recognised authority took responsibility for the financial statements.

citation.ref: the requirements on the name of the engagement partner for a listed entity, the place of signature, and the dating of the report no earlier than the date sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained including that those with the recognised authority have taken responsibility for the financial statements

items.scenario: A listed company's audit report is signed by the engagement partner at Pune on 12 May and is dated 5 May, the day the team finished its fieldwork. The board approved the financial statements on 11 May. The report carries the firm's name and its registration number, no individual's name, and no mention of where it was signed. The partner's view is that the firm is the appointed auditor, so the firm's name is what belongs on the report.

items.stem: What does SA 701 require of the description?

options.text: The description should also state the auditor's separate conclusion on revenue, so that the reader knows how the matter turned out
options.misconception: turns a key audit matter into a separate opinion, which the standard says the auditor does not provide
options.why: The introduction to the Key Audit Matters section states that the matters were addressed in the context of the audit of the financial statements as a whole and in forming the auditor's opinion thereon, and that the auditor does not provide a separate opinion on these matters. A conclusion on revenue alone would be exactly the separate opinion the standard rules out.

options.text: Nothing more — a key audit matter is selected from the matters communicated with those charged with governance, and naming the matter under a subheading is the requirement
options.misconception: stops at selecting and naming the matter, when the standard prescribes what the description must contain
options.why: Selection is the first half. SA 701 goes on to say what the description must address — why the matter was one of most significance and how it was addressed in the audit — because a reader who is told only the name of an account has learned nothing about the audit.
keywords: how it was addressed in the audit

options.text: The matter should be moved to an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, which is the proper place for a matter of significance in the financial statements
options.misconception: swaps two different devices, when an Emphasis of Matter is barred for a matter determined to be a key audit matter
options.why: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph draws attention to a matter presented or disclosed in the financial statements that is fundamental to users' understanding, and it is available only where the matter has not been determined to be a key audit matter. The two cannot both carry the same matter, and a key audit matter is described in its own section.

options.text: A reference to the related disclosure in the financial statements, a statement of why the matter was considered to be one of most significance in the audit and therefore determined to be a key audit matter, and a description of how the matter was addressed in the audit — and materiality on its own is not why a matter required significant auditor attention
options.why: SA 701 prescribes the content. Each key audit matter is described under an appropriate subheading, the description includes a reference to the related disclosure, if any, in the financial statements, and it addresses why the matter was considered to be one of most significance in the audit and therefore determined to be a key audit matter, and how the matter was addressed in the audit. The determination itself runs through matters that required significant auditor attention — higher assessed risks, significant judgements, significant events or transactions — and a balance being large is not one of them on its own.
keywords: how the matter was addressed in the audit

citation.ref: para 13 on the description of each key audit matter, read with the three-stage determination and with para 14

items.scenario: A listed company's draft report carries one key audit matter, reproduced here in full under the subheading "Revenue recognition": "Revenue is a key audit matter because revenue is material to the financial statements. We performed audit procedures over revenue." There is no reference to any note, and nothing about what was done.

items.stem: What must change in that report?

options.text: Only the heading — the body of a disclaimer is otherwise the standard unmodified report wording
options.misconception: changes the label and leaves the report saying the opposite of what the label means
options.why: A report headed Disclaimer of Opinion whose body expresses an opinion contradicts itself on its own first page. The standard amends the Opinion section, the Basis heading, the description of the auditor's responsibilities and the statement about compliance with the Standards on Auditing, all together.

options.text: All four — the heading becomes "Disclaimer of Opinion"; the section states that the auditor does not express an opinion and that he has not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for an audit opinion; the Key Audit Matters section is not included unless law or regulation requires it; and the sentence about conducting the audit in accordance with the Standards on Auditing is replaced by a statement that the auditor was engaged to audit the financial statements
options.why: SA 705 (Revised) changes the report in more than one place. The Opinion section is headed Disclaimer of Opinion; it says the auditor does not express an opinion and that, because of the significance of the matter described, he has not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for an audit opinion; the Basis heading is amended to match. Where an opinion is disclaimed the report does not include a Key Audit Matters section unless the auditor is required by law or regulation to communicate key audit matters, and the statement about the audit having been conducted in accordance with the Standards on Auditing is replaced by a statement that the auditor was engaged to audit the financial statements.

options.text: The "except for the possible effects" wording is correct and should stay, since the modification arises from an inability to obtain evidence rather than from a misstatement
options.misconception: applies the qualified-opinion wording for a scope limitation to a disclaimer, where the possible effects are material and pervasive
options.why: "Except for the possible effects" is the wording of a qualified opinion arising from an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and a qualification is available only where the possible effects could be material but not pervasive. Here they are material and pervasive, so no opinion is expressed at all and the phrase has nothing to except from.

options.text: The Key Audit Matters section must stay, the entity being listed and SA 701 applying to it
options.misconception: keeps a section SA 705 removes when an opinion is disclaimed, unless law or regulation requires it
options.why: SA 701 applies to listed entities and SA 705 (Revised) overrides it in this one case: where the auditor disclaims an opinion, the report does not include a Key Audit Matters section unless he is required by law or regulation to communicate key audit matters. Describing how matters were addressed in an audit that produced no opinion would tell the reader the opposite of what the disclaimer says.

citation.ref: para 16, para 20 and para 21, read with para 11 to para 14 and with the requirements that apply where the auditor disclaims an opinion

items.scenario: You cannot obtain audit evidence over a subsidiary whose figures are material and pervasive to the consolidated financial statements. Withdrawal is not possible under the applicable law, so you disclaim an opinion. The draft report keeps the heading "Opinion", says "except for the possible effects of the matter described in the Basis for Opinion section", keeps a Key Audit Matters section describing goodwill, and keeps the standard sentence that the audit was conducted in accordance with the Standards on Auditing.

items.stem: What does SRE 2400 (Revised) require?

options.text: Issue an unmodified conclusion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph drawing the reader's attention to the margin movement
options.misconception: uses an emphasis paragraph to carry a matter that, if the financial statements are materially misstated, requires the conclusion itself to be modified
options.why: An emphasis paragraph draws attention to something properly presented in the financial statements. A closing inventory the practitioner suspects is overstated is not properly presented, and where the financial statements are materially misstated the conclusion is qualified or adverse, not emphasised.

options.text: Design and perform additional procedures sufficient to conclude on the matter or to determine that a modified conclusion is needed — and if the financial statements are materially misstated, qualify the conclusion, or express an adverse conclusion where the effects are material and pervasive
options.why: Inquiry and analytical procedures are where a review starts, not a ceiling on it. Where a matter comes to the practitioner's attention causing him to believe the financial statements may be materially misstated, SRE 2400 (Revised) requires him to design and perform additional procedures sufficient to enable him to conclude on the matter or to determine that a modified conclusion is needed. Where they are materially misstated the conclusion is qualified, and adverse where the effects are material and pervasive.

options.text: Convert the engagement into an audit, since evidence beyond inquiry and analytical procedures is now being sought
options.misconception: treats additional procedures within a review as a change in the level of assurance, which would be a change in the terms of the engagement
options.why: Performing additional procedures inside a review does not turn it into an audit. The level of assurance stays limited assurance and the conclusion stays in the negative form; a change to an audit would be a change in the terms of the engagement, needing its own justification and a new agreement.

options.text: Issue the unmodified conclusion — a review gives limited assurance expressed in the negative form, so nothing coming to attention through inquiry and analytical procedures is the whole of the test
options.misconception: reads the negative form of the conclusion as permission to stop, when something has in fact come to the practitioner's attention
options.why: The negative form says nothing has come to the practitioner's attention that causes him to believe the financial statements are not properly prepared. Something has come to his attention here — a margin movement whose explanation the data contradicts — so the very condition the form describes has failed, and limited assurance is not the same as no work.

citation.ref: the requirement to design and perform additional procedures where a matter comes to the practitioner's attention causing him to believe the financial statements may be materially misstated, and the modified conclusions that follow

items.scenario: You are reviewing a company's half-yearly financial statements under SRE 2400 (Revised). Your analytical procedures show the gross margin up sharply on a flat sales line, and management's explanation — a change in product mix — is contradicted by the mix data it supplies. You suspect closing inventory is overstated. The manager says a review consists of inquiry and analytical procedures, so the file should record the inquiry, the explanation and an unmodified conclusion.

items.stem: What does SAE 3420 permit you to opine on, and what happens to the adjustments?

options.text: The synergy savings are acceptable because the board has a reasonable basis for expecting them; only the audit fee adjustment must come out
options.misconception: replaces "factually supportable" with "reasonably expected", which is the test for a forecast rather than for a pro forma adjustment
options.why: A best-estimate assumption about events management expects is the language of a forecast. A pro forma adjustment has to be factually supportable — capable of being supported by evidence such as an executed agreement, an invoice or a valuation — and an expectation, however reasonable, is not a fact about the period being illustrated.

options.text: The opinion is only on whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, on the basis of the applicable criteria — not on what the group would have earned — and the synergy savings and the hoped-for fee reduction are not pro forma adjustments, since they are neither directly attributable to the transaction nor factually supportable
options.why: SAE 3420 gives a reasonable assurance engagement on a narrow subject matter: whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, by the responsible party on the basis of the applicable criteria. The practitioner expresses no opinion on whether the actual outcome of the transaction will be as illustrated. Pro forma adjustments must be directly attributable to the event or transaction, factually supportable, and consistent with the entity's applicable financial reporting framework and its accounting policies — savings the board hopes to realise and a fee it hopes to negotiate meet none of that.

options.text: The engagement cannot be accepted at all, since pro forma information concerns future events and no assurance may be expressed on information about the future
options.misconception: confuses pro forma information, which applies an illustration to a past period, with prospective financial information about the future
options.why: Pro forma financial information illustrates the effect of an event or transaction on a period that has already happened, as if it had occurred at an earlier date. Prospective financial information is about the future and is dealt with under a different standard, where the practitioner expresses negative assurance on the assumptions. The two are not the same engagement.

options.text: The opinion asked for may be given, since SAE 3420 is a reasonable assurance engagement and reasonable assurance supports a positive opinion on the figures themselves
options.misconception: takes the high level of assurance to widen the subject matter, when the level is high and the subject matter narrow
options.why: Level of assurance and subject matter are different things. The assurance is reasonable assurance, and the subject matter is whether the information has been compiled on the basis of the applicable criteria. Nobody can opine on what a group would have earned in a year that did not happen.

citation.ref: the opinion on whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, on the basis of the applicable criteria, and the requirement that pro forma adjustments be directly attributable to the event or transaction, factually supportable, and consistent with the applicable financial reporting framework and the entity's accounting policies

items.scenario: A prospectus presents pro forma results for the year as though an acquisition completed in December had been completed on the first day of the year. The adjustments include the acquired company's audited results for the earlier months, an amount described as "synergy savings the board expects to realise", and a reduction in the audit fee the directors believe they can negotiate from the group auditor. The merchant banker asks you to give an opinion that the pro forma results fairly present what the group would have earned.

items.stem: What is wrong with that conclusion?

options.text: The team should have obtained a written representation from management that all journal entries during the year were properly authorised
options.misconception: substitutes a representation for the investigation of exceptions the analytic exists to produce
options.why: A written representation is not sufficient appropriate audit evidence on its own about any of the matters it deals with, and management's word about journal entries is the weakest possible answer to an analytic built to test management's journal entries. The exceptions still have to be investigated.

options.text: Nothing — testing one hundred per cent of a population is the strongest form of testing there is and leaves no risk to conclude on
options.misconception: reads the removal of sampling risk as the removal of audit risk, when non-sampling risk is untouched by coverage
options.why: Coverage answers one risk. Non-sampling risk — a procedure that tests the wrong attribute, a data extraction that missed a ledger, evidence misinterpreted — is by definition the risk of an erroneous conclusion for a reason unrelated to sampling, and running the analytic over every row does nothing to it.

options.text: The only error is in the aggregation — the flagged entries should have been projected to the population before being compared with performance materiality
options.misconception: projects from a population that was tested in full, when projection is what sampling requires and full coverage removes
options.why: Projection is how a sample speaks about the population it came from. Where the whole population was tested there is nothing to project to, and the error lies earlier: treating flagged entries as misstatements at all, and comparing them with performance materiality before any of them was investigated.

options.text: The flagged entries are items carrying the characteristic the analytic was asked to find, not misstatements — each has to be investigated with professional skepticism — and full coverage removes sampling risk only, saying nothing about whether the extraction was accurate and complete or whether the rule tested the right attribute
options.why: An analytic returns a population of exceptions, and an exception is a question, not a finding. Investigating them is where professional skepticism is exercised, and concluding a control effective without looking at four thousand of them is a conclusion drawn from a list nobody read. Testing everything removes sampling risk — the risk that a conclusion based on a sample differs from the conclusion on the whole population — and leaves untouched whether the data extracted from the entity's systems was accurate and complete, and whether the rule was written to the right threshold.

citation.ref: Ch. Digital Auditing and Assurance, read with SA 500 on information produced by the entity

items.scenario: A team extracts every journal entry for the year from the client's system and runs an analytic that flags entries posted outside business hours by users who do not normally post journals. Some four thousand entries are flagged. The working paper reads: "Population tested one hundred per cent. No sampling risk. Flagged entries individually and in aggregate below performance materiality. Journal entry control concluded effective."

items.stem: What is the position under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.text: Both appointments are open, since neither is prohibited where the audit committee approves the arrangement and the fees are disclosed
options.misconception: treats an audit committee approval as capable of curing a prohibition section 144 imposes outright
options.why: Section 144 prohibits an auditor appointed under the Act from rendering internal audit services to the company, directly or indirectly. It is a bar, not a matter for approval, and an audit committee cannot consent to a service the Act forbids.

options.text: The general manager may be appointed — the internal auditor may be a chartered accountant or a cost accountant, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board, and may or may not be an employee of the company — but the statutory auditors may not be, and no approval cures that
options.why: Section 138 says the internal auditor shall either be a chartered accountant or a cost accountant, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board, and the Explanation adds that the internal auditor may or may not be an employee of the company. A cost accountant on the payroll therefore qualifies on both counts. The statutory auditor cannot hold the office, because section 144 lists internal audit among the services an auditor appointed under the Act shall not render, directly or indirectly, to the company.
keywords: such other professional as may be decided by the Board
may or may not be an employee

options.text: Neither may be appointed — the internal auditor must be selected from a panel and the Board has no discretion over who the professional is
options.misconception: removes the discretion the section gives the Board to decide such other professional as may conduct the internal audit
options.why: There is no panel in section 138. The section names a chartered accountant or a cost accountant and then adds such other professional as may be decided by the Board — a discretion, not a shortlist — to conduct the internal audit of the functions and activities of the company.
keywords: such other professional as may be decided by the Board

options.text: The director is right on both counts — the internal auditor must be a chartered accountant, and must be independent of the company, so an employee cannot hold the office
options.misconception: reads the qualification requirement more narrowly than the section does, and imports the statutory auditor's independence rules into an office the Act expressly allows an employee to hold
options.why: The section is wider than the objection. A cost accountant may be appointed, and so may such other professional as may be decided by the Board. And the Explanation settles the second point in one line: the internal auditor may or may not be an employee of the company.
keywords: such other professional as may be decided by the Board
may or may not be an employee

citation.ref: Section 138(1) with its Explanation, read with section 144

items.scenario: A company falls within the class required to appoint an internal auditor. The board proposes appointing its own general manager (finance), a cost accountant on the company's payroll. One director objects that an internal auditor must be an outside firm and must be a chartered accountant, and proposes appointing the company's statutory auditors instead, since they already know the business; the audit committee, he says, can approve the arrangement.

items.stem: What does SA 720 require you to do?

options.text: Read the investor presentation and treat it as the other information, since it is the only document available and carries the same figures
options.misconception: makes a document other information because it was published, when the test is whether it forms part of the annual report
options.why: Other information is information included in an entity's annual report, and a document is caught because it forms part of that report, not because it was published near it or repeats the same numbers. An investor presentation issued in April is not the annual report, and reading it discharges nothing.

options.text: Nothing further — the auditor's responsibility under SA 720 is to read the other information, and where none is available before the report date there is nothing to read
options.misconception: reads the standard as beginning and ending with the reading, when it sets out how the auditor obtains the other information in the first place
options.why: The reading requirement is preceded by a requirement to obtain. The auditor determines which documents comprise the annual report and makes arrangements to obtain the final version, and the standard provides expressly for information that arrives after the date of the auditor's report — it does not treat the absence of a document as the end of the matter.
keywords: which documents comprise the annual report
after the date of the auditor's report

options.text: Determine through discussion with management which documents comprise the annual report and the planned manner and timing of their issuance, arrange to obtain the final version prior to the date of the auditor's report if possible, and — since it will not be available by then — request a written representation that the final version will be provided when available and prior to its issuance by the entity
options.why: SA 720 makes the auditor determine, through discussion with management, which documents comprise the annual report and the entity's planned manner and timing of their issuance, and make appropriate arrangements to obtain the final version in a timely manner and if possible prior to the date of the auditor's report. Where some or all of them will not be available until after that date, he requests management to provide a written representation that the final version will be provided to him when available and prior to its issuance by the entity.
keywords: which documents comprise the annual report
prior to the date of the auditor's report
prior to its issuance by the entity

options.text: Delay the auditor's report until the annual report is typeset in July, since the auditor cannot report until he has read the other information
options.misconception: makes the other information a precondition to the audit opinion, when the auditor expresses no opinion on it and the standard provides for it arriving later
options.why: The auditor expresses no opinion or conclusion on the other information, so it cannot hold up the opinion on the financial statements. SA 720 deals with the timing difference by having the auditor obtain a written representation that the final version will be provided when available and prior to its issuance by the entity.

citation.ref: para 13, read with the reading requirement at para 14

items.scenario: Two weeks before you expect to sign, you ask the finance head for the directors' report and the management discussion and analysis. He says the annual report is typeset in July, well after the audit report will be signed, and there is nothing to give you now. He offers instead the investor presentation the company issued in April, which he says carries the same figures.

items.stem: What does the auditor do?

options.text: Recompute the drawing power after deducting the margin stipulated in the sanction and creditors for goods, test whether the outstanding then exceeded the drawing power and for how long, and test the branch's identification of non-performing assets himself rather than accepting the system-generated list
options.why: Drawing power is worked out from the latest stock and book-debt statement after deducting the margin stipulated in the sanction and the creditors for goods; on the gross value it is a limit the borrower never had, and an outstanding above the real drawing power is what the norms read. The system-generated list is produced on parameters configured by the entity, so it is information produced by the entity: its accuracy and completeness are established, and the auditor examines the symptoms himself.

options.text: Obtain a written representation from the branch manager that the drawing power has been correctly computed and that the list of non-performing assets is complete
options.misconception: substitutes management's word for the recomputation and the testing the auditor can perform himself
options.why: A written representation is audit evidence but is not sufficient appropriate audit evidence on its own about any of the matters it deals with, and here the auditor can recompute the drawing power from the statement in front of him. Taking the branch's word about the branch's own returns is the weakest evidence available on the point.

options.text: Accept the classification, since the outstanding is within the sanctioned limit of ₹4 crore and the account has not exceeded it
options.misconception: reads the sanctioned limit as the only ceiling, when the drawing power is the operative one and can be far lower
options.why: The sanctioned limit is the outer ceiling; the drawing power is what the borrower may actually draw on a given date, and it moves with the stock and book-debt statement. An outstanding comfortably inside the sanctioned limit can sit above the drawing power for months, and that is one of the conditions the norms treat as an out-of-order account.

options.text: Accept the classification but report the drawing power computation in the long form audit report, the LFAR being the place for advances observations
options.misconception: routes a finding by its subject to a questionnaire instead of testing whether the figures being reported on are wrong
options.why: The long form audit report describes; it does not correct a classification. If the recomputed drawing power shows the account was out of order, the classification and the provision in the branch returns are wrong and the branch auditor's own report and memorandum of changes are what carry that, whatever the LFAR also says.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — drawing power computed from the latest stock and book-debt statement after the margin stipulated in the sanction, and the auditor's own testing of the branch's identification of non-performing assets, read with SA 500 on information produced by the entity

items.scenario: At a bank branch you examine a cash credit facility of ₹4 crore against hypothecation of stock and book debts. The branch has computed drawing power from the borrower's stock statement on the gross value of the stock, without deducting the margin stipulated in the sanction and without deducting creditors for the goods included in that stock. The account is not on the branch's system-generated list of non-performing assets, and the manager says the list is produced centrally from the core banking system and needs no further work.

items.stem: What is the auditor's finding?

options.text: Report the matter at once to the Central Government under section 143(12), off-market rebooking being an offence involving fraud
options.misconception: jumps from a control deficiency and a suspicious pattern to a statutory fraud report before there is reason to believe an offence involving fraud has been committed
options.why: Section 143(12) is engaged where the auditor has reason to believe that an offence involving fraud is being or has been committed against the company by its officers or employees. A weak segregation and a pattern worth investigating is not yet that belief; the step here is to investigate the rebooked deals and to communicate the deficiency, and the reporting machinery starts if the investigation produces the belief.

options.text: A significant deficiency in internal control — the front, mid and back office functions are not segregated, and cancellation and rebooking at off-market rates is a recognised means of postponing a loss; the auditor confirms deals independently with the counterparty and the exchange and communicates the deficiency
options.why: A dealer who confirms his own deals and writes his own slips has collapsed the front, mid and back office into one person, and the independent check that the whole treasury control structure rests on has gone. Cancellation and rebooking with the same counterparty at off-market rates is the classic route by which a loss is moved to a later period, so the auditor confirms deals independently with the counterparty and against the exchange or clearing corporation record rather than from the dealer's slip.

options.text: No finding — every deal was inside the counterparty and open-position limits sanctioned by the board, and a limit not breached means the control worked
options.misconception: treats a limit check as a substitute for the segregation of duties that makes the limit check meaningful
options.why: A limit is a ceiling on exposure; it says nothing about whether the deal reported is the deal that was struck. Where one person deals, confirms and records, the figures against which the limit is monitored are produced by the person the limit is meant to restrain, so compliance with the limit proves nothing about the segregation of duties.

options.text: Record it in the long form audit report alone, since it is an internal control matter and the financial statements are unaffected
options.misconception: parks a significant deficiency in internal control in a supplementary questionnaire instead of communicating it as SA 265 requires
options.why: SA 265 requires the auditor to communicate in writing, to those charged with governance, deficiencies in internal control that he has identified during the audit and that are of sufficient importance to merit their attention. A questionnaire answered for another reader does not discharge that, and off-market rebooking is not safely assumed to leave the financial statements unaffected until it has been examined.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — segregation of the front, mid and back office, independent confirmation of deals with the counterparty and the exchange, and scrutiny of deals cancelled and rebooked at off-market rates, read with SA 265

items.scenario: In a bank's treasury you find that one senior dealer strikes deals, telephones the counterparty to confirm them himself, and prepares the deal slips that go to accounts. Over the year fourteen deals with one counterparty were cancelled and rebooked, several at rates materially away from the market rate ruling at the time. The head of treasury tells you every deal was inside the counterparty and open-position limits sanctioned by the board and that no loss has arisen, so there is nothing to report.

items.stem: Which committee does each file answer to?

options.text: Neither — the committees' recommendations are the bank's internal management matter and the statutory auditor does not report on them
options.misconception: treats a matter the LFAR expressly asks about as outside the auditor's reporting
options.why: The long form audit report expressly asks the auditor to report on the implementation of both sets of recommendations, and what he reports is compliance rather than recital: a recommendation not implemented is reported as not implemented, and one implemented on paper with no evidence that it operated is not implemented.

options.text: The first file answers the Ghosh Committee, which was on frauds and malpractices in banks; the second answers the Jilani Committee, which was on the internal control and inspection or audit system in banks
options.why: The Ghosh Committee dealt with frauds and malpractices in banks, and its recommendations are the anti-fraud housekeeping — rotation of staff on sensitive seats and compulsory leave, joint custody, control over security stationery, verification of specimen signatures and prompt reconciliation. The Jilani Committee dealt with the internal control and inspection or audit system in banks, and its recommendations are the machinery that checks — an independent inspection department, the inspection cycle, concurrent audit and the rectification of irregularities. The auditor reports on the implementation of both in the long form audit report.

options.text: The first answers the Jilani Committee and the second the Ghosh Committee
options.misconception: swaps the two committees, which is the single commonest error on this question
options.why: It is the other way round. Joint custody, compulsory leave and control over security stationery are measures aimed at preventing and detecting a fraud, which is the Ghosh Committee's subject. An inspection cycle and concurrent audit coverage are the audit and inspection machinery, which is the Jilani Committee's.

options.text: Both answer the Ghosh Committee; the Jilani Committee dealt with the recovery of non-performing assets
options.misconception: attaches the Jilani Committee to a subject it never dealt with, leaving the internal control recommendations unreported
options.why: The Jilani Committee's subject was the internal control and inspection or audit system in banks, not recovery. Answering both files under one committee leaves the internal control and inspection recommendations unreported in the long form audit report, which is itself the reporting failure the question is testing.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — the Ghosh Committee on frauds and malpractices in banks, the Jilani Committee on the internal control and inspection or audit system in banks, and the reporting on implementation of both in the long form audit report

items.scenario: Your senior asks you to complete the part of the long form audit report dealing with the two committees. The branch has given you one file marked "rotation of staff on sensitive seats, compulsory leave, joint custody of security stationery and specimen signature verification" and a second marked "inspection cycle for the branch, concurrent audit coverage and rectification of irregularities reported in the last inspection".

items.stem: What is the correct treatment?

options.text: List all four in the memorandum of changes and issue an unqualified report, since the memorandum forms part of the report and the central statutory auditors will apply the changes
options.misconception: uses the memorandum as a substitute for the modification a material unaccepted change requires
options.why: The memorandum tells the head office what to change; the opinion tells the reader whether the figures reported are right. A material misstatement the branch has refused to correct requires a modified opinion, and the two accepted entries are not changes at all because they are already in the books.

options.text: Only the two unaccepted changes go in the memorandum of changes; and being material and refused, they require the branch audit report to be qualified as well, the memorandum quantifying what has been qualified
options.why: A change the branch has already passed is in the books and is not a change to the returns being reported on, so the two accepted entries come out of the memorandum of changes. The two refused changes go in whether or not the branch agrees, and because their effect is material to the branch's financial statements the report is qualified: the memorandum quantifies the qualification and does not replace it.

options.text: List all four in the memorandum and describe the refusal in the long form audit report, which is where the central auditors will read it
options.misconception: parks a material unaccepted change in a supplementary questionnaire instead of qualifying the report
options.why: A matter grave enough to affect the branch's figures belongs in the report carrying the opinion, qualified. The long form audit report is a supplement and answers a different reader, and it never carries a modification the audit report should have carried.

options.text: Include only the two accepted changes, since the other two are disputed and the branch's view on its own advances should prevail
options.misconception: lets the auditee decide what the auditor reports
options.why: The memorandum of changes is the auditor's statement of the changes he considers necessary, and a change goes in whether or not the branch has accepted it. Excluding the disputed items would leave the central statutory auditors with the branch's figures and no notice that the auditor disagrees with them.
keywords: whether or not the branch has accepted

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — the memorandum of changes: changes included whether or not accepted by the branch, changes already carried out in the books excluded, and the memorandum as a supplement to the branch audit report rather than a substitute for a qualification

items.scenario: As branch auditor you proposed four changes. The branch accepted two and passed the entries before you signed. It refuses the other two, which reclassify three advances and increase the provision on them by an amount material to the branch's own results. Your manager proposes to list all four changes in the memorandum of changes and to issue an unqualified branch audit report, on the footing that the memorandum tells the central statutory auditors everything.

items.stem: What must you do?

options.text: Wait for the legal advice, and resign if the Board still disagrees when it arrives
options.misconception: substitutes withdrawal for the reporting the directions require, and lets the auditee set the timing of a duty with its own time limit
options.why: Resignation reports nothing to anybody, and the directions fix a period within which the exception report is to be made, so waiting on the company's advisers can put the auditor out of time on a duty that is his. He reports first; what the legal advice says goes to the Board and, if it changes his conclusion, to the regulator as well.

options.text: Report the matter to the Central Government under section 143(12), non-compliance with the Reserve Bank's requirements being an offence involving fraud
options.misconception: turns a regulatory non-compliance into an offence involving fraud, which section 143(12) alone addresses
options.why: Section 143(12) is engaged where the auditor has reason to believe that an offence involving fraud is being or has been committed against the company by its officers or employees. A change in the asset and income pattern that costs the company its entitlement to the certificate is a regulatory matter, not by itself such an offence, and the route for it is the Regional Office of the Reserve Bank.
