options.text: A qualified or adverse opinion, opening inventory at 22 per cent of total assets being material to the current period's financial statements
options.misconception: applies the misstatement pair of opinions to a case that is an inability to obtain evidence
options.why: Qualified or adverse is the answer where the opening balances contain a misstatement that is not properly dealt with. Nothing here says the figure is wrong; what is absent is the evidence, and absent evidence produces a qualification or a disclaimer.

options.text: An unmodified opinion with an Other Matter paragraph recording that the prior period was not audited
options.misconception: uses an Other Matter paragraph to carry an inability to obtain audit evidence
options.why: A paragraph recording that fact tells the reader who audited the comparatives and nothing more. It supplies no evidence about a balance that flows into this year's cost of sales, and a paragraph never carries a modification.

options.text: An unmodified opinion, provided the notes disclose that the comparative figures are unaudited
options.misconception: treats a disclosure by the entity as curing the auditor's own inability to obtain evidence
options.why: A disclosure by the entity is not audit evidence, and the difficulty is not with the comparatives as such. The opening balances feed this year's figures, so the auditor's inability to obtain evidence about them is answered in his opinion rather than in the company's notes.

options.text: A qualified opinion or a disclaimer of opinion, as appropriate, this being an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding the opening balances
options.why: SA 510 separates the two ways an opening balance damages the current opinion, and this is the first of them. Where the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding the opening balances, he expresses a qualified opinion or a disclaimer of opinion, as appropriate, under SA 705 (Revised). The qualified-or-adverse pair belongs to the other case, where an opening balance contains a misstatement that materially affects the current period and the effect is not properly accounted for or adequately presented or disclosed.
keywords: unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding the opening balances
qualified opinion or a disclaimer of opinion

citation.ref: para 10, read against para 11

items.scenario: You are appointed for the first time to audit a company whose previous year was audited by nobody, the company having been below the threshold then. Opening inventory is 22 per cent of total assets. The records of the previous count are missing, the goods are perishable and the population has turned over several times, so no roll-back from the current count is possible. Nothing suggests the figure is wrong; you simply cannot obtain evidence about it.

items.stem: What follows in each case?

options.text: Neither — in each case the answer is to have the sentence about arm's length terms taken out of the notes
options.misconception: answers a problem with a disclosure by removing the disclosure, dropping a requirement of the framework in the process
options.why: Deleting the sentence would remove a disclosure the applicable financial reporting framework requires where the assertion is made, and would leave the reader knowing less than before. The auditor obtains evidence about the assertion and then reports what his work found.

options.text: Both are inabilities to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, neither company having supported the assertion it made
options.misconception: files a contradicted assertion as missing evidence, when the evidence exists and disproves it
options.why: The first file is not empty. It holds evidence, and that evidence points the other way. Evidence contradicting an assertion is a finding about the disclosure rather than an absence of evidence about it, and treating it as unaudited would leave a disclosure the auditor has disproved standing in the notes.

options.text: In the first the assertion is misstated and is dealt with as any other misstatement; in the second there is an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about a disclosure the framework requires, with the consequences SA 705 (Revised) attaches
options.why: SA 550 requires the auditor to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about an assertion that a related party transaction was conducted on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction, and that work can end in two different places. Where the audit evidence contradicts the assertion, the disclosure is wrong and it is a misstatement, accumulated and evaluated like any other. Where there is an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about an assertion the framework requires to be disclosed, SA 705 (Revised) decides what the opinion says.
keywords: inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence
terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction

options.text: Both are misstatements, because an assertion the auditor cannot support is an assertion that should never have been made
options.misconception: converts an inability to obtain evidence into a misstatement, which asserts more than the auditor knows
options.why: Unsupported and disproved are not the same thing. Where nothing can be obtained about an assertion the framework requires to be disclosed, what the auditor has is an inability to obtain evidence, and SA 705 (Revised) is where that is answered.

citation.ref: para 24, read with SA 705 (Revised)

items.scenario: Two companies in the same group each pay a ₹40 crore management fee to the parent, and the notes of each state that the fee was on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction, which the applicable financial reporting framework requires to be disclosed where the assertion is made. In the first company your work produces market data showing that unrelated providers charge a third of that fee for the same services. In the second you can find no comparable at all, and management's process for supporting the assertion produces nothing you can test.

items.stem: What must the practitioner do before agreeing to accept the engagement?

options.text: Begin the work and raise each of these matters in the report, acceptance turning on the engagement letter alone and every one of them being describable as a limitation
options.misconception: converts a set of pre-acceptance determinations into matters to be disclosed in the report
options.why: The standard makes them acceptance matters, which means they decide whether there is an engagement at all. A practitioner who cannot obtain a sufficient understanding of the acquiree cannot perform the procedures, and describing that in a report he was never in a position to write answers nothing.

options.text: Accept, provided the modified opinion on the sources is quoted in full in his own report, which puts the reader in the same position as the practitioner
options.misconception: answers a question about what the law permits by doing the very thing whose permissibility is in doubt
options.why: What the standard asks is whether the relevant law or regulation permits the use of, or a reference in the practitioner's report to, the modified audit opinion on those sources. Whether he may quote it is the question, and quoting it assumes the answer.

options.text: Accept on the footing that a prospectus is a statutory document, so the responsible party's acknowledgement of its responsibilities is implied by law and need not be obtained
options.misconception: treats the statutory character of the document as substituting for an acknowledgement the standard requires the practitioner to obtain
options.why: The standard requires the practitioner to obtain the responsible party's agreement acknowledging and understanding its responsibility for describing the applicable criteria to the intended users where these are not publicly available, for compiling the information on the basis of those criteria, and for giving him access to all relevant information, to any additional information he requests, and to the people from whom he determines it necessary to obtain evidence. Nothing about a prospectus supplies that agreement.

options.text: Work through the acceptance matters — his capabilities and competence; that the applicable criteria are suitable and it is unlikely the information will be misleading for the purpose intended; that he will likely be able to express the prescribed opinion; whether law or regulation permits use of, or reference to, the modified opinion on the sources; whether he can obtain a sufficient understanding of the never-audited acquiree; and obtain the responsible party's acknowledgement of its responsibilities
options.why: SAE 3420 puts a defined list before acceptance rather than after it. The practitioner determines that he has the capabilities and competence to perform the engagement; on a preliminary knowledge of the circumstances and discussion with the responsible party, that the applicable criteria are suitable and that it is unlikely the pro forma financial information will be misleading for the purpose for which it is intended; and, where the wording is prescribed by law or regulation, that he will likely be able to express the opinion so prescribed on the basis of the procedures this standard specifies. Where the sources carry a modified audit opinion he considers whether the relevant law or regulation permits their use or a reference to them in his report; where an acquiree's historical financial information has never been audited or reviewed he considers whether he can obtain a sufficient understanding of the acquiree and its accounting and financial reporting practices. And he obtains the responsible party's agreement acknowledging its responsibilities, which cannot wait for a draft.
keywords: capabilities and competence to perform the engagement
misleading for the purpose for which it is intended

citation.ref: the matters the practitioner considers before agreeing to accept an engagement to report on the compilation of pro forma financial information included in a prospectus, including the responsible party's acknowledgement of its responsibilities

items.scenario: A practitioner is asked to report on whether pro forma financial information in a prospectus has been compiled on the basis of the applicable criteria. The transaction is the acquisition of a family-owned target whose historical financial information has never been audited or reviewed. The issuer's own unadjusted financial information is extracted from statements carrying a modified audit opinion. The regulator prescribes the exact wording of the practitioner's opinion. The responsible party says it will discuss its own responsibilities "once the report is drafted".

items.stem: What does SA 540 (Revised) require of you?

options.text: Accept the ₹185 crore, since it falls inside a range the company's own expert produced and any figure inside an expert's range is by definition reasonable
options.misconception: treats a number sitting inside somebody's range as proof that management addressed the estimation uncertainty, when the choice of where to sit inside it is the whole question
options.why: A range is the measure of the estimation uncertainty, not an answer to it. Management chose a point near one end and recorded no reasoning for that choice, which is exactly the gap the standard fills by having the auditor build his own range.

options.text: Compute your own single best figure, substitute it for management's, and treat the whole difference as a misstatement to be corrected
options.misconception: replaces management's estimate with the auditor's own point figure, when the standard has him develop a range to test reasonableness rather than to supplant the estimate
options.why: The auditor evaluates the reasonableness of management's estimate; he does not make the estimate. Where his range and management's figure do not overlap there is a misstatement to discuss, but a single auditor's figure imposed on the accounts turns the reviewer into the preparer.

options.text: Qualify the opinion at once for an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, an outcome spread of that width not being auditable
options.misconception: converts high estimation uncertainty into a scope limitation before performing the procedures the standard prescribes for exactly that situation
options.why: High estimation uncertainty is the condition SA 540 was written for, not a reason to stop. The standard supplies the response — the auditor's own range, tests of the data and assumptions, and evidence from events up to the report date — and a modification is considered only after those have been performed and have failed.

options.text: Develop a range with which to evaluate the reasonableness of the estimate, management not having adequately addressed the effects of the estimation uncertainty on an estimate giving rise to a significant risk; and, among your responses, determine whether events occurring up to the date of the auditor's report provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence about it
options.why: Where management has not adequately addressed the effects of estimation uncertainty on an accounting estimate that gives rise to a significant risk, the auditor shall develop a range with which to evaluate the reasonableness of the estimate. The responses to the assessed risk also include testing the data used, evaluating whether the method of measurement is appropriate and the assumptions reasonable, and determining whether events occurring up to the date of the auditor's report provide evidence about the estimate — an actual tender or settlement after the year end being worth more than a debate about the model.
keywords: events occurring up to the date of the auditor's report

citation.ref: the responses to the assessed risks of material misstatement for an accounting estimate, and the auditor's range where management has not adequately addressed the effects of estimation uncertainty on an estimate giving rise to a significant risk

items.scenario: A company carries a decommissioning provision for an offshore platform. Its own consultant gave a range of plausible outcomes running from ₹180 crore to ₹520 crore, and management has booked ₹185 crore, near the bottom of that range. The file records no assessment by management of the effect of the estimation uncertainty on the amount chosen, and you have assessed the provision as an estimate giving rise to a significant risk.

items.stem: What does SA 560 require of you now?

options.text: Issue a new auditor's report with an Other Matter paragraph describing the fact, a fresh report being the only lever the auditor has once the statements are out
options.misconception: reports afresh on financial statements management has not amended, when the amendment is the condition on which a new report is issued at all
options.why: The new or amended report with its Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph belongs to the case where management does amend. Reporting again on unamended statements would put a second report on the same wrong numbers and leave the members no better off.

options.text: Resign as auditor and say nothing further, the duty of confidentiality barring any step that reaches the members directly
options.misconception: uses confidentiality to bar the step the standard names, and treats resignation as a substitute for it
options.why: The standard directs the auditor to seek to prevent future reliance on his own report, which is his document and his name. Resigning leaves the report standing and the members relying on it, which is the outcome the requirement exists to prevent.

options.text: Nothing further — after the financial statements have been issued the auditor has no obligation to perform any audit procedures on them, and management's refusal ends the matter
options.misconception: reads the end of the duty to search as the end of the duty once a fact has arrived and management has refused to act on it
options.why: The sentence removing the obligation removes the duty to go looking. It says nothing about what happens once a fact has reached the auditor, and the requirement that follows it is written for precisely the refusal described here.

options.text: Notify management and those charged with governance that you will seek to prevent future reliance on the auditor's report, and if they still do not act, take appropriate action to seek to prevent that reliance
options.why: Where management does not take the steps needed to ensure that everyone in receipt of the previously issued financial statements is informed, and does not amend them when the auditor requires it, the auditor shall notify management and those charged with governance that he will seek to prevent future reliance on the auditor's report. If they still do not act, he takes appropriate action to seek to prevent that reliance. The discussion, the determination whether amendment is needed and the inquiry into management's intentions have already happened here; this is the step after them.
keywords: notify management and those charged with governance

citation.ref: the auditor's action where management neither amends the previously issued financial statements nor informs those who received them

items.scenario: The financial statements and your report went to members on 12 August and were laid before the annual general meeting. On 5 October a fact reaches you that, had you known it at the date of your report, would have caused you to modify your opinion. You discuss it with management and with those charged with governance and ask how they intend to address it. They decline to amend the financial statements and decline to inform anyone who already holds them.

items.stem: What does SA 610 (Revised) still require before that work is used?

options.text: Obtain a written representation from the head of internal audit that the counts were properly performed, and place it on file instead of the evaluation
options.misconception: substitutes a representation from the party whose work is being judged for the external auditor's own evaluation of that work
options.why: A representation from the function is not evidence about the quality of the function's work, and a written representation is never sufficient appropriate audit evidence on its own. The standard asks the external auditor to read the reports, evaluate the work and perform his own procedures on it.

options.text: Re-perform every procedure the function carried out at all nine depots, since responsibility for the opinion is the external auditor's alone
options.misconception: turns a sample of reperformance into a duplicate audit, which would make using the work pointless and is not what the standard asks for
options.why: Sole responsibility for the opinion is real and it does not mean doing the work twice. The requirement is to perform sufficient audit procedures on the body of work as a whole, reperformance included, so that the external auditor can judge the work — not to repeat all of it, which would leave nothing for the function's work to contribute.

options.text: Nothing more — the three conditions have been met, so the function's work may be taken as it stands
options.misconception: treats the gate on the function as a gate on every file the function produces, when the two are separate evaluations
options.why: The first evaluation is about the function; the second is about the work. A competent and objective function applying a disciplined approach can still produce a file that was under-supervised or that reaches a conclusion its own evidence does not support, and the standard asks the external auditor to look.

options.text: Read the function's reports on the work being used and evaluate whether that work was properly planned, performed, supervised, reviewed and documented, whether sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained and whether the conclusions reached are appropriate; perform audit procedures on the body of that work as a whole, including reperformance; and communicate to those charged with governance how the use of the function's work has been planned
options.why: Passing the three conditions decides that the function's work may be used at all. Before any particular body of work is used the external auditor reads the relevant reports and evaluates whether the work was properly planned, performed, supervised, reviewed and documented, whether sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained to support the conclusions, and whether those conclusions are appropriate; and he performs audit procedures on that body of work as a whole, including reperformance of some of it. He also communicates the planned use to those charged with governance, so the people who oversee the audit know what rests on the function.
keywords: properly planned, performed, supervised, reviewed and documented

citation.ref: the evaluation of the internal audit function's work before it is used, the audit procedures on the body of work as a whole including reperformance, and the communication to those charged with governance of the planned use of that work

items.scenario: You have evaluated the internal audit function's organisational status and relevant policies and procedures, its level of competence and whether it applies a systematic and disciplined approach, and all three are satisfactory. The team now plans to take the function's inventory count files for nine depots straight into the audit file, having read the one-page dashboard the function circulates to the audit committee, and to tell nobody outside the team that it has done so.

items.stem: What does SA 710 require in your report on the current period?

options.text: Withdraw last year's auditor's report and issue a fresh report on last year's financial statements
options.misconception: reopens a completed engagement instead of dealing with the corresponding figures in the report the auditor is about to sign
options.why: SA 710 deals with the misstatement where it now sits, in the corresponding figures of the current period's financial statements. Reissuing a prior year report is the machinery of SA 560 for facts known after that report was issued, and it is not what this requirement directs.

options.text: An Other Matter paragraph describing the prior year error, the opinion itself being left unmodified
options.misconception: answers a misstatement with a paragraph that carries no opinion, when the standard answers this one inside the opinion
options.why: An Other Matter paragraph communicates a matter relevant to users' understanding of the audit or the report. It does not cure figures that are wrong. Where the misstatement has not been dealt with under the framework, the standard calls for a modified opinion.

options.text: Verify whether the misstatement has been dealt with as required by the applicable financial reporting framework and, since it has not, express a qualified or an adverse opinion on the current period's financial statements, in respect of the corresponding figures
options.why: The rule that the opinion does not refer to the corresponding figures carries exceptions, and this is one of them. Where the auditor obtains evidence that a material misstatement exists in prior period financial statements on which an unmodified opinion was previously issued, he verifies whether the misstatement has been dealt with as required under the applicable financial reporting framework and, if it has not, expresses a qualified or an adverse opinion on the current period's financial statements, modified in respect of the corresponding figures included in them.

options.text: Nothing in the opinion — where comparatives are presented as corresponding figures the opinion refers to the current period only and does not refer to them
options.misconception: reads the general rule as absolute, when SA 710 sets out the exceptions in which the current opinion does reach the corresponding figures
options.why: That rule is the starting point and it has named exceptions. One is a prior modification still unresolved; the other is this one, a material misstatement discovered in a prior period that carried an unmodified opinion. The corresponding figures sit inside this year's financial statements, so a misstatement left in them is a misstatement in the statements you are reporting on.

citation.ref: the exceptions to the rule that the auditor's opinion does not refer to the corresponding figures, where a material misstatement exists in prior period financial statements on which an unmodified opinion was issued

items.scenario: You audited this company last year and issued an unmodified opinion. During this year's audit you obtain evidence that last year's closing inventory was overstated by ₹31 crore, an amount material to last year. The comparatives are presented as corresponding figures. Management has left the corresponding figures exactly as they were reported and has made no restatement or disclosure of the error anywhere in this year's financial statements.

items.stem: What must the Other Matter paragraph in your report state?

options.text: That the corresponding figures are unaudited
options.misconception: uses the paragraph written for figures nobody audited on figures a predecessor auditor did audit and did report on
options.why: That statement belongs to the different case where the prior period financial statements were not audited at all. Saying it here would be untrue, and it would also drop the predecessor's opinion out of sight.

options.text: That the corresponding figures were audited by the predecessor auditor, the type of opinion the predecessor expressed and, if that opinion was modified, the reasons for the modification, and the date of that report
options.why: SA 710 names three things for the Other Matter paragraph in exactly this situation — that the corresponding figures were audited by the predecessor auditor, the type of opinion he expressed together with the reasons for any modification, and the date of that report. A reader then knows who stood behind last year's figures, what he concluded and as at when.

options.text: Only that a change of auditor took place during the year and the name of the outgoing firm
options.misconception: names the person and omits the two facts a reader actually needs, being what the predecessor concluded and the date on which he concluded it
options.why: The identity of the predecessor is one of three elements. Without the type of opinion and the date of the report a reader cannot tell whether the corresponding figures were reported on cleanly, or as at what point in time.

options.text: Nothing — where the prior period was audited by another firm the incoming auditor says nothing about it, the opinion covering the current period only
options.misconception: reads the rule that the opinion does not refer to the corresponding figures as removing every reporting obligation about them
options.why: Not referring to the corresponding figures in the opinion is one thing; the Other Matter paragraph is another, and SA 710 requires it in the situations where a reader would otherwise not know who audited the comparatives or what he found.

citation.ref: the Other Matter paragraph where the prior period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor

items.scenario: This is your first year as auditor of a company. The prior period's financial statements were audited by the outgoing auditor, whose report was unmodified and was dated 12 July 2025. The comparatives are presented as corresponding figures, and nothing in law or regulation prohibits you from referring to the predecessor's report.

items.stem: Is the manager right?

options.text: No, and the section should state that the auditor has audited the other information and found it consistent with the financial statements
options.misconception: converts a section whose whole purpose is to say that no opinion is given into one that gives a clean opinion
options.why: The auditor does not audit the other information and expresses no opinion or conclusion on it. The section says so in terms, and a sentence claiming an audit of it would contradict the statement immediately above.

options.text: No — for an unlisted entity the section is included where the auditor has obtained some or all of the other information at the date of his report, and where nothing is wrong it carries a statement that the auditor has nothing to report
options.why: The Other Information section is triggered by the other information having been obtained, not by a finding. For an unlisted entity it is included where the auditor has obtained some or all of the other information at the date of his report. It identifies what was obtained, says that management is responsible for it, states that the auditor's opinion does not cover it and that no opinion or conclusion is expressed on it, describes his responsibilities for reading and considering it, and then either says he has nothing to report or describes the uncorrected material misstatement.

options.text: He is wrong about unlisted entities but right about listed ones, where the section covers only other information actually obtained before the date of the report
options.misconception: drops the half of the listed-entity trigger that reaches other information the auditor expects to obtain after the date of his report
options.why: For a listed entity the section is included where the auditor has obtained, or expects to obtain, other information, and it identifies both the other information obtained before the date of the report and that expected after it. Leaving out what is expected would hide the part of the annual report that is usually typeset last.

options.text: Yes — the section is there to describe an uncorrected material misstatement of the other information, so with nothing to describe it is omitted
options.misconception: makes the section conditional on a finding, when it is conditional on other information having been obtained or, for a listed entity, expected
options.why: The section tells the reader what the auditor did with the other information and, just as importantly, what he did not do with it. A reader who sees no such section cannot tell whether the auditor read the directors' report or never saw it.

citation.ref: the Other Information section of the auditor's report — when it is included for a listed and for an unlisted entity, and what it contains

items.scenario: You are signing the report of an unlisted company. Before the date of your report you obtained the directors' report and the management discussion and analysis, read both, and found no material inconsistency and nothing else materially misstated. The manager proposes to leave the Other Information section out of the report altogether, saying that the section exists to describe a problem and there is no problem, and that in any event it is a listed company requirement.

items.stem: What does SA 800 require of the auditor here?

options.text: Qualify the opinion for the ambiguity, since a reader cannot tell which reading produced the revenue figure
options.misconception: modifies the opinion before performing the step the standard requires first, which is to obtain the understanding of the interpretation management adopted
options.why: The understanding comes first. It may show that management's reading is the one the contract bears, or that the interpretation adopted needs disclosing. A modification is what happens after that work, not instead of it.

options.text: Nothing — the contract is the framework, and interpreting a contract is a question of law for the parties rather than a matter for the auditor
options.misconception: treats the framework's own ambiguity as somebody else's problem, when the framework is the measure against which the opinion is given
options.why: The opinion says whether the statements are prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the framework. Where the framework itself can be read two ways and the readings differ materially, the auditor cannot form that opinion without understanding which reading management took and why.

options.text: Refuse the engagement, a framework capable of two reasonable readings not being an acceptable financial reporting framework
options.misconception: rejects a contractual framework outright, when the standard provides for one and asks instead about its attributes and about management's interpretations of it
options.why: Financial reporting provisions of a contract are one of the standard's own examples of a special purpose framework. Ambiguity in a clause is dealt with by understanding and, where needed, by disclosure of the interpretation adopted — not by declining the work.

options.text: Obtain an understanding of the significant interpretations of the contract that management made in preparing the financial statements — an interpretation being significant where the adoption of another reasonable interpretation would have produced a material difference in the information presented — a contractual framework being acceptable only where it exhibits the attributes normally exhibited by an acceptable financial reporting framework
options.why: Where financial statements are prepared under the provisions of a contract, SA 800 has the auditor obtain an understanding of any significant interpretations of the contract that management made. An interpretation is significant where the adoption of another reasonable interpretation would have produced a material difference in the information presented in the financial statements, which is exactly what the second reading does here. At acceptance the question is whether the framework the contract sets up exhibits the attributes normally exhibited by an acceptable financial reporting framework — a framework laid down by an authorised body or prescribed by law is presumed acceptable, but a contract is not.

citation.ref: acceptability of the financial reporting framework, and the significant interpretations of a contract where the financial statements are prepared under the financial reporting provisions of that contract

items.scenario: A concession agreement requires the operator to deliver audited financial statements prepared under the accounting clauses of that agreement. One clause defines the revenue the operator may recognise in language that bears two readings. Management has adopted one of them; on the other, equally reasonable, reading, revenue for the year would be ₹64 crore lower on a stated top line of ₹300 crore.

items.stem: What does SA 805 require?

options.text: Nothing — both opinions are unmodified, so no reader is worse off for the two sitting side by side
options.misconception: treats presentation as cosmetic, when the risk being guarded against is a reader taking a report on one element as a report on the whole
options.why: The hazard is not the content of either opinion but the confusion between them. A reader who takes a clean opinion on a receivables schedule for a clean opinion on the financial statements has been misled by the layout alone.

options.text: Combine the two engagements into one auditor's report carrying one opinion covering the financial statements and the schedule together
options.misconception: merges two engagements the standard deliberately keeps apart, each with its own scope, its own materiality and its own opinion
options.why: The two are separate engagements. Materiality determined for a specific element may be lower than for the complete set, and the procedures differ accordingly, so one combined opinion would describe neither engagement accurately.

options.text: Ask management to rectify the presentation, because the audited specific element is being published together with the complete set and the presentation does not sufficiently differentiate it from them, and do not issue the report on the specific element until you are satisfied with the differentiation; a separate opinion is expressed for each engagement
options.why: Where an audited single financial statement or specific element is published together with the entity's complete set of financial statements and the presentation does not sufficiently differentiate the one from the other, the auditor asks management to rectify the situation, and he shall not issue the auditor's report containing the opinion on the specific element until he is satisfied with that differentiation. Where the same auditor does both, he expresses a separate opinion for each engagement.

options.text: Add an Other Matter paragraph to the report on the complete set cross-referring to the report on the schedule
options.misconception: answers a presentation problem with a paragraph, leaving the presentation that caused it unchanged
options.why: A cross-reference does not separate two documents a reader sees as one. The standard's answer is to have the presentation itself put right before the report on the element is released.

citation.ref: publication of an audited single financial statement or specific element together with the complete set of financial statements, and the separate opinion for each engagement

items.scenario: You audited a company's complete set of financial statements and issued an unmodified opinion. You were separately engaged to audit its schedule of trade receivables, and that work is also complete and clean. The company now proposes to print your report on the schedule immediately after the financial statements in the same annual report, under the same running heads and with continuous page numbering, so that the schedule reads as one further statement in the set.

items.stem: What does SA 810 require your report on the summary financial statements to say?

options.text: That the auditor's report on the audited financial statements contains a disclaimer of opinion, with a description of the basis for it, and that as a result of the disclaimer it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the summary financial statements
options.why: Where the auditor's report on the audited financial statements contains an adverse opinion or a disclaimer of opinion, the report on the summary financial statements states that fact, describes the basis for that adverse opinion or disclaimer of opinion, and states that as a result it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the summary financial statements. A summary cannot be sounder than what it summarises, however faithfully it reproduces it.

options.text: An unmodified opinion that the summary financial statements are consistent, in all material respects, with the audited financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria
options.misconception: applies the ordinary consistency test to a source on which no opinion was expressed, so a faithful summary of unaudited numbers would carry a clean opinion
options.why: Consistency with the audited financial statements is the ordinary form of the opinion, and it presupposes an opinion on those statements. Where the auditor disclaimed one, a statement that the summary is consistent with them would tell a reader far more than the audit supports.

options.text: The disclaimer itself should be repeated as the opinion on the summary financial statements
options.misconception: expresses a disclaimer on the summary, when the standard has the auditor say that expressing any opinion on it is inappropriate
options.why: A disclaimer of opinion on the summary would suggest the auditor was unable to obtain evidence about the summary. The problem lies with the source, and the standard's wording says exactly that.

options.text: The engagement must be refused outright, no report of any kind being possible where the source carried a disclaimer
options.misconception: treats a report the standard actually prescribes as an engagement that cannot be accepted at all
options.why: The standard does not close the engagement; it fixes what the report says. The report is issued, it states the disclaimer and its basis, and it says that expressing an opinion on the summary is inappropriate — which is a good deal more informative to a reader than silence.

citation.ref: the report on summary financial statements where the auditor's report on the audited financial statements contains an adverse opinion or a disclaimer of opinion

items.scenario: You audited a company's financial statements and disclaimed an opinion on them, having been unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about a large intangible asset. The company now asks you to report on a summary set derived from those same financial statements. It points out that you were the auditor of the source statements, that the criteria applied are disclosed, and that the summary agrees line for line with what you audited.

items.stem: Is there any route other than the additional date?

options.text: Yes — the auditor may instead provide a new or amended auditor's report that includes an Emphasis of Matter paragraph or an Other Matter paragraph stating that his procedures on subsequent events are restricted solely to the amendment of the financial statements as described in the relevant note
options.why: Where law, regulation or the financial reporting framework does not prohibit management from restricting the amendment to the effects of the subsequent event, and those responsible for approving the statements are not prohibited from restricting their approval to that amendment, the auditor is permitted to restrict his subsequent-event procedures to the amendment. He may then either amend the report to include an additional date restricted to that amendment, or provide a new or amended report containing an Emphasis of Matter paragraph or an Other Matter paragraph saying that his procedures on subsequent events are restricted solely to that amendment. Both routes rest on the same permission.
keywords: Emphasis of Matter paragraph or an Other Matter paragraph

options.text: No — the additional date is the only mechanism the standard provides for restricting the procedures to the amendment
options.misconception: keeps one of the two routes the standard offers and treats the other as unavailable
options.why: The standard offers a choice of two forms for the same restriction, and the paragraph route exists precisely for an auditor who does not want a second date on the report. What cannot be done is to restrict the procedures without saying so in one form or the other.

options.text: Yes — leave the report dated 20 May and say nothing, the amendment being management's own act
options.misconception: leaves a report dated before an amendment it does not mention, so the report on file does not match the statements it accompanies
options.why: The amended financial statements need a report that addresses them. A report predating the amendment and silent about it would be a report on a different set of statements from the one the members receive.

options.text: Yes — simply re-date the whole report to 4 June, which avoids two dates and needs no additional wording
options.misconception: takes a later date without the work a later date carries, which is subsequent-event procedures up to that date
options.why: Re-dating the report to 4 June extends the auditor's responsibility for subsequent events to 4 June and requires procedures up to that day. The restricted routes exist so that he may avoid that, and choosing the new date without the work would claim a responsibility he has not discharged.

citation.ref: the two routes where management restricts the amendment to the effects of a subsequent event — the additional date, and the Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph

items.scenario: Your report on the 31 March financial statements is dated 20 May. On 4 June, before the statements are issued, a major debtor is declared insolvent. Management amends the financial statements for that event alone and describes it in a note. Neither law nor the financial reporting framework prohibits management from restricting the amendment to that event, and those approving the statements are not prohibited from restricting their approval to the amendment. The engagement partner does not want two dates printed under his signature.

items.stem: What does SRE 2400 (Revised) require?

options.text: Express an adverse conclusion, a refusal of access on that scale meaning the financial statements do not give a true and fair view
options.misconception: uses the misstatement half of the modification grid to answer a problem sitting on the evidence half
options.why: An adverse conclusion says the financial statements are wrong. Nothing here says that; what has happened is that the practitioner has not been allowed to find out. Inability to obtain evidence leads to a qualified conclusion or a disclaimer, not to an adverse one.

options.text: Where the practitioner is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence he expresses a qualified conclusion if the possible effects could be material but not pervasive, and disclaims a conclusion if they could be both material and pervasive; and where management imposed the limitation after acceptance such that he believes he may need to disclaim, and the engagement is not required by law or regulation, he withdraws where practicable and possible
options.why: Modification in a review follows two tracks. Where the financial statements are materially misstated the conclusion is qualified or adverse. Where the practitioner is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence he expresses a qualified conclusion if the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be material but not pervasive, and disclaims a conclusion if they could be both material and pervasive. A limitation imposed by management after acceptance adds a further step — where he believes he may need to disclaim a conclusion because of it, and the engagement is not required by law or regulation, he withdraws from the engagement where withdrawal is practicable and possible.

options.text: Issue the unmodified conclusion — a review gives only limited assurance, so restricted access is already contemplated by the level of assurance
options.misconception: treats limited assurance as a licence to conclude on whatever evidence happens to be available
options.why: Limited assurance describes the level of the conclusion, not the amount of evidence needed to reach it. The practitioner must still obtain sufficient appropriate evidence for the conclusion he gives, and where he cannot, the conclusion is modified or withdrawn from.

options.text: Convert the engagement into an audit, so that access to the branch records can be insisted on as a matter of right
options.misconception: answers a scope limitation by changing the level of assurance, which is a change in the terms of the engagement and not a response to the limitation
options.why: Changing a review into an audit changes what was agreed with the client and needs its own justification and a new agreement. It would also give management, which has just restricted access, the choice of whether the change happens at all.

citation.ref: the modified conclusions where the practitioner is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence, and the withdrawal where management imposes a limitation after acceptance

items.scenario: You accepted an engagement to review a company's half-yearly financial statements. It is not required by any law or regulation; the company asked for it to satisfy a lender. After acceptance, management refuses you access to the records of four branches that between them carry a large part of revenue, and offers no alternative. You conclude that the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive.

items.stem: May those two sentences be deleted?

options.text: Yes to the first and no to the second — a report can hardly speculate about findings from procedures nobody performed
options.misconception: reads a statement about the limits of the procedures as speculation about what an audit would have found
options.why: The sentence makes no claim about what other work would have shown. It says that the procedures were the agreed ones and that others were not performed, which is why the reader draws his own conclusions rather than relying on an opinion.

options.text: Yes — both say in a longer way that no assurance is expressed, and the report states that once already
options.misconception: treats two statements about the limits of the work as a repetition of the statement about the level of assurance
options.why: Saying that no assurance is expressed tells the reader what the conclusion is worth. These two tell him what was and was not looked at, which is a different thing and the thing a reader of a seven-procedure report most needs.

options.text: No, but they belong in the engagement letter rather than in the report, where the parties agreed the scope in the first place
options.misconception: moves statements the report is required to carry into a document only the engaging parties hold
options.why: The engagement letter also records the procedures and the restriction on distribution, and it does not travel with the report. The statements are required in the report itself, where whoever reads the findings will see them.

options.text: No — both are elements the report of factual findings is required to contain
options.why: SRS 4400 lists what the report of factual findings contains, and both sentences are on the list. One is the statement that had the auditor performed additional procedures, or an audit or a review, other matters might have come to light that would have been reported. The other is the statement that the report relates only to the elements specified and does not extend to the entity's financial statements taken as a whole. Between them they stop a reader treating a set of seven procedures as an examination of the company.
keywords: other matters might have come to light

citation.ref: the elements of the report of factual findings — the statement that additional procedures, an audit or a review might have brought other matters to light, and the statement that the report relates only to the elements specified

items.scenario: You have drafted the report of factual findings on seven procedures agreed with a bank and its borrower. It lists each procedure and what it showed. The engagement partner wants two sentences struck out as boilerplate — one saying that had you performed additional procedures, or an audit or a review, other matters might have come to light that would have been reported; the other saying that the report relates only to the elements specified and does not extend to the entity's financial statements taken as a whole.

items.stem: What is the position under SAE 3400?

options.text: The Standard does not apply to the examination of prospective financial information expressed in general or narrative terms, such as management discussion and analysis in an annual report; where it does apply, the examination need not be performed by the statutory auditor of the financial statements, and the level of assurance it provides is moderate
options.why: SAE 3400 does not apply to the examination of prospective financial information expressed in general or narrative terms, and the study material's own example of that is management discussion and analysis in an annual report. Where the Standard does apply, it need not be performed by the statutory auditor of the financial statements, and the level of assurance is moderate — a negative assurance statement on whether the assumptions provide a reasonable basis, with an opinion on preparation and presentation.

options.text: The Standard applies to any forward-looking statement in an annual report, and only the statutory auditor of the financial statements may perform the engagement
options.misconception: stretches the Standard over any words about the future and reserves the work to the statutory auditor, neither of which it does
options.why: Two separate errors. The scope is prospective financial information, not narrative outlook, and the Standard says so; and the examination is not reserved to the statutory auditor, who may or may not be the person engaged.

options.text: The Standard applies and would give reasonable assurance on the narrative, that being the highest level available for an assurance engagement
options.misconception: keeps a subject matter the Standard excludes and raises the level of assurance above the one it provides
options.why: The level of assurance under this Standard is moderate, not reasonable, because the evidence about future events is itself future-oriented and speculative. And a narrative outlook is outside its scope in any case.

options.text: No standard reaches any forward-looking information, so the firm may design and word the engagement as it wishes
options.misconception: reads one scope exclusion as an absence of any standard governing prospective financial information
options.why: The exclusion is narrow — information in general or narrative terms. Prospective financial information itself is squarely within SAE 3400, which sets the acceptance considerations, the examination procedures and the form of the report.

citation.ref: the scope of the Standard, which does not extend to prospective financial information expressed in general or narrative terms, and the moderate level of assurance provided

items.scenario: A company asks your firm to examine, under SAE 3400, the outlook section of its annual report — a page of management discussion and analysis in words, with no figures and no schedules. The company adds that the work must be done by its statutory auditor and that it wants the highest level of assurance available.

items.stem: What does SAE 3400 require on presentation and disclosure?

options.text: Neither is required so long as the arithmetic on the stated assumptions is correct and the assumptions themselves are listed
options.misconception: reduces presentation and disclosure to arithmetic, when the Standard sets out a list of disclosures the auditor assesses in addition
options.why: Correct arithmetic on the assumptions is what the opinion on proper preparation covers. The separate assessment is whether the presentation is informative and not misleading, and a forecast with no preparation date and an unannounced change of policy is neither.

options.text: The date is required, but the policy is not — a forecast is free to adopt whatever accounting policy management thinks best represents the future
options.misconception: lets the forecast float free of the historical financial statements it will inevitably be compared against
options.why: A reader compares a forecast with the last set of historical figures. Where the policy has moved between them, the reason for the change and its effect on the prospective financial information must be disclosed, or the comparison misleads without either document being wrong on its own.

options.text: The date as of which the prospective financial information was prepared must be disclosed, with management confirming that the assumptions are appropriate as of that date even though the underlying information was accumulated over a period of time; and where the accounting policy has changed from that disclosed in the most recent historical financial statements, the reason for the change and its effect on the prospective financial information must be adequately disclosed
options.why: Both are on the Standard's own checklist for presentation and disclosure. The date as of which the prospective financial information was prepared is disclosed, and management confirms that the assumptions are appropriate as of that date even though the underlying information may have been accumulated over a period of time — otherwise a reader cannot tell how stale the inputs are. And where the accounting policy has changed from that disclosed in the most recent historical financial statements, the reason for the change and its effect on the prospective financial information are adequately disclosed, because a forecast is read against the history it grew out of.
keywords: accumulated over a period of time

options.text: Both are matters for the date of the auditor's report on the forecast rather than for the notes to the prospective financial information
options.misconception: moves an entity disclosure into the auditor's report, where a reader of the notes alone would never find it
options.why: The date of the auditor's report says when his work finished. The date as of which the information was prepared, and the change in accounting policy, are disclosures in the notes to the prospective financial information, made by the entity that prepared it.

citation.ref: the assessment of presentation and disclosure — the date as of which the prospective financial information was prepared and management's confirmation of the assumptions as of that date, and the disclosure of a change in accounting policy from the most recent historical financial statements

items.scenario: A forecast you are examining carries its assumptions and its accounting policies in the notes. Two things are missing. The notes nowhere say as of what date the forecast was prepared, although the underlying information was accumulated over four months. And the company has moved to a different revenue recognition policy from the one disclosed in its most recent historical financial statements, with no mention of the change or of what it does to the forecast.

items.stem: What is the position under SAE 3402?

options.text: Without the service organisation's written assertion — that the description fairly presents the system, that the controls were suitably designed and, in a type 2 report, that they operated effectively throughout the specified period — the service auditor does not accept or continue the engagement unless law or regulation requires otherwise; and he must be independent of the service organisation but is not required to be independent of the user entities
options.why: The written assertion is what the report is built on. It says that, in all material respects and on suitable criteria, the description fairly presents the service organisation's system, that the controls were suitably designed, and, in a type 2 report, that they operated effectively throughout the specified period. Where the service organisation will not provide it, the service auditor does not accept or continue the engagement unless law or regulation requires otherwise. On independence, he must be independent of the service organisation, which is the party being reported on; he is not required to be independent of the user entities.

options.text: The assertion is needed only for a type 1 report, where there is no testing of operating effectiveness to stand behind the description
options.misconception: makes the assertion a substitute for testing, when it is required for both types and covers more ground in a type 2 report
options.why: Both types of report rest on a written assertion. In a type 2 report the assertion covers more, not less — the fair presentation of the description, the suitability of the design of the controls, and their operating effectiveness throughout the specified period.

options.text: The assertion may be replaced by a management representation letter taken at the end of the engagement
options.misconception: substitutes the closing representations for the assertion the whole report is addressed to, when the Standard requires both and they do different work
options.why: Written representations are requested as well, and they reaffirm the assertion rather than replace it. The assertion is the responsible party's public statement, which the service auditor's opinion then reports on; a letter to the auditor at the end is not that.

options.text: The assertion is optional where management cooperates fully in every other way, and independence is required of every user entity as well as of the service organisation
options.misconception: drops the one document the opinion attaches to and extends independence to fifty parties the service auditor does not report on
options.why: Cooperation is not the same as a signed statement of responsibility. And independence attaches to the party being reported on. A service auditor with fifty user entities to be independent of could not accept the engagement at all, which is not what the Standard contemplates.

citation.ref: the service organisation's written assertion and the consequence where it is not provided, and the service auditor's independence of the service organisation

items.scenario: A payroll processing organisation engages you to issue a type 2 report. Its management will prepare a description of the system and will answer whatever you ask, but declines to sign any written assertion, saying the description speaks for itself and a signature adds nothing. It also asks whether you have to be independent of the fifty user entities whose auditors will read the report.

items.stem: What does SAE 3420 actually require?

options.text: Audit the source financial statements afresh, since the practitioner cannot express any opinion resting on work another firm performed
options.misconception: turns an engagement on the compilation into a re-audit of the historical figures, which the Standard expressly says the practitioner has not performed
options.why: The opinion is on whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled on the basis of the applicable criteria. Re-auditing the source would answer a question nobody asked, and the report itself states that the practitioner has not audited or reviewed the historical financial information used.

options.text: Read nothing outside the pro forma tables and their notes, the subject matter of the engagement being the compilation alone
options.misconception: keeps the narrow subject matter and drops the requirement to read the document the information sits inside
options.why: The subject matter is narrow and the reading requirement is real. The practitioner reads the other information in the prospectus to identify material inconsistencies with the pro forma financial information, because a prospectus that contradicts its own illustration misleads whichever half the reader believes.

options.text: Obtain evidence about the appropriateness of the source from which the unadjusted financial information was extracted and determine whether the responsible party extracted it appropriately — not audit it again, the practitioner being neither responsible for reissuing any report on the historical financial information used nor having audited or reviewed it — and read the other information in the prospectus to identify material inconsistencies with the pro forma financial information
options.why: The engagement is on the compilation, and the steps run from identifying the source, through extracting the unadjusted financial information from it and making the pro forma adjustments, to presenting the information with its disclosures. The practitioner obtains evidence about the appropriateness of the source and about whether the responsible party appropriately extracted the unadjusted financial information from it. His report says that he is not responsible for reissuing any report on the historical financial information used and that he has not audited or reviewed that information. He also reads the other information in the prospectus to identify any material inconsistency with the pro forma financial information.

options.text: Decline the engagement wherever there is no audit or review report on the source, no evidence about the unadjusted information being obtainable in that case
options.misconception: treats an unaudited source as a bar, when the Standard has the practitioner perform procedures to satisfy himself that the source is appropriate
options.why: Where there is no audit or review report on the source, the practitioner performs procedures to be satisfied that the source is appropriate. Whether he can obtain a sufficient understanding of the entity is a question at acceptance, not an automatic refusal.

citation.ref: the procedures on the source of the unadjusted financial information and its extraction, the statement that the practitioner is not responsible for reissuing any report on the historical financial information used, and the reading of the other information in the prospectus

items.scenario: The unadjusted financial information in a prospectus was extracted from financial statements audited by another firm. Your manager proposes two things: to audit those financial statements again himself, because an opinion cannot rest on another firm's work; and to ignore the rest of the prospectus, because the practitioner's subject matter is the pro forma tables and nothing else.

items.stem: What must the principal auditor still do?

options.text: Nothing further — a component reporting on group policies produces figures already on the group's framework, so there is nothing left to check
options.misconception: takes the absence of conversion adjustments as the absence of any question about the policies the components were told to apply
options.why: The conversion adjustments have gone; the question they answered has not. It has moved upstream to the manual, and if the manual departs from the framework the parent must report under, every component departs with it and no adjustment anywhere reveals it.

options.text: Rely on the local auditors' reports on the manual-based statements without more, the manual being the parent's own document and therefore consistent with the parent's framework by construction
options.misconception: treats a document the parent wrote as proof that it complies with the framework the parent reports under
options.why: The local auditors report on compliance with the manual, not on whether the manual itself is right. Somebody has to test the manual against the accounting principles applicable to the parent, and the guidance puts that on the principal auditor.

options.text: Perform the procedures necessary to determine that the group accounting policies set out in the group accounting manual comply with the generally accepted accounting principles applicable to the parent
options.why: A component may prepare its financial statements on the parent's accounting policies as set out in the group accounting manual instead of being converted afterwards, and the local auditor may then audit and report on statements prepared on those group accounting policies. When that route is used, the principal auditor performs the procedures necessary to determine the compliance of the group accounting policies with the generally accepted accounting principles applicable to the parent — the manual being the parent's own document and not evidence of its own correctness.

options.text: Require the conversion route in any event, the group accounting manual approach not being open where a component's local generally accepted accounting principles differ from the parent's
options.misconception: closes an alternative the guidance expressly provides, and treats a difference in local principles as ruling it out
options.why: The manual route is offered precisely for components whose local principles differ. It works by having them report on group accounting policies from the start, rather than by correcting local figures afterwards.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: component financial statements prepared on the parent's accounting policies as set out in the group accounting manual, and the principal auditor's procedures on the compliance of those policies with the parent's generally accepted accounting principles

items.scenario: Rather than convert each foreign subsidiary's audited financial statements after the event, a listed parent issues a group accounting manual and requires every component to prepare its financial statements on the accounting policies it sets out. The local auditors audit those statements and report on them. The parent's auditor plans to take the component figures into the consolidation with no further work, since no conversion adjustments now arise.

items.stem: Which requirements of the internal audit engagement has the team failed?

options.text: Only the sampling, SIA 5 being the sole Standard on Internal Audit that governs fieldwork
options.misconception: picks one Standard out of a step that names five, leaving the source of the data, the analytics, the evidence, the documentation and the review unanswered
options.why: Sampling is one of them. Analytical procedures, audit evidence, documentation and the review of work before an interim report is issued each have their own Standard, and the failure here runs across all of them.

options.text: Information must so far as possible be obtained directly from the source with checks on its correctness and integrity; analytical procedures are performed under SIA 6, samples selected under SIA 5, evidence collected and stored under SIA 320, work papers documented under SIA 330, and an interim report issued only after proper review of the work performed under SIA 350
options.why: Step three of the engagement has the internal auditor obtain the required information and perform checks to ensure its correctness and integrity, obtaining it directly from the source so far as possible — the process owner's own spreadsheet is not that. Step four then names the Standards: analytical procedures to identify key trends and outliers under SIA 6, sampling where needed under SIA 5, evidence collected and stored under SIA 320, work papers documented under SIA 330, and interim reports issued only after proper review of the work performed under SIA 350.

options.text: None — the conduct of fieldwork is a matter for the internal auditor's professional judgement, the Standards on Internal Audit reaching only planning and reporting
options.misconception: confines the Standards on Internal Audit to the two ends of the engagement, when they name the procedures in the middle of it as well
options.why: Professional judgement decides how much testing is enough; it does not decide whether evidence is collected, whether work papers exist or whether an interim report is reviewed before it goes out. Each of those has a Standard on Internal Audit of its own.

options.text: Only the interim report, which should never have been issued at all — an internal auditor reports once, at the end of the assignment
options.misconception: bars interim reporting outright, when the requirement is that an interim report is issued only after proper review of the work performed
options.why: Interim reports are contemplated and are useful where a finding cannot wait. What the requirement adds is the review before issue, so that a report going to management rests on work somebody senior has looked at.

citation.ref: Ch. Internal Audit — gathering the required information directly from the source with checks on its correctness and integrity, and performing the audit checks under SIA 6, SIA 5, SIA 320, SIA 330 and SIA 350

items.scenario: The scope of an internal audit of the purchase-to-pay cycle has been approved by the audit committee and the Board and fieldwork has begun. The team takes its vendor master data from a spreadsheet the process owner maintains rather than from the enterprise resource planning system, runs no analytical work over the year's transactions, picks a handful of invoices by eye, and emails an interim report to the chief financial officer the same evening without anyone reviewing it.

items.stem: What is wrong with that plan?

options.text: Nothing — reading the working papers and signing them off is the review the Standard asks for, and the written agreements cover the rest
options.misconception: treats reading a conclusion as reviewing the work behind it, which is the distinction the Standard draws for staff who are not independent of the entity
options.why: A working paper records what its preparer says he did. Because the preparers here are the entity's own employees, the Standard asks the external auditor to go behind some of those papers to the underlying audit evidence itself rather than to accept the record of the work.

options.text: The internal auditors' work must be re-performed in full by the external auditor, precisely because they are not independent of the entity
options.misconception: converts checking back to the underlying evidence for some of the work into a duplicate of all of it, which would leave direct assistance no purpose
options.why: The requirement is that the review include checking back to the underlying audit evidence for some of the work performed, and that direction, supervision and review be sufficient for the external auditor to be satisfied that sufficient appropriate audit evidence supports the conclusions. Redoing everything is neither required nor what an assistance arrangement is for.

options.text: The review of work performed by internal auditors providing direct assistance must include the external auditor checking back to the underlying audit evidence for some of that work, the nature, timing and extent of direction, supervision and review recognising that the internal auditors are not independent of the entity; and the external auditor communicates to those charged with governance the nature and extent of the planned use of direct assistance
options.why: Two things are missing. The nature, timing and extent of direction, supervision and review must recognise that the internal auditors are not independent of the entity, and the review shall include the external auditor checking back to the underlying audit evidence for some of the work performed by them — reading their conclusions is not enough. And the external auditor communicates to those charged with governance the nature and extent of the planned use of direct assistance, so the people who oversee the audit know how much of it was done by the entity's own staff.
keywords: checking back to the underlying audit evidence

options.text: The communication to those charged with governance is required only where the internal auditors are used on a significant risk, and no significant risk is involved here
options.misconception: attaches a condition to the communication that the Standard does not impose, so that the arrangement most likely to go unmentioned is the routine one
options.why: The external auditor communicates the nature and extent of the planned use of direct assistance to those charged with governance, and the requirement is not limited to significant risks. Areas involving significant judgments and higher assessed risks are dealt with separately, by being closed to direct assistance altogether.

citation.ref: the direction, supervision and review of internal auditors providing direct assistance, including checking back to the underlying audit evidence for some of the work performed, and the communication to those charged with governance of the planned use of direct assistance

items.scenario: Two internal auditors are providing direct assistance on work that is not prohibited — vouching a sample of expense claims and tracing goods received notes to purchase orders. The written agreements are in place. The manager plans to read the working papers the two produce and sign them off, and to say nothing about the arrangement to the audit committee, on the view that how the firm staffs its own audit is an internal matter.

items.stem: What is the position?

options.text: Only the inventory point is a departure, attendance at physical inventory counting being an absolute requirement of SA 501 that admits of no condition
options.misconception: reads a conditional requirement as an absolute one by dropping the condition that opens it
options.why: The attendance requirement is conditional on inventory being material to the financial statements. A company with no inventory at all does not meet that condition, so the requirement is not relevant rather than departed from.

options.text: Both are departures, and the file must record how the alternative audit procedures performed achieve the aim of each requirement and the reasons for departing from it
options.misconception: treats a requirement whose condition never arose as a requirement the auditor abandoned, which would put a departure note in every file for every SA the entity does not engage
options.why: That documentation belongs to a genuine departure — a relevant requirement the auditor judged it necessary to depart from in exceptional circumstances. A condition that never arose is not a departure, and recording one would say in the file that a rule was broken when none applied.

options.text: Neither is a departure, because a departure from a requirement of an SA never needs documenting in any event
options.misconception: reaches the right conclusion through a rule that does not exist, and would leave a real departure invisible in the file
options.why: A genuine departure is documented, and documented twice over — how the alternative audit procedures performed achieve the aim of the requirement, and the reasons for the departure. The answer here is that no departure occurred, not that departures go unrecorded.

options.text: Neither is a departure — the auditor complies with each requirement of an SA unless the entire SA is not relevant, or the requirement is not relevant because it is conditional and the condition does not exist, and neither condition exists here, so there is nothing to document as a departure
options.why: The auditor complies with a requirement in all cases where it is relevant, and a requirement is not relevant in two situations — where the entire SA is not relevant, and where the requirement is conditional and the condition does not exist. Inventory attendance is conditional on inventory being material to the financial statements, and SA 610 is not relevant to an entity with no internal audit function. Nothing has been departed from, so nothing about a departure goes in the file.
keywords: conditional and the condition does not exist

citation.ref: compliance with the requirements of an SA, and the two situations in which a requirement is not relevant, read with the documentation of a departure at SA 230 para 12

items.scenario: You are completing the audit of a small trading company that carries no inventory of any kind and has no internal audit function. An article on documentation has left a junior worried. He asks whether the file must record a departure from SA 501's requirement to attend physical inventory counting, and from SA 610, together with the alternative procedures that achieved the aim of each.

items.stem: Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is the body that resulted from the merger of the SASB Foundation and the International Integrated Reporting Council
options.why: The Value Reporting Foundation is a non-profit organisation that was the result of the merger between the SASB Foundation and the International Integrated Reporting Council. It belongs to the consolidation phase of sustainability reporting, in which a crowded field of frameworks began combining rather than multiplying.

options.text: It is the framework created in 2015 by the Financial Stability Board for consistent climate-related disclosures
