citation.ref: the confirmations the parent's auditor obtains from component auditors as to independence and compliance with the code of ethics and the information required for the consolidation and disclosures, read with the Other Matter paragraph stating that his opinion on the amounts in respect of those components is based solely on the reports of the other auditors

items.scenario: Three of the group's components were audited by other auditors, and their reports have been furnished to you by the management of the holding company. Your manager has drafted the Other Matter paragraph giving the number of those components and the amounts they represent, and proposes to sign, saying that once the reports are on the file the opinion in respect of those amounts may be based solely on them.

items.stem: What route does the long form audit report actually take?

options.text: To the bank's management, whose acceptance of the comments closes the matter; the Board and the Reserve Bank see only the statutory audit report
options.misconception: treats management's acceptance as the end of the route, when the report is placed before the Board's committee and copied to the regulator
options.why: Management is one stop, not the last. The report is placed before the Audit Committee of the Board with the action taken or proposed, and a copy with the Board's views or directions goes to the Reserve Bank.

options.text: Straight from the branch to the Reserve Bank, the long form audit report being a return the regulator prescribes and the branch answers
options.misconception: sends the report to the regulator without the bank's own governance ever seeing it, which is the step the whole route exists for
options.why: What the Reserve Bank wants is not only the report but the bank's answer to it. That is why the report reaches the Audit Committee of the Board first and goes on with the Board's views or directions and a note about what will be done.

options.text: The statutory branch auditors submit their long form audit reports to the statutory central auditors; the consolidation is done at head office level and the long form audit report on the bank is submitted by the statutory central auditors to management; it is then placed before the Audit Committee of the Board, which indicates the action taken or proposed for rectification of the irregularities in it; and a copy of the report and the relative agenda note, together with the Board's views or directions, goes to the Reserve Bank within sixty days of its submission by the statutory auditors
options.why: The report climbs the bank before it leaves it. Branch auditors submit their long form audit reports to the statutory central auditors; the consolidation is done at head office level, and the long form audit report on the bank is submitted by the statutory central auditors to management. It is then placed before the Audit Committee of the Board after due examination, indicating the action taken or proposed to be taken for rectification of the irregularities mentioned in it. A copy of that report and the relative agenda note, together with the Board's views or directions, is submitted to the Reserve Bank within sixty days of the submission of the long form audit report by the statutory auditors.
keywords: consolidation is done at head office

options.text: To the statutory central auditors and no further — the consolidated long form audit report is a working paper supporting their own report on the bank
options.misconception: stops the route at the central auditors, so the report never reaches management, the Board or the regulator
options.why: The consolidated report is submitted by the statutory central auditors to management, placed before the Audit Committee of the Board, and copied to the Reserve Bank. A document with that journey is not a working paper.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — the long form audit report given by statutory branch auditors and statutory central auditors, its consolidation at head office, its placing before the Audit Committee of the Board, and the copy submitted to the Reserve Bank within sixty days

items.scenario: A branch auditor has finished his long form audit report. His assistant asks where it goes now. The branch manager says the branch will send it straight to the Reserve Bank, the long form audit report being a Reserve Bank requirement, and that once it is with the regulator nothing further has to happen inside the bank.

items.stem: Whose recommendations do these facts engage?

options.text: The Ghosh Committee's, but the auditor's only duty is to report the unreconciled balances as a weakness in the branch's own records, the long form audit report asking about implementation rather than about balances
options.misconception: separates the balances from the recommendation they answer, when the balances are the evidence that the recommendation is not implemented
options.why: The two are the same finding. What the long form audit report asks is whether the recommendation on prompt reconciliation has been implemented, and a year-old outstanding entry in the inter-branch account is how the auditor knows it has not.

options.text: The Jilani Committee's — reconciliation is an internal control matter, and the internal control system was that committee's subject
options.misconception: sorts by the words "internal control" rather than by what each committee actually dealt with
options.why: The Jilani Committee dealt with the internal control and inspection or audit system in banks — the machinery that checks: an independent inspection department, the inspection cycle, concurrent audit and the rectification of irregularities. Reconciliation of inter-branch, nostro and suspense accounts is anti-fraud housekeeping, and it is Ghosh's.

options.text: Neither — the two committees dealt with custody, staff rotation, inspection cycles and concurrent audit, and reconciliation appears in neither set of recommendations
options.misconception: remembers each committee by two or three headline items and treats the rest of its recommendations as not existing
options.why: Prompt reconciliation of inter-branch accounts, nostro accounts and suspense and sundry accounts is a Ghosh Committee recommendation. Learning a committee by its most quoted items leaves gaps in exactly the places an examiner reaches for.

options.text: The Ghosh Committee's — its recommendations on frauds and malpractices in banks include the prompt reconciliation of inter-branch accounts, of nostro accounts and of suspense and sundry accounts, and the auditor reports on the implementation of them in the long form audit report
options.why: The Ghosh Committee dealt with frauds and malpractices in banks, and its recommendations run wider than custody and staff. Prompt reconciliation of inter-branch accounts, of nostro accounts and of suspense and sundry accounts is among them, and the reason is exactly the one the manager denies: an account nobody reconciles is where a fraud can sit undisturbed, because the entry that would expose it is never matched against anything. A year-old outstanding entry is therefore a recommendation not implemented, and the auditor reports on the implementation of the recommendations in the long form audit report.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — the Ghosh Committee on frauds and malpractices in banks, including prompt reconciliation of inter-branch, nostro and suspense and sundry accounts, and the reporting on implementation in the long form audit report

items.scenario: At the branch you find entries outstanding for more than a year in the inter-branch account and in the suspense and sundry accounts, and nostro balances that have not been reconciled at all this year. The branch manager says these are back-office housekeeping matters with no bearing on frauds, and that the committee whose recommendations deal with frauds is concerned with custody, staff rotation and security stationery, none of which is in issue here.

items.stem: How are the two matters actually reported?

options.text: In the observations or qualifications paragraph of Form 3CA — the report states that the particulars given in Form 3CD are true and correct subject to the observations or qualifications set out there, so the particulars themselves are stated in Form 3CD and the auditor's reservation is carried in that paragraph of the report
options.why: The report and the annexure do different jobs and neither is left blank. Form 3CD carries the particulars, stated as best the auditor can state them. Form 3CA is the report that covers them, and it says that in the auditor's opinion and to the best of his information and according to the explanations given to him the particulars given in Form 3CD are true and correct, subject to the observations or qualifications set out in that paragraph. An unverified particular and a disputed value both go there, where a reader looking for the auditor's reservations will find them.

options.text: In a note to the financial statements, the tax auditor having no place of his own in which to record a reservation
options.misconception: puts the auditor's reservation into the assessee's own statements, where the assessee controls the wording
options.why: The auditor has a place of his own and it is in his report. A note in the financial statements is the assessee's statement about itself; the observations or qualifications paragraph is the auditor's statement about the particulars.

options.text: In the opinion paragraph of Form 3CB, since a reservation about the particulars is a reservation about the accounts from which they are drawn
options.misconception: reaches for the form used where no other audit exists, and turns a reservation on particulars into a reservation on the accounts
options.why: Form 3CB is used where the accounts are not audited under any other law, and this company's are. The tax auditor here reports in Form 3CA, and the reservation belongs in that report's observations or qualifications paragraph rather than in an opinion on accounts another auditor has already opined on.

options.text: Leave the two particulars blank in Form 3CD, a blank being the recognised way of showing that the auditor could not verify or could not agree
options.misconception: uses silence to carry a reservation, which leaves the reader unable to tell an omission from a disagreement
options.why: A blank says nothing about why it is blank. The form provides a paragraph for observations or qualifications precisely so that the auditor can state what he could not verify and what he does not agree with, in words.

citation.ref: Section 44AB with Rule 6G — Form 3CA and Form 3CB, and the observations or qualifications paragraph in which the auditor states his reservations on the particulars given in Form 3CD

items.scenario: In the tax audit of a company whose statutory audit under the Companies Act is complete, you cannot verify a particular required by one clause of Form 3CD, and you disagree with the assessee on the value stated under another. The article assistant proposes two fixes: leave both particulars blank in Form 3CD, and attach a covering letter to the return explaining why.

items.stem: How should clause 3(xviii) be answered?

options.text: Leave it blank — the reportable matter is the concerns raised by the outgoing auditor, and where he raised none there is nothing to report
options.misconception: collapses the clause's two limbs into the second one, so a clean resignation disappears from the report entirely
options.why: The two limbs are separate and the first stands on its own. Whether there has been any resignation is reported whatever the answer to the second limb, and "there was a resignation and no issues, objections or concerns were raised" is a materially different statement to a reader from silence.
keywords: whatever the answer to the second limb

options.text: It must be answered, not left blank — the clause is engaged by any resignation of the statutory auditors during the year whatever the reason for it, and the answer states that there was a resignation and that you took into consideration the issues, objections or concerns raised by the outgoing auditor, of which there were none
options.why: The clause asks two things in sequence, and the first is simply whether there has been any resignation of the statutory auditors during the year. Nothing in it turns on whether the exit was friendly: a retirement, a firm winding up and a dispute all answer that question the same way. Only then does the second limb ask whether the incoming auditor has taken into consideration the issues, objections or concerns raised by the outgoing auditors, and the honest answer where none were raised is to say so — which is a report, not a blank.
keywords: any resignation of the statutory auditors during the year

options.text: It is answered by the outgoing auditor rather than by you, since only he knows what he raised and why he left
options.misconception: hands a clause of the incoming auditor's own report to the auditor who has left office
options.why: CARO 2020 is an annexure to the report of the auditor now in office, and clause 3(xviii) is his statement about a predecessor. The outgoing auditor has his own and quite separate obligation, which is the statement he files under section 140(2); it is not this clause and it does not answer it.

options.text: Leave it blank — a resignation caused by a firm winding up is a cessation of office rather than a resignation, so the clause is not engaged
options.misconception: reads a reason into a clause that asks only whether a resignation happened
options.why: The clause contains no test of cause. The auditor left office by resigning, and the resignation is the fact reported; inventing a category of exits the clause does not reach leaves the reader with no information at all about a change the annexure exists to surface.

citation.ref: paragraph 3(xviii)

items.scenario: The previous statutory auditor resigned in September. The reason was that his firm's sole partner retired and the firm wound up; he wrote to you saying so, adding that he had raised nothing with the company and had no concerns of any kind, and you found none. You communicated with him in writing before accepting, and he confirmed he had no objection. Drafting the CARO annexure, the senior proposes to leave clause 3(xviii) blank on the ground that the clause is aimed at auditors who leave under a cloud, and nothing of that sort happened.

items.stem: What does the guidance require before that question arises?

options.text: The financial statements of all components should be audited or subjected to audit procedures in the context of a multi-location group audit, and those audits or procedures may be performed either by the auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements or by the components' auditors — so the first step is to perform procedures on the three yourself or arrange for them, and only what genuinely remains unaudited then goes into the evaluation of a possible modification
options.why: The reporting question is the second question, not the first. The financial statements of all components should be audited or subjected to audit procedures in the context of a multi-location group audit, and those audits and audit procedures can be performed by the auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements or by the components' auditors. Access to one shared system makes that practicable here. Only where components continue to remain unaudited does the auditor evaluate the qualitative and quantitative factors on the possible effect of the amounts remaining unaudited, and consider a modification under SA 705.
keywords: auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements
possible effect of the amounts remaining unaudited

options.text: Obtain the parent's internal audit reports on the three entities, which supply the audit the components never had
options.misconception: treats the internal audit function's reports as the audit or the audit procedures the guidance asks for, and skips the gates SA 610 sets before that work may be used at all
options.why: Internal audit work is not an audit of the component and does not become one by being filed. Whether any of it may be used at all is decided under SA 610 (Revised), on the function's objectivity, competence and systematic and disciplined approach, and even where it may be used the group auditor still performs his own procedures on the body of work.
keywords: not an audit of the component

options.text: Nothing comes before it — an unaudited component is an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and the only live question is qualified or disclaimer
options.misconception: treats the evidence gap as fixed and unclosable, when the auditor reporting on the group may close it himself
options.why: It becomes an inability only if it stays unaudited. Treating it as settled at the moment it is noticed skips the step where the group auditor performs the procedures, and turns a working problem into a reporting problem before anyone has tried to solve it.

options.text: Ask the parent to leave the three entities out of the consolidation until they have been audited, and disclose the exclusion in the notes
options.misconception: converts a shortage of audit evidence into an exemption from consolidation
options.why: Whether an entity is consolidated is decided by the applicable accounting standards on control, not by whether anyone has audited it. Leaving a controlled entity out because it is unaudited misstates the consolidated financial statements instead of auditing them.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Components not audited — the requirement that all components be audited or subjected to audit procedures in a multi-location group audit, and the evaluation of a possible modification under SA 705 for what remains unaudited

items.scenario: A group consolidates eleven components. Three of them are small overseas selling entities in jurisdictions where no statutory audit is required, and none has ever been audited. You are the auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements, the group's records are all kept on one system to which you have access, and the three entities together carry 7 per cent of consolidated revenue. The manager opens the file note with "the only question is whether we qualify or disclaim".

items.stem: What do SA 580 and the guidance on consolidated financial statements require here?

options.text: No acknowledgement of responsibility is needed from the parent at all, each component's management having already acknowledged responsibility for its own financial statements to its own auditor
options.misconception: adds up component-level acknowledgements and treats the sum as covering a set of statements no component's management ever prepared
options.why: Nobody but the parent's management prepares the consolidated financial statements — it identifies the components, obtains their information, makes the consolidation adjustments and harmonises the policies — so nobody but the parent's management can acknowledge responsibility for them.

options.text: The draft is acceptable, because the group chief financial officer's signature binds the parent's management and a signature is what a written representation is for
options.misconception: treats the identity of the signatory as curing what the letter actually says
options.why: Who signs does not change what is being represented. A correctly signed letter acknowledging responsibility for the wrong statements under the wrong framework, and silent on approval, is a letter that fixes management's position on matters the auditor did not ask about.

options.text: The draft is right on the framework — a group with components on different frameworks cannot represent about a single one — but wrong on approval, which the audit committee has given
options.misconception: lets the components' own frameworks decide what the parent represents about, and treats a committee's noting as the board's approval
options.why: The consolidated financial statements are prepared under one framework, the parent's, and a component on a different framework is dealt with by conversion before consolidation rather than by splitting the representation. Noting is not approving, and the representation the auditor seeks is that the statements have been approved.

options.text: The acknowledgement must be of the parent management's responsibility for a true and fair presentation of the consolidated financial statements in accordance with the financial reporting framework applicable to the parent; and the auditor must separately obtain evidence that the parent's management has approved those consolidated financial statements
options.why: Two things are wrong with the draft. The subject of the acknowledgement is the consolidated financial statements, not each component's own, and the framework named is the financial reporting framework applicable to the parent — which is the framework the consolidated statements are actually prepared under, whatever books a component keeps. And approval is a second and separate representation: the auditor obtains evidence that parent management has approved the consolidated financial statements, which noting by a committee is not.
keywords: financial reporting framework applicable to the parent

citation.ref: Ch. Group Audits — the parent management's acknowledgement of responsibility for a true and fair presentation of the consolidated financial statements in accordance with the financial reporting framework applicable to the parent, and its approval of those statements, read with SA 580

items.scenario: An Indian parent reporting under Ind AS consolidates a US subsidiary that keeps its own books under US GAAP. The draft representation letter has the parent's management acknowledging its responsibility "for a true and fair presentation of each component's financial statements in accordance with the framework applicable to that component". The letter is signed by the group chief financial officer. The consolidated financial statements have not yet been put to the parent's board; the audit committee has seen and noted them.

items.stem: How do these two facts stand?

options.text: Only the June meeting is a problem — the auditor's attendance in May was a matter for the chairperson's discretion, and a committee that shuts out its own chief financial officer cannot properly consider the accounts
options.misconception: inverts both limbs, making the statutory right discretionary and the discretionary exclusion unlawful
options.why: Discretion sits on the June side, not the May side. What the chairperson may decide is whom to invite beyond the statute; what he may not decide is whether the auditor is heard when the committee considers the auditor's report.
keywords: Discretion sits on the June side

options.text: The May meeting is the problem and the June one is not — Section 177(7) gives the auditor a right to be heard in the meeting when the committee considers his report, and a right does not wait on an invitation; a committee that occasionally meets without any executive of the listed entity present is doing something the listing framework expressly allows
options.why: The right to be heard under Section 177(7) is statutory, and the agenda item that triggers it — consideration of the auditor's report — is exactly what May was. A secretary's oversight cannot remove a right the Act confers. June is the opposite case: the listing framework has the committee invite a representative of the statutory auditor and other executives at its discretion, and expressly allows it occasionally to meet without any executive of the listed entity present, which is how a committee holds a conversation about management.
keywords: without any executive of the listed entity present

options.text: Both are problems — the auditor attends only when invited, so the oversight cost him nothing he was entitled to, and the committee may never exclude the finance function from its own deliberations
options.misconception: turns a statutory right into a courtesy that depends on somebody remembering, and turns a discretion to exclude executives into a prohibition on doing so
options.why: The two halves fail in opposite directions. Section 177(7) confers the right directly, so the oversight cost the auditor exactly what the section gives him; and excluding executives is a power the framework grants the committee, not a breach of it.

options.text: Neither is a problem, and in any case the auditor's right to be heard runs to every meeting of the audit committee, so missing one changes nothing
options.misconception: widens a right the section ties to the consideration of the auditor's report into a general right of attendance, and then uses the width to say the breach did not matter
options.why: The section ties the right to the meetings in which the committee considers the auditor's report; it is not a standing seat at every meeting. Because the right is tied to that agenda item, missing the one meeting that carried it is the whole of the breach rather than a small part of a larger entitlement.

citation.ref: Section 177(7), read with Regulation 18 and the audit committee's discretion to invite a representative of the statutory auditor and its power occasionally to meet without any executive of the listed entity present

items.scenario: A listed company's audit committee met in May to consider the statutory auditor's report. No written invitation was sent to the auditor and nobody from the firm attended; the secretary says an invitation was simply overlooked. At a later meeting in June the committee asked the chief financial officer and the head of internal audit to leave, and then sat and deliberated with only its own members present.

items.stem: Is the partner right?

options.text: No, but only because of the regulator's new report — growth in the business and a misunderstanding of scope are matters for the audit strategy rather than for the terms
options.misconception: sorts two of the standard's own named circumstances out of the terms and into planning
options.why: All three are on the same list and none of them is demoted to the strategy. Growth changes what is being audited and a misunderstanding changes what the client believes it is buying; the standard names both alongside the new reporting requirement precisely because each can make the existing terms describe something other than the engagement being performed.

options.text: No — a significant change in the nature or size of the entity's business, a change in other reporting requirements, and any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit are each among the circumstances SA 210 names, and all three are present
options.why: The standard's list is wider than ownership, management and the framework. It also names a significant change in the nature or size of the entity's business, which one plant to nine plainly is; a change in other reporting requirements, which the sectoral regulator's new report is; and any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit, which a request to confirm that the audit will detect any fraud by any employee is in one sentence.
keywords: nature or size of the entity's business

options.text: Yes on the facts, but the chief financial officer's letter should be answered in conversation, since a misunderstanding by one officer is not a change in the engagement
options.misconception: treats a stated misunderstanding of what the audit is for as a personal matter rather than as one of the circumstances the standard names
options.why: A conversation is worth having and is not the answer the standard gives. Any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit is itself a listed circumstance, and the point of revising or reconfirming the terms is that the understanding ends up in writing rather than in somebody's memory of a call.

options.text: Yes — the circumstances the standard names are a change of senior management, a change in ownership and a change in the financial reporting framework, and none of the three has happened
options.misconception: treats the three best-known entries on the list as the whole of it
options.why: Those three are on the list and are not the list. The standard also reaches a change in the nature or size of the business, a change in legal or regulatory requirements, a change in other reporting requirements, revised or special terms, and any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit.

citation.ref: para 13, read with the circumstances that may make it appropriate to revise the terms of the audit engagement or to remind the entity of the existing terms

items.scenario: Seventh year of the same audit. The owners are unchanged, the directors are unchanged and the financial reporting framework is unchanged. In the year the company went from one plant to nine and began operating in two new states; a sectoral regulator now requires an additional report from the statutory auditor each year; and the newly appointed chief financial officer has written asking you to confirm "that your audit will detect any fraud committed by any employee". The partner says none of the circumstances SA 210 lists has occurred.

items.stem: What does SA 300 say about who does the planning?

options.text: Nothing — planning is a manager's task, and the engagement partner discharges his responsibility by reviewing and approving the completed strategy and plan
options.misconception: satisfies a requirement to be involved in making the plan with an act performed after it is made
options.why: Approval at the end and involvement throughout are different things, and the standard asks for the second. A partner reading a finished plan can see what it says; he cannot see the alternatives that were never written down, which is where his experience would have been worth most.

options.text: Only the team discussion is a problem, and it is SA 315's requirement rather than SA 300's, so nothing in SA 300 has been breached
options.misconception: files the discussion under one standard alone, when SA 300 names participation in it as part of the involvement it requires
options.why: SA 315 has its own discussion requirement and that does not empty SA 300's. SA 300 names planning and participating in the discussion among engagement team members as part of what the engagement partner and other key members are to be involved in, so the seniors holding it alone fails both standards rather than only one.
keywords: planning and participating in the discussion
engagement partner and other key members

options.text: The engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team shall be involved in planning the audit, including participating in the discussion among engagement team members — their experience is what the involvement is for, and reviewing a finished plan is not being involved in making it
options.why: SA 300 states it as a requirement, not a preference: the engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team shall be involved in planning the audit, including planning and participating in the discussion among engagement team members. The reason the standard gives is that their involvement draws on their experience and insight, which enhances the effectiveness and efficiency of the planning process — and experience brought to a finished document can only approve or reject it, never shape where the work was aimed.
keywords: engagement partner and other key members

options.text: The engagement partner must perform the planning himself, since planning is the exercise of the judgement the opinion rests on and cannot be delegated
options.misconception: reads a requirement to be involved as a bar on anyone else doing the work
options.why: The standard requires involvement, not sole authorship, and it expressly contemplates other key members of the engagement team being involved alongside the partner. A manager and seniors drafting is normal; the partner absent from the drafting is what fails.
keywords: other key members of the engagement team

citation.ref: the requirement that the engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team be involved in planning the audit, including planning and participating in the discussion among engagement team members

items.scenario: On a large audit the manager and two seniors build the overall audit strategy and the audit plan over a fortnight. The engagement partner is committed to another client throughout and sees the plan for the first time when it is finished, reviewing it in an hour and signing it off. The discussion among the team about where the financial statements are most likely to be misstated is held by the two seniors between themselves.

items.stem: May the engagement partner date the auditor's report today?

options.text: No — before the auditor's report is dated the engagement partner shall determine that sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained to support the conclusions reached and for the auditor's report to be issued, and a completed engagement quality review does not supply evidence that has not yet arrived
options.why: SA 220 (Revised) sets two things before the date and the manager has counted only one. The engagement partner shall determine that sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained to support the conclusions reached and for the auditor's report to be issued; and, separately, where an engagement quality review is required, the report shall not be dated until he is notified that the review is complete. A reviewer confirms that the judgements made were appropriate on what was on the file; he cannot confirm a confirmation that has not come back.
keywords: sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained
for the auditor's report to be issued

options.text: No, and the answer is to date the report today with an Other Matter paragraph recording that two areas were still open at the date of signature
options.misconception: uses a paragraph in the report to disclose a shortage of evidence instead of obtaining the evidence
options.why: Describing a hole is not filling it. An Other Matter paragraph communicates something relevant to users' understanding of the audit; it cannot sit under an unmodified opinion that the partner is not yet in a position to support.

options.text: Yes, provided the report is dual dated next week when the confirmation and the actuary's letter arrive
options.misconception: borrows a mechanism built for facts arising after the report date and uses it to date a report before the evidence exists
options.why: Dual dating exists for a subsequent event amended after the original report was properly issued on complete evidence. It is not a way of issuing a report on incomplete evidence and finishing the audit afterwards; the original date would still be asserting that the evidence supporting the opinion was there when it was not.

options.text: Yes — the engagement quality review is complete and the manager's review is complete, which are the two requirements that gate the date
options.misconception: counts two reviews as the two gates, when one of the gates is about evidence rather than about review
options.why: The manager's review is not a gate on the date at all, and putting it in the pair hides the one that is missing. What gates the date alongside the engagement quality review is the engagement partner's own determination that sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained.
keywords: not a gate on the date
sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained

citation.ref: the engagement partner's determination, before the auditor's report is dated, that sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained to support the conclusions reached and for the report to be issued, read with the requirement not to date the report until he is notified that a required engagement quality review is complete

items.scenario: The engagement quality reviewer has finished and the engagement partner has been notified of it in writing. The manager has completed his review of every working paper. Two areas remain marked in the file as "conclusion pending — awaiting the confirmation from the counterparty and the actuary's final letter, both expected next week", one being a related party transaction and the other a warranty provision. The client wants the report dated today for a lender's deadline, and the manager says the two gates on the date have both been passed.

items.stem: How does SA 265 have you decide what goes to those charged with governance?

options.text: The cash finding goes up, but the two purchase-cycle findings stay out, neither being significant on its own
options.misconception: assesses deficiencies one at a time when the standard asks for them to be assessed individually or in combination
options.why: Assessing them one at a time is exactly what the standard rules out: deficiencies are judged individually or in combination. Two harmless findings that together let a buyer raise and approve his own order are a combination, and the combination is what is judged.

options.text: Deficiencies are assessed individually or in combination, on the likelihood that a misstatement could occur and on its potential magnitude — so a significant deficiency can exist even though no misstatement was identified during the audit, and the susceptibility to loss of an asset is one of the factors
options.why: The significance of a deficiency, or of a combination of deficiencies, depends not only on whether a misstatement has actually occurred but also on the likelihood that a misstatement could occur and the potential magnitude of it. Significant deficiencies may therefore exist even though the auditor has not identified misstatements during the audit, and the susceptibility to loss of an asset is a factor in deciding. That reaches the cash finding directly, and it reaches the two purchase-cycle findings because the standard has them weighed individually or in combination.
keywords: likelihood that a misstatement could occur

options.text: Communicate nothing to those charged with governance — no misstatement was found, so no deficiency has been shown to be significant
options.misconception: makes an actual misstatement the test of significance, when the standard tests the likelihood of one and its potential size
options.why: A control that has not yet failed is not a control that works. Significant deficiencies may exist even though the auditor has not identified misstatements during the audit, which is the whole reason the test is written around likelihood and potential magnitude rather than around outcomes.

options.text: All three go up, since any deficiency touching cash or purchases is significant by nature and the late report is a deficiency too
options.misconception: replaces a judgement about likelihood and magnitude with a list of sensitive cycles, so a two-day reporting delay travels to the board
options.why: The cycle a deficiency sits in is not the test. Susceptibility to loss of an asset is one factor among several, and a report arriving two days late carries neither a real likelihood of misstatement nor a potential magnitude that would merit the attention of those charged with governance.

citation.ref: the determination of whether identified deficiencies, individually or in combination, constitute significant deficiencies, read with the significance of a deficiency depending on the likelihood and potential magnitude of misstatement and on susceptibility to loss of an asset

items.scenario: Three findings sit on the internal control memorandum. One person holds the cash and the cheque books and also performs the bank reconciliation; your testing found no misstatement in the cash cycle all year. In the purchase cycle, two smaller findings — a stale approval matrix and an unrestricted "urgent order" route — are each harmless alone, but together let one buyer raise and approve his own purchase order. A third finding is a monthly report that reaches the accounts team two days late. The senior proposes to communicate nothing to those charged with governance because no misstatement was found anywhere.

items.stem: What is wrong with that proposal?

options.text: The route the manager has chosen is not open to him — substantive procedures combined with tests of controls for the intervening period is available where the auditor relies on those controls, and none were tested here, so the remaining period has to be covered by further substantive procedures that themselves provide a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end
options.why: SA 330 offers two routes across the gap, and they are not interchangeable on any facts. The first combines substantive procedures with tests of controls for the intervening period, which presupposes controls the auditor has tested and is relying on; a team that tested none all year cannot start relying on them for four months at the end. That leaves the second — further substantive procedures only, where the auditor determines that is sufficient — and whichever route is taken it must provide a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end.
keywords: tests of controls for the intervening period
reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions

options.text: Nothing, provided the tests of controls cover the whole of December to March rather than a sample of months within it
options.misconception: fixes the coverage of a procedure that cannot supply the evidence needed in the first place
options.why: Full coverage of the wrong evidence is still the wrong evidence. Controls that were never tested for design, implementation or operation over the first eight months give the auditor no basis for concluding they operated in the last four, however completely the last four are examined.

options.text: Nothing — the standard names two routes and leaves the choice between them to the auditor's judgement
options.misconception: reads two permitted routes as two routes always available, when the first depends on controls the auditor has actually tested
options.why: There is a choice, and it is a choice between routes that are open. The first route is built on tests of controls for the intervening period, so it exists only where there are controls being relied on; where the approach was wholly substantive from the start, the judgement is about the extent of the further substantive procedures, not about which route to take.
keywords: tests of controls for the intervening period

options.text: Nothing about the procedures, but a written representation from management that no material inventory movement occurred between 30 November and 31 March must be obtained as well
options.misconception: adds a representation to close a gap that only audit procedures can close
options.why: A written representation is audit evidence and is not sufficient appropriate audit evidence on its own about any of the matters it deals with. It cannot be the reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end, and obtaining one does not make the chosen route available.
keywords: reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions

citation.ref: para 22 — covering the remaining period by substantive procedures combined with tests of controls for the intervening period, or by further substantive procedures alone, either providing a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end

items.scenario: Inventory was substantively tested at 30 November for a 31 March year end and the results were clean. The team assessed a wholly substantive approach for inventory at the planning stage and tested no controls over inventory movements at any point in the year. The manager now proposes to cover December to March by performing tests of controls over goods received and goods despatched for that intervening period, and to do no further substantive work on inventory.

items.stem: What follows for the audit?

options.text: The control objective the review was necessary to achieve cannot be treated as achieved for this client, so the type 2 report supports no reliance on the accuracy of billed amounts, and the evidence over that has to come from your own substantive procedures
options.why: A complementary user entity control is one the service organisation assumed, in designing its service, that user entities would implement, and it is named in the description because the stated control objective cannot be achieved without it. The service auditor never tests it, and his unmodified opinion says nothing about it. Where the user entity has not implemented it, the chain the control objective depends on is broken at the client's end, and the auditor obtains the evidence he needs by his own substantive procedures instead.

options.text: Nothing follows for reliance — the report is unmodified and covers the whole year, so the unimplemented review is a matter for the management letter
options.misconception: reads an unmodified service auditor's opinion as covering a control that was never inside its scope
options.why: The opinion covers the provider's controls and only those. The description names the review precisely because the provider does not perform it, so an unmodified opinion is exactly what you would expect to see whether or not the client ever did.

options.text: Report the failure to the provider, which will extend its own controls to cover the rate table review from next month
options.misconception: hands back to the service organisation a control it deliberately left with the user entity, and treats a future fix as evidence about the year under audit
options.why: The provider designed its service on the footing that somebody at the client would look at the rate table, which is why it is a complementary user entity control rather than one of the provider's own. And a control extended next month says nothing about the twelve months being audited.

options.text: The service auditor's opinion must be treated as modified, a complementary user entity control that was not implemented having invalidated his report
options.misconception: makes a failure at the user entity a defect in a report about a different entity
options.why: Nothing about the provider's system has changed. The report remains a correct statement about the provider; what has failed is at the client, and it is the user auditor's reliance on the report, not the report itself, that the failure destroys.

citation.ref: para 8(a) and the requirement, when a type 1 or type 2 report is used, to determine whether the complementary user entity controls identified by the service organisation are relevant and to test them at the user entity

items.scenario: Your client's billing runs on a cloud provider. The type 2 report covers the full year and carries an unmodified service auditor's opinion. Its description of the system names one complementary user entity control: the user entity must review and approve the monthly rate table before it is loaded, and the report says this control is necessary to achieve the control objective on the accuracy of billed amounts. You establish that the client's finance head signs the loading form each month without opening the rate table, and has done so all year.

items.stem: What does SA 580 require of you?

options.text: Disclaim the opinion, because SA 580 answers any refused written representation with a disclaimer
options.misconception: applies the rule for the two responsibilities representations to every representation in the letter
options.why: The disclaimer is not the standard's answer to refusal in general. It is prescribed where management does not provide the representations about its own responsibilities, or where the auditor concludes that doubt about management's integrity makes those unreliable. Everything else runs through the graded response, which may still end at a disclaimer but only after the evaluation.

options.text: Discuss the matter with management; re-evaluate the integrity of management and the effect that has on the reliability of representations, oral and written, and of audit evidence in general; and take appropriate actions, including determining the possible effect on the opinion — the automatic disclaimer is prescribed for the two representations about management's own responsibilities, and this is not one of them
options.why: Where a requested written representation is not provided, SA 580 sets a sequence rather than an outcome. The auditor discusses the matter with management, re-evaluates the integrity of management and the effect that has on the reliability of representations and of audit evidence in general, and takes appropriate actions including determining the possible effect on the opinion. The disclaimer the standard prescribes without that grading is for the two representations about management's responsibilities, both of which were given here; what was refused is a specific representation, and a refusal on it still contaminates the rest, which is why the re-evaluation reaches audit evidence in general rather than only this paragraph.

options.text: Nothing follows — a written representation is not sufficient appropriate audit evidence about any matter it deals with, so an absent one leaves the evidence exactly where it was
options.misconception: reasons from what a representation is worth as evidence to what its refusal is worth as information
options.why: It is true that a representation is never sufficient on its own. But a refusal is not the same event as an absence: management has been asked to confirm something and has declined, and SA 580 treats that as information about management, reaching the reliability of the representations it did give and of audit evidence in general.
keywords: refusal is not the same event as an absence

options.text: Accept an oral confirmation from the group legal head in place of the struck-out paragraph and complete the file note
options.misconception: substitutes an oral statement from a third officer for a written representation management has deliberately declined to give
options.why: The standard requires the representation in writing from management, and the significant fact here is the deliberate deletion, not the absence of words on the subject. Taking a spoken assurance from someone else records agreement that management has just refused to give.

citation.ref: para 19 — the actions where requested written representations are not provided — read with para 20, which prescribes a disclaimer for the representations about management's responsibilities

items.scenario: Management signs the representation letter, including both representations about its own responsibilities — that it has fulfilled its responsibility for the preparation of the financial statements, and that it has provided you with all relevant information and access agreed in the terms of the engagement. It strikes out one other paragraph: the one confirming that it has disclosed to you all known instances of non-compliance with laws and regulations. The finance director says the group legal head would not put his name to that sentence and offers no further explanation.

items.stem: Is that split defensible under SA 620?

options.text: Yes — the four matters must be agreed with both experts, but the standard requires the agreement to be in writing when appropriate, and access to confidential information, an expert not previously used, the extent and significance of the work and its complexity are the factors that make writing appropriate; all of them point at the engineer and none at the actuary
options.why: The agreement itself is not optional for either. The same four matters are agreed with every auditor's expert: the nature, scope and objectives of the work, the respective roles and responsibilities, the nature, timing and extent of communication including the form of any report, and the need to observe confidentiality requirements. What varies is the form. The standard asks for it in writing when appropriate, and the factors it names are whether the expert will have access to confidential entity information, whether the auditor has not previously used work performed by that expert, the greater extent and significance of the work in the context of the audit, and how complex the matter is.

options.text: No — every agreement with an auditor's expert must be in writing, without exception
options.misconception: hardens a standard that says "when appropriate" into an unqualified rule
options.why: The standard's words are that the auditor shall agree, in writing when appropriate, on the four matters. Reading the qualification out of it turns a judgement the standard asks the auditor to make into a formality, and gives no way to tell the engineer's engagement apart from the actuary's.

options.text: Yes, but for a different reason — writing is required for an external expert and never for an internal one, and that line settles it by itself
options.misconception: promotes one of several factors into the whole test, so a first-time internal expert on a highly complex matter would need nothing in writing
options.why: Whether the expert is internal or external is one factor among several, and the others can carry the answer on their own. An internal expert given confidential information for a large and complex matter he has never worked on before is a case where writing would be appropriate, and a rule drawn on the internal-external line alone would miss it.

options.text: No — an internal expert is a member of the firm and needs no agreement at all, the four matters being covered by the firm's own quality management system
options.misconception: uses membership of the firm to remove the agreement rather than to inform the judgement about its form
options.why: Membership of the firm bears on whether writing is appropriate, not on whether there is anything to agree. Somebody still has to fix what the actuary is valuing, on what basis, by when and in what form, and a system of quality management does not answer any of those for a particular engagement.

citation.ref: para 11 — the four matters agreed with the auditor's expert, in writing when appropriate — read with the factors bearing on whether writing is appropriate

items.scenario: Two experts are used on one audit. The first is an actuary who is a partner in your own firm's actuarial team, has worked on this client for six years, and is doing a routine review of a small gratuity valuation. The second is an external petroleum engineer the firm has never used before, engaged on a large and technically complex reserves estimate, and given the client's confidential reserve data to do it. The manager proposes a written agreement with the engineer and a short file note recording the arrangement with the actuary.

items.stem: Which of these fall within SA 720?

options.text: Only the bound volume — other information has to be published together with the financial statements it accompanies, so a separately issued booklet is outside the standard
options.misconception: makes physical packaging the test, when the definition turns on purpose and allows a combination of documents
options.why: A combination of documents that serve the same purpose is an annual report, and the separate booklet is one of them. Deciding scope by what is between the same covers would let an entity move its most optimistic commentary out of the volume and out of the audit's reach at once.

options.text: All four — everything the company published about the year's results reaches owners and carries the same figures, so all of it is other information
options.misconception: treats subject matter and audience as the test, when the standard excludes two categories by name
options.why: Overlapping figures do not make a document part of the annual report. SA 720 excludes preliminary announcements of financial information and securities offering documents, including prospectuses, and reporting on the second of those has its own regime rather than none.

options.text: The bound volume and the management discussion and analysis booklet — an annual report may be a single document or a combination of documents that serve the same purpose — while the standard does not apply to preliminary announcements of financial information or to securities offering documents, including prospectuses
options.why: The definition does the work. An annual report is a document, or combination of documents, prepared typically on an annual basis by management or those charged with governance in accordance with law, regulation or custom, whose purpose is to provide owners with information on the entity's operations and its financial results and position. A booklet issued the same day and described as part of the year's reporting is inside that; binding is not the test. And SA 720 says in terms that it does not apply to preliminary announcements of financial information, or to securities offering documents including prospectuses.

options.text: The bound volume and the prospectus — a prospectus reproduces the audited financial statements and goes to investors, which is what other information is for
options.misconception: brings in by reasoning the one document the standard excludes by name
options.why: Reproducing the financial statements is not the test either, and here the standard leaves no room to reason: it does not apply to securities offering documents, including prospectuses. What a practitioner does about the other information in a prospectus is a separate engagement under its own standard.

citation.ref: the definition of an annual report as a document or combination of documents, and the exclusion of preliminary announcements of financial information and securities offering documents including prospectuses from the scope of the SA

items.scenario: A listed company issues four documents around its results. A bound volume carrying the directors' report, the corporate governance report and the audited financial statements. A separate management discussion and analysis booklet, posted to shareholders on the same day and described in the bound volume as forming part of the year's reporting. An unaudited preliminary announcement of the year's results, released to the exchanges three weeks before your report is signed. And a prospectus for a bond issue two months later, which reproduces the audited financial statements. The finance head tells you only the bound volume is the annual report.

items.stem: What does SAE 3402 require?

options.text: Modify the opinion for the description and disclaim separately on the access control, so the report carries a modification and a disclaimer side by side
options.misconception: splits one opinion into two conclusions on the same subject matter, when the standard answers multiple faults with one modified opinion carrying all the reasons
options.why: There is one opinion on the description, the design and, in a type 2 report, the operating effectiveness. Where more than one thing is wrong, the answer is a single modified opinion whose report contains a clear description of all the reasons for the modification, not two conclusions that a reader has to reconcile.
keywords: all the reasons for the modification

options.text: Both are grounds for modification — the description does not fairly present the system, and you are unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence — and the report shall contain a clear description of all the reasons for the modification, not the one that is easiest to state
options.why: The service auditor modifies the opinion where the description does not fairly present the system as designed and implemented, where the controls were not suitably designed, where in a type 2 report the controls tested did not operate effectively, or where he is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence. Two of the four are engaged here. And the standard settles the drafting as well as the grounds: the report shall contain a clear description of all the reasons for the modification, so a user auditor reading it knows everything that is wrong and not only the part that was convenient to write.
keywords: does not fairly present the system
unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence
all the reasons for the modification

options.text: Neither is a ground — in a type 2 report the opinion is modified only where the controls tested did not operate effectively, and both problems are about something else
options.misconception: keeps one of the four grounds and discards the other three
options.why: Operating effectiveness is one ground of four. Fair presentation of the description, suitability of the design and an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence each stand alongside it, and an inability to obtain evidence is precisely what four months of purged logs leaves.
keywords: inability to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence

options.text: Modify for the purged logs alone — a description that management has undertaken to correct next year is a matter for a letter to the service organisation
options.misconception: treats a promise about next year's document as curing this year's, and drops a named ground for modification out of the report
options.why: The report describes the system for the period reported on, and for that period the description asserts a control nobody performs. A user auditor relying on the description would be relying on a reconciliation that does not exist, which is why "does not fairly present the system" is a ground in its own right.
keywords: does not fairly present the system

citation.ref: the grounds on which the service auditor's opinion is modified — a description that does not fairly present the system, controls not suitably designed, controls tested that did not operate effectively in a type 2 report, and an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence — with the requirement that the report contain a description of all the reasons for the modification

items.scenario: You are the service auditor completing a type 2 report. Two problems stand. The service organisation's description of its system says a daily reconciliation between the ledger and the settlement file is performed, and it is not performed at all. Separately, you could not test one access control because the system logs for four months were purged under a retention setting nobody had reviewed. You propose to modify the opinion naming only the purged logs, on the ground that the description point is minor and management has undertaken to correct the wording next year.

items.stem: What is missing from the report under SAE 3400?

options.text: Three elements — a statement that management is responsible for the prospective financial information including the underlying assumptions; where applicable, a reference to the purpose and/or restricted distribution of the prospective financial information; and a statement that the examination procedures included examination, on a test basis, of evidence supporting the assumptions, amounts and other disclosures
options.why: The three gaps map onto three named elements of the report. A statement that management is responsible for the prospective financial information including the underlying assumptions answers who prepared it, and matters most on a document about the future, where a reader may otherwise take the numbers for the auditor's. A reference to the purpose and/or restricted distribution answers what a forecast built for one lender's covenant is doing in anyone else's hands. And a statement that the examination procedures included examination, on a test basis, of evidence supporting the assumptions, amounts and other disclosures tells the reader what the work was.
keywords: management is responsible for the prospective financial information

options.text: A statement that the auditor is responsible for the assumptions, since it is the assumptions he gave negative assurance on
options.misconception: reads assurance given on assumptions as responsibility taken for them
options.why: Giving negative assurance on whether the assumptions provide a reasonable basis is a statement about somebody else's assumptions. Management is responsible for the prospective financial information including the underlying assumptions, and a report saying otherwise would put the auditor behind a forecast of events that may never occur.

options.text: Nothing — those three belong in the engagement letter, and the report is complete once it carries the negative assurance, the opinion and the caveat
options.misconception: moves three named elements of the report into the engagement letter, leaving the report silent on responsibility, purpose and work performed
options.why: The engagement letter records the arrangement between two parties; the report speaks to whoever reads it. Responsibility for the information, the purpose it was prepared for and the nature of the examination are elements of the report itself, and a reader who never sees the engagement letter would otherwise learn none of them.

options.text: Only the reference to restricted distribution — responsibility and the nature of the procedures are implied by the reference to the applicable standard
options.misconception: lets a citation of the standard stand in for the statements the standard says the report shall contain
options.why: Naming a standard tells a reader which rules were followed, not what the auditor did or who made the forecast. The standard sets out the elements a report shall contain precisely so that a reader does not have to go and look them up, and the statements on responsibility and on the test-basis examination are two of them.

citation.ref: the elements of a report on an examination of prospective financial information — including the statement that management is responsible for the information and the underlying assumptions, the reference where applicable to the purpose and/or restricted distribution, and the statement that the procedures included examination on a test basis of evidence supporting the assumptions, amounts and other disclosures

items.scenario: You have examined a three-year forecast prepared solely for one lender under a covenant in its loan agreement, and you are satisfied with the assumptions and the preparation. The draft report carries a title, an addressee, an identification of the forecast, a reference to the applicable standard, the negative assurance sentence on the assumptions, the opinion on preparation and presentation, a caveat about achievability, the date, the place of signature and the signature. It says nothing about who prepared the forecast, nothing about the fact that it was prepared only for the lender, and nothing about what your examination consisted of.

items.stem: Which file breaches the standard's effective date of application?

options.text: Neither file — both periods end before the standard became mandatory, which is for periods ending on or after 31 March 2026
options.misconception: moves the mandatory date two years later than the standard sets it
options.why: The mandatory stage begins with assurance reports covering periods ending on or after 31 March 2024. The year ended 31 March 2025 is inside it, and a report drafted without reference to the standard for that period is a breach.

options.text: File B only — SSAE 3000 applied on a voluntary basis to assurance reports covering periods ending on 31 March 2023 and on a mandatory basis to assurance reports covering periods ending on or after 31 March 2024
options.why: The effective date is written in two stages. On a voluntary basis it applied to assurance reports covering periods ending on 31 March 2023, so File A departed from a standard nobody was yet obliged to follow. On a mandatory basis it applied to assurance reports covering periods ending on or after 31 March 2024, which catches a report on the year ended 31 March 2025 squarely.

options.text: Both files — the standard bound every assurance engagement on sustainability information from the day ICAI issued it
options.misconception: treats the date of issue as the date of application, ignoring a two-stage effective date the standard states in terms
options.why: A standard's effective date is a separate question from when it was issued, and this one was deliberately phased. The voluntary stage for periods ending on 31 March 2023 exists so that firms could adopt it early without a breach hanging over anyone who did not.

options.text: Neither file — SSAE 3000 binds only assurance engagements for the top 1000 listed companies by market capitalisation, and this company is outside that class
options.misconception: imports a reporting threshold that applies to entities into a standard that applies to the engagement
options.why: The top 1000 listed companies by market capitalisation is the class on which a reporting obligation was placed; it is not a limit on an assurance standard. SSAE 3000 applies to assurance engagements on sustainability information, and what decides its application is the period the report covers.

citation.ref: Effective date of application — voluntary basis for assurance reports covering periods ending on 31 March 2023, mandatory basis for assurance reports covering periods ending on or after 31 March 2024

items.scenario: A firm's quality review picks up two files. File A is a limited assurance report on a listed company's sustainability information for the year ended 31 March 2023; it makes no reference to SSAE 3000 and follows a format of the team's own. File B is a limited assurance report on the same company's sustainability information for the year ended 31 March 2025, also drafted without reference to SSAE 3000. Neither company is among the top 1000 listed companies by market capitalisation.

items.stem: What does SA 250 require you to do about telling an authority outside the company?

options.text: Say nothing to anyone outside the company in any circumstances, confidentiality being absolute once an engagement letter records it
options.misconception: reads confidentiality as absolute, when SA 250 contemplates that law or regulation may require the auditor to report
options.why: Confidentiality is a strong duty and it is not an absolute one. SA 250 expressly contemplates reporting where law or regulation requires it, and in India several statutes do exactly that in their own fields.

options.text: Report the matter to the municipal authority and to the police at once — a suspected bribe is a matter of public interest and public interest overrides confidentiality
options.misconception: treats public interest as a self-executing override of the professional duty of confidentiality, when SA 250 asks first whether reporting is required by law or regulation
options.why: Public interest is the reason the law sometimes compels reporting; it is not itself the authority to report. The standard sends the auditor to the law of the jurisdiction, and a disclosure made without that footing is a breach of confidence rather than a duty discharged.

options.text: Withdraw from the engagement and treat the withdrawal as your answer to the question of external reporting
options.misconception: substitutes withdrawal for the determination the standard requires, when withdrawal answers a different question and does not settle whether anyone outside must be told
options.why: Withdrawal is a separate consideration in SA 250, and it does not dispose of the reporting question. An auditor who resigns still has to decide whether the law obliges him to tell somebody, and resigning may well leave that duty exactly where it was.

options.text: Determine whether you have a responsibility to report the suspected non-compliance to a party outside the entity, bearing in mind that your professional duty of confidentiality ordinarily prevents it unless reporting is required by law or regulation — and consider obtaining legal advice
options.why: SA 250 makes this a determination rather than a reflex. The auditor shall determine whether he has a responsibility to report the identified or suspected non-compliance to parties outside the entity. His professional duty of confidentiality ordinarily precludes such reporting unless it is required by law or regulation, and because the answer turns on the law of the place the standard treats legal advice as an appropriate step.

citation.ref: para 28 and para 29, read with para 24 on withdrawal

items.scenario: Auditing a construction company, you identify payments routed through a consultant that you suspect are bribes paid to obtain municipal clearances. You discuss the matter with management and then with those charged with governance. Both accept that the payments happened, decline to investigate further, and decline to inform anybody outside the company. Your engagement letter contains an ordinary confidentiality clause and no statute names you as a reporter of this kind of conduct.

items.stem: How does SA 299 (Revised) allocate responsibility for the two problems?

options.text: The missing disclosure is the responsibility of all three jointly and severally; the inventory overstatement is L's alone
options.why: SA 299 (Revised) splits responsibility in two. Each joint auditor is responsible for the work divided to him, so the badly performed stock count belongs to L. Presentation and disclosure of the financial statements as required by the applicable financial reporting framework is one of the matters for which the joint auditors are jointly and severally responsible, along with undivided work carried out by all of them and with ensuring that the audit report complies with the requirements.
keywords: audit report complies with the requirements

options.text: Both are the responsibility of all three jointly and severally, joint auditors sharing one appointment and one report
options.misconception: collapses the division of work into joint responsibility, when SA 299 makes each joint auditor responsible for the work divided to him
options.why: A common appointment and a common report do not make the work common. The standard divides the work precisely so that responsibility for performing it can be located, and a stock count divided to one firm is that firm's to answer for.

options.text: Both are L's, the inventory being his area and the missing disclosure relating to inventory quantities he was closest to
options.misconception: uses the subject matter of a disclosure to move a joint and several responsibility onto the joint auditor whose area it touches
options.why: Disclosure is not allocated by topic. It sits on the joint and several list because the financial statements are presented as a whole, and no joint auditor may point at another when the statements do not comply with the framework.

options.text: Neither can be allocated, because responsibility among joint auditors is settled by the engagement letter rather than by the standard
options.misconception: treats a professional responsibility fixed by the standard as something the parties can contract about
options.why: An engagement letter records the division of work; it cannot rewrite who answers for what. SA 299 (Revised) sets the allocation itself and names the matters that stay joint and several however the work is split.

citation.ref: para 13 on division of work and para 14 on joint and several responsibility

items.scenario: Three firms are joint auditors of a company. The work is divided: L takes inventory and fixed assets, M takes payables and payroll, N takes receivables. The notes to the financial statements, the presentation of the statements and the audit report itself were settled by all three together. After the report is signed two problems surface. A disclosure the applicable framework requires is missing from the notes. Separately, a stock count L attended was performed badly and inventory is overstated.

items.stem: What does SA 300 say about that file?

options.text: It is incomplete — the documentation must show the strategy, the plan, and any significant changes made to either during the engagement together with the reasons for those changes
options.why: SA 300 requires the audit documentation to include the overall audit strategy, the audit plan, and any significant changes made during the audit engagement to the overall audit strategy or the audit plan, and the reasons for such changes. Holding only the final version records the destination and loses the journey, and the acquisition is exactly the kind of event the reasons for such changes are meant to capture.

options.text: It is complete, because a mid-audit acquisition is a change in the entity rather than a change in the audit strategy
options.misconception: separates the entity from the audit of it, when a new location and a new accounting package change the scope, timing and direction of the audit
options.why: A new location and a second accounting package change what the audit has to cover and how it is resourced. That is a change to the overall audit strategy in the ordinary sense of the words, whatever caused it.

options.text: It is incomplete, but only because the superseded documents were deleted — keeping them would have satisfied the requirement without any note
options.misconception: treats retaining the old version as equivalent to recording the change and the reason for it
options.why: Two documents side by side show that something changed and leave the reader to guess why. The standard asks for the reasons, which is the part that cannot be reconstructed from the papers later.

options.text: It is complete — SA 300 asks for a strategy and a plan, and the file holds a correct one of each
options.misconception: reads the documentation requirement as two documents, when it has a third element covering changes and the reasons for them
options.why: The requirement lists three things and the file holds two. A reviewer reading it cannot tell that the scope of the audit moved mid-engagement, which is the single most important planning fact of this year.

citation.ref: para 12 on documentation, read with para 10 on changes to planning decisions during the audit

items.scenario: Halfway through an audit the client acquires a business, which brings in a new location and a second accounting package. The engagement partner reworks the overall audit strategy and the team rewrites the audit plan. The old versions of both are deleted from the working papers because, the senior says, a file holding two plans confuses the reviewer. The new documents are complete and correct and carry no note about what changed or why.

items.stem: What does SA 330 require?

options.text: Reliance is permissible without testing, because the control addresses no significant risk and this is only its second audit since it was last tested
options.misconception: applies the three-audit rotation to a control that has changed, when the rotation is conditional on the absence of changes
options.why: The absence of a significant risk removes one restriction and leaves the other standing. The rotation was never a fixed licence to skip two years; it operates only once the auditor has satisfied himself that the control is still the control he tested.
