Direct assistance is prohibited only where law or regulation prohibits it, or where there are significant threats to the internal auditor's objectivity or he lacks sufficient competence for the proposed work.

options.text: The organisational status settles it — a function reporting to the audit committee rather than to management supports the objectivity of its auditors, and that is the test the Standard sets
options.misconception: makes the reporting line the whole of the objectivity question, when three further factors go to the individual and the particular work
options.why: Organisational status is one of the factors and it is about the function. Objectivity is the ability to perform the proposed work without allowing bias, conflict of interest or undue influence of others to override professional judgments, and a man testing the department he worked in for six years faces a threat no reporting line removes.

options.text: The organisational status of the function is one factor among several, and the others answer each of the three cases — association with the division or department in the entity to which the work relates, family and personal relationships with an individual working in or responsible for the aspect of the entity to which the work relates, and significant financial interests in the entity other than remuneration on terms consistent with those applicable to other employees at a similar level of seniority — and the evaluation must include inquiry of the internal auditors themselves about interests and relationships that may create a threat
options.why: Reporting to the audit committee is the first factor and it goes to the function as a whole. The remaining factors are about the individual and the particular work: association with the division or department to which the work relates, which is the first internal auditor's six years in purchases; family and personal relationships with an individual working in or responsible for the aspect of the entity to which the work relates, which is the second's brother-in-law; and significant financial interests in the entity other than remuneration on terms consistent with those for other employees at a similar level of seniority, which is the third's shareholding. And the evaluation of the existence and significance of threats to objectivity shall include inquiry of the internal auditors regarding interests and relationships that may create a threat, so the external auditor asks them rather than inferring it.

options.text: Only the financial interest disqualifies — a shareholding is measurable while a past posting and a family connection are matters of degree that the external auditor's own supervision can contain
options.misconception: keeps the one threat that can be quantified and treats supervision as a safeguard against the two that cannot
options.why: All three are named factors and none of them is answered by supervision. The external auditor shall not use an internal auditor to provide direct assistance where there are significant threats to his objectivity, and the assessment of significance is made before the work is assigned rather than managed afterwards.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit Planning, Strategy and Execution — SA 610 (Revised): the factors relevant in evaluating the existence and significance of threats to the objectivity of an internal auditor providing direct assistance — the extent to which the function's organisational status and relevant policies and procedures support objectivity, family and personal relationships with an individual working in or responsible for the aspect of the entity to which the work relates, association with the division or department to which the work relates, and significant financial interests in the entity other than remuneration on terms consistent with those for other employees at a similar level of seniority — together with the requirement that the evaluation include inquiry of the internal auditors

items.scenario: An external auditor proposes to use three internal auditors to provide direct assistance. The first spent six years in the purchases department and is to be put on purchases testing. The second is the brother-in-law of the officer who authorises the payments he would be testing. The third holds shares in the company worth several times his annual salary, granted on terms not available to other employees at his level. The external auditor says the internal audit function reports to the audit committee, which settles the objectivity question for all three.

items.stem: May it?

options.text: No — where the law prescribes the wording the auditor is confined to what the law says, and a report in a prescribed form can never claim to have been made under the Standards on Auditing
options.misconception: reads a prescribed layout as cutting the report off from the Standards on Auditing altogether, when the standard provides expressly for the reference and states the condition on which it may be made
options.why: SA 700 (Revised) anticipates exactly this and gives the answer. It does not forbid the reference; it makes it conditional, and the condition is the list of minimum elements. A prescribed form that carries them may refer to the Standards on Auditing.

options.text: Yes, and no minimum applies — a report in the form the law prescribes complies with the Standards on Auditing by operation of the law that prescribed it
options.misconception: treats compliance with a prescribed layout as compliance with the Standards, when the reference to the Standards is conditional on the listed elements actually being present
options.why: The law settles what the report looks like; it does not settle what the report may claim. The claim to have audited in accordance with the Standards on Auditing is conditional, and the condition is that the thirteen elements are all there. A prescribed form missing one of them may not carry the reference.

options.text: Yes, but only once the Other Information section is added back, that section being one of the minimum elements the report must carry
options.misconception: puts the Other Information section among the minimum elements, when the list stops short of it and of two other sections the ordinary layout carries
options.why: It is not on the list. The minimum elements run from the title to the date and include nothing about other information, nothing about where the description of the auditor's responsibilities is located, and no separate section for other reporting responsibilities — which is why a prescribed form can be shorter than SA 700's own layout and still refer to the Standards.

options.text: Yes — a report whose layout or wording is prescribed by law or regulation may refer to the Standards on Auditing so long as it includes, at a minimum, each of the thirteen elements the standard lists, and an Other Information section, the location of the description of the auditor's responsibilities and the other reporting responsibilities section are not among them
options.why: The condition is a floor, not the whole of SA 700's own layout. Where the auditor is required by law or regulation applicable to the entity to use a specific layout or wording, his report shall refer to the Standards on Auditing only if it includes, at a minimum, each of thirteen elements — the title, the addressee, an Opinion section with a reference to the applicable financial reporting framework, an identification of the financial statements audited, the independence statement referring to the Code of Ethics issued by ICAI, the sections addressing SA 570 and a Basis for Qualified or Adverse Opinion and SA 701 where each is applicable, a description of management's responsibilities with an identification of those responsible for oversight of the financial reporting process, a reference to the Standards on Auditing and to the law or regulation with a description of the auditor's responsibilities, the signature, the place and the date. Everything the regulator's form is missing sits outside that list.
keywords: Code of Ethics issued by ICAI

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 700 (Revised): where law or regulation requires a specific layout or wording, the auditor's report shall refer to the Standards on Auditing only if it includes at a minimum each of the thirteen listed elements

items.scenario: A regulator prescribes, word for word, the form of the auditor's report for the entities it supervises. The prescribed form carries a title, an addressee, an Opinion section naming the framework, an identification of the statements audited, the independence statement referring to the Code of Ethics issued by ICAI, a description of management's responsibilities with the persons responsible for oversight named, a reference to the Standards on Auditing and to the regulator's own rules with a description of the auditor's responsibilities, the signature, the place and the date. It has no Other Information section, no paragraph on where the description of the auditor's responsibilities is located, and no separate section for other reporting responsibilities. The engagement partner wants to know whether the report may still say the audit was conducted in accordance with the Standards on Auditing.

items.stem: What does SA 700 (Revised) allow?

options.text: Not that — the report may refer to both only if there is no conflict between the two sets of requirements that would lead the auditor to form a different opinion, or not to include an Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph that the Standards on Auditing require in the circumstances, and only if it carries at a minimum the same elements a prescribed report must carry; where the reference is made, the report clearly identifies both, including the jurisdiction of origin of the other standards
options.why: Dropping the paragraph is the conflict, so the dual reference fails on its own terms. The auditor may refer to the Standards on Auditing in addition to the International Standards on Auditing or the standards of another jurisdiction only if there is no conflict between them that would lead him to form a different opinion or not to include an Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph that is required by the Standards on Auditing in the particular circumstances, and only if the report includes at a minimum each of the elements listed for a report prescribed by law or regulation. And when the report does refer to both, it clearly identifies them, including the jurisdiction of origin of the other auditing standards.
keywords: Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph

options.text: Refer to both with no condition at all — naming two sets of standards is a description of what was done, not a claim about either of them
options.misconception: reads the dual reference as a factual description, when the standard makes it conditional on the absence of conflict and on the minimum elements being present
options.why: It is a claim, and SA 700 (Revised) fences it with two conditions: no conflict of the kind described, and the minimum elements all present. A reference made without them tells the reader the report satisfies both sets of requirements when it satisfies only one.

options.text: Drop the paragraph and refer to both, with the explanatory sentence — a conflict that is disclosed to the reader is a conflict he can allow for
options.misconception: treats a disclosure of the conflict as curing it, when the condition for the dual reference is that no such conflict exists at all
options.why: The standard does not ask the auditor to explain the conflict; it asks whether there is one. A conflict that leads him not to include a paragraph the Standards on Auditing require is precisely the conflict named, and no sentence in the report makes the dual reference available once it exists.

options.text: Refer only to the other jurisdiction's standards, since the report is being prepared for the parent's group audit and those standards govern what it must contain
options.misconception: lets the reader of the report choose which standards the audit was conducted under, when the audit was conducted under both and the Standards on Auditing require the paragraph
options.why: The audit was conducted in accordance with the Standards on Auditing as well, and dropping the reference does not drop the requirement. The paragraph is required in the circumstances by the Standards on Auditing, and an audit conducted under them includes it whatever else the report refers to.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 700 (Revised): an auditor's report for an audit conducted in accordance with both the Standards on Auditing and the International Standards on Auditing or the auditing standards of another jurisdiction may refer to both only where no conflict would lead the auditor to a different opinion or to omitting a required Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph, and only where the minimum elements are present, and it shall clearly identify both including the jurisdiction of origin of the other standards

items.scenario: An Indian subsidiary of a foreign group is audited in accordance with the Standards on Auditing issued by ICAI and also the auditing standards of the parent's jurisdiction. A significant subsequent event has occurred which the Standards on Auditing require to be brought to users' attention in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph; the other jurisdiction's standards do not call for one, and the group reporting team has asked that the paragraph be dropped. The manager proposes to drop it and to have the report refer to both sets of standards, adding a sentence explaining that the other jurisdiction's standards do not require such a paragraph.

items.stem: How does SA 700 (Revised) treat the two?

options.text: The appendix is not covered and, management having refused, the auditor modifies his opinion because the presentation of the financial statements as a whole is now misleading
options.misconception: answers a presentation problem in the unaudited information with a modification of the opinion on the financial statements, when the standard answers it by identifying the information and explaining that it has not been audited
options.why: The defect is in how unaudited information is presented, not in the financial statements the opinion covers. SA 700 (Revised) gives the remedy: ask management to change the presentation, and on refusal identify the unaudited supplementary information and explain in the report that it has not been audited.

options.text: Both are covered by the opinion, since both are printed with the audited financial statements and a reader takes everything between the same covers as audited
options.misconception: extends the opinion to everything bound with the statements, when the standard provides for information that can be clearly differentiated and is not covered
options.why: The risk that a reader takes everything as audited is the reason for the differentiation requirement, not a reason to audit everything. Information that can be clearly differentiated from the financial statements is not covered by the opinion; what the standard requires is that the presentation make the difference visible.

options.text: Neither is covered by the opinion, both being outside what the framework requires, and the auditor states in his report that all supplementary information is unaudited
options.misconception: makes the framework's requirements the test, when the test is whether the information is an integral part of the financial statements by its nature or by how it is presented
options.why: Being outside the framework's requirements is what makes the information supplementary in the first place; it does not answer the question the standard asks next. Some supplementary information is an integral part of the statements by its nature or its presentation, and that information is covered by the opinion.

options.text: The reconciliation note is an integral part of the financial statements and is covered by the auditor's opinion; the appendix can be clearly differentiated, so it is not covered, and because management has refused to change how it is presented the auditor identifies the unaudited supplementary information and explains in his report that it has not been audited
options.why: The test is whether the supplementary information is nevertheless an integral part of the financial statements due to its nature or how it is presented. A note explaining or reconciling the extent of compliance with another framework, cross-referenced from the statements, is information that cannot be clearly differentiated from them, and where it is an integral part it shall be covered by the auditor's opinion. An additional profit and loss account presented as a separate schedule in an appendix is information that can be clearly differentiated; the auditor then evaluates whether it is presented in a way that sufficiently and clearly differentiates it, asks management to change the presentation where it is not, and where management refuses, identifies the information and explains in his report that it has not been audited.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 700 (Revised): supplementary information that is an integral part of the financial statements shall be covered by the auditor's opinion, and where it is not an integral part but is not sufficiently and clearly differentiated the auditor asks management to change the presentation and, on refusal, identifies it and explains in his report that it has not been audited

items.scenario: Two things are printed with a company's audited financial statements and neither is required by the applicable framework. The first is a note that reconciles the extent to which the statements comply with another financial reporting framework, and it is cross-referenced from note 4. The second is an additional profit and loss account disclosing specific items of expenditure, presented as a separate schedule in an appendix, laid out in the same type and format as the statements with no marking to set it apart. Management refuses to change how the appendix is presented.

items.stem: Is he right under SA 700 (Revised)?

options.text: No, and the auditor must ask management to move the schedule into an appendix so that it can be clearly differentiated and left out of the opinion
options.misconception: treats the differentiation route as available for information that is an integral part of the financial statements, when that route is for information which is not
options.why: The two routes are alternatives and the first one is already closed. Asking management to change the presentation is what the standard requires for supplementary information that is not an integral part; a schedule the notes depend on is an integral part, and moving it does not change that.

options.text: No — the auditor evaluates whether the supplementary information is nevertheless an integral part of the financial statements due to its nature or how it is presented, and where it is, it shall be covered by his opinion; a schedule cross-referenced from the notes is covered, and a label cannot take it out
options.why: The label describes what management would like the schedule to be; the standard asks what it is. The auditor evaluates whether, in his professional judgement, supplementary information not required by the framework is nevertheless an integral part of the financial statements due to its nature or how it is presented, and when it is an integral part it shall be covered by the auditor's opinion. The module puts it plainly: the opinion would also cover notes or supplementary schedules that are cross-referenced from the financial statements.

options.text: Yes — information marked unaudited is by that fact outside the opinion, and the auditor's only duty is to check that the marking is prominent
options.misconception: lets a label decide the scope of the opinion, when the standard decides it on the nature of the information and how it is presented
options.why: If a label could decide it, any figure could be put beyond the opinion by heading it "unaudited", and the differentiation requirement would have nothing to do. Where the information is an integral part of the financial statements it is covered by the opinion whatever it is headed.

options.text: Yes, provided the auditor adds an Other Matter paragraph recording that the schedule is outside the scope of his opinion
options.misconception: uses a paragraph to move information out of an opinion the standard says covers it, rather than answering the question of whether it is an integral part
options.why: A paragraph cannot narrow an opinion the standard says extends to the information. The question is whether the schedule is an integral part of the financial statements, and a schedule the notes rely on and cross-refer to is one; the paragraph would tell the reader something untrue about the scope of the opinion.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 700 (Revised): supplementary information that is an integral part of the financial statements due to its nature or how it is presented shall be covered by the auditor's opinion, the opinion covering notes or supplementary schedules cross-referenced from the financial statements

items.scenario: A company presents, within its financial statements, a schedule of key operating ratios headed "Unaudited — for information only". The schedule is cross-referenced from note 12, which relies on it to explain a movement in trade receivables. The finance director says the heading settles the matter and that the auditor's opinion cannot reach anything marked unaudited.

items.stem: What does SA 701 have the section say?

options.text: The section stays, and because the report already carries those two sections the paragraph reads that except for the matters described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section and the Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section, the auditor has determined that there are no other key audit matters to communicate in his report
options.why: Both readings are half right. Where the auditor determines that there are no key audit matters to communicate, the report must still carry the section and say so — so deleting it is wrong. But a flat statement that there are no key audit matters would contradict the rest of the report, because a matter giving rise to a modification and a material uncertainty related to going concern are by their nature matters of most significance. The illustration in the module carries the exception on the face of the sentence: except for the matter described in the Basis for Qualified (Adverse) Opinion section or Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section, the auditor has determined that there are no other key audit matters to communicate.
keywords: Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern

options.text: Keep the section with the plain sentence that the auditor has determined that there are no key audit matters to communicate, the two matters having their own sections and so being outside this one
options.misconception: says there are none at all in a report that carries two matters which are of most significance by their nature, so the sentence contradicts the rest of the report
options.why: They are outside the section and they are still of most significance in the audit, which is why the illustration keeps the word "other" in the sentence and names the sections the excepted matters sit in. Without the exception the report says on one page that nothing was of most significance and on another that the opinion is qualified.

options.text: Delete the section — a heading with nothing under it tells the reader less than no heading at all, and the two matters are already described elsewhere in the report
options.misconception: reads the requirement to communicate key audit matters as conditional on there being something to describe, when the section is required and carries a statement that there are none
options.why: The section is not conditional on its contents. Where the auditor has determined that there are no key audit matters to communicate, the report must specifically mention that by carrying a Key Audit Matters paragraph which says so. A reader of a listed company's report expects the section and its absence is itself information.

options.text: Keep the section and describe the inventory misstatement and the going concern uncertainty in it as the key audit matters, they being the most significant matters in the audit
options.misconception: turns a cross-reference into a description, when the paragraph names those matters only to except them from a statement that there are no others
options.why: Naming them and describing them are different acts. Communicating a key audit matter is not a substitute for expressing a modified opinion or for reporting under SA 570, so those two matters are reported in their own sections; the Key Audit Matters section refers to them and goes no further.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 701: where there are no key audit matters to communicate the report carries a Key Audit Matters paragraph saying so, and the illustration excepts the matter described in the Basis for Qualified (Adverse) Opinion section or the Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section and states that there are no other key audit matters to communicate

items.scenario: The report on a listed company carries a Basis for Qualified Opinion section on an inventory misstatement and a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section. Nothing else in the audit required significant auditor attention. One manager wants the Key Audit Matters section deleted, since there is nothing left to put in it. Another wants it kept with a single sentence saying that the auditor has determined that there are no key audit matters to communicate.

items.stem: What does SA 710 require in the report you are about to sign?

options.text: Your opinion refers to the current period only, comparatives never being covered by the opinion, so the earlier year is dealt with by a note in the accounts if management chooses
options.misconception: applies the corresponding figures rule to comparative financial statements, where the opinion refers to each period presented
options.why: That is the corresponding figures rule, and it is the other approach. The two differ in exactly this: for corresponding figures the opinion refers to the current period only, whereas for comparative financial statements it refers to each period for which financial statements are presented.

options.text: Express the different opinion on the earlier period and put the reasons for the difference in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, the matter being fundamental to users' understanding
options.misconception: uses the paragraph reserved for a matter appropriately presented in the financial statements to carry the reasons for a change of opinion, which the standard places in an Other Matter paragraph
options.why: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph refers to a matter appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements. Why the auditor's opinion has changed is not in the financial statements at all; it is a matter relevant to users' understanding of the audit and of the report, and SA 710 names the Other Matter paragraph for it.

options.text: Reissue last year's report carrying the new opinion, and confine this year's report to this year, since an opinion is amended in the report that expressed it
options.misconception: reopens a completed engagement instead of expressing the changed opinion in the current report with its reasons in an Other Matter paragraph
options.why: SA 710 does not send the auditor back to the old report. The prior period is presented again in this year's financial statements and is covered by this year's opinion, so the different opinion is expressed here and the substantive reasons for it are disclosed in an Other Matter paragraph.

options.text: Because comparative financial statements are presented, your opinion refers to each period for which financial statements are presented, so a different opinion may be expressed on the earlier period now — and where the opinion on the prior period financial statements differs from the opinion you previously expressed on them, the substantive reasons for the different opinion are disclosed in an Other Matter paragraph in your report
options.why: Under the comparative financial statements approach the auditor's opinion refers to each period for which financial statements are presented, so the earlier year is not closed by last year's report — it is being reported on again. SA 710 then deals with the awkward case directly: when reporting on the current period's audit, if the auditor's opinion on the prior period financial statements differs from the opinion previously expressed, he shall disclose the substantive reasons for the different opinion in an Other Matter paragraph. The changed opinion goes in the opinion; the reasons for the change go in the paragraph.
keywords: differs from the opinion previously expressed

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 710: with comparative financial statements the auditor's opinion refers to each period for which financial statements are presented, and where the opinion on the prior period differs from the opinion previously expressed the substantive reasons for the different opinion are disclosed in an Other Matter paragraph

items.scenario: A company presents comparative financial statements for two years, both audited by you, and you expressed an unmodified opinion on the earlier year. Work on the current year has established that a warranty provision in the earlier year was materially understated on a basis you now accept was wrong, and the earlier year's figures as presented are unchanged. Your manager says the opinion you gave last year is final and this year's report can only deal with this year.

items.stem: What does SA 710 require you to do first?

options.text: Include an Other Matter paragraph stating that the prior period was audited by a predecessor auditor, the type of opinion he expressed and the date of his report, and leave the misstatement there
options.misconception: uses the paragraph that identifies a predecessor's report to carry a misstatement the standard deals with by informing management and the predecessor
options.why: That paragraph tells the reader who audited the prior period and what he concluded, which is a different job. A material misstatement in previously audited figures is reported to management with a request that the predecessor auditor be informed, and the paragraph does not stand in place of it.

options.text: Say nothing about the prior period — it was reported on by the predecessor auditor, and a successor does not go behind another member's report
options.misconception: treats the predecessor's report as closing the period, when the auditor reporting on comparative financial statements is expressing an opinion on that period as well
options.why: He is not going behind the report; he is expressing his own opinion on the same period, because with comparative financial statements the opinion refers to each period presented. Silence would leave him giving an opinion on figures he believes are materially misstated.

options.text: Qualify your opinion on the prior period at once, the opinion under comparative financial statements referring to each period presented
options.misconception: goes straight to the opinion, when the standard first requires management to be told and the predecessor auditor to be informed, and provides for the statements being amended instead
options.why: The opinion does reach the prior period, which is why the misstatement matters — but SA 710 does not have the auditor start there. He reports the matter to management and asks that the predecessor be informed, and where that leads to amended statements and a new report from the predecessor, he reports only on the current period.

options.text: Report the matter to the appropriate level of management and request that the predecessor auditor be informed — and if the prior period financial statements are then amended and the predecessor auditor agrees to issue a new report on them, report only on the current period
options.why: The standard puts two steps before the opinion. Where the auditor concludes that a material misstatement is present in previously audited figures of the financial statements, he should report it to the appropriate level of the management and request that the predecessor auditor be informed. If the prior years' statements are then amended and a new report is issued on them by the predecessor auditor, the auditor shall report only on the current period. The route exists because the person who reported on those figures is the person who can put them right.
keywords: request that the predecessor auditor be informed
report only on the current period

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 710: where the auditor concludes that a material misstatement is present in previously audited figures he reports it to the appropriate level of management and requests that the predecessor auditor be informed, and where the prior period statements are amended and the predecessor issues a new report he reports only on the current period

items.scenario: You are in your first year with a company that presents comparative financial statements. The prior period was audited by a predecessor auditor who expressed an unmodified opinion. Your work establishes that a material misstatement exists in those previously audited figures and was never dealt with. A partner suggests you simply qualify your opinion on the prior period, since under this approach the opinion covers both years anyway.

items.stem: What else must that section contain?

options.text: The other statements, but they belong in the Responsibilities of Management and Auditor's Responsibilities sections rather than in a section of their own
options.misconception: scatters the required contents across other sections, when the standard requires a separate section headed Other Information carrying all of them
options.why: The standard requires a separate section with the heading Other Information, and it requires that section to include the statements. Spreading them elsewhere leaves the reader assembling from three places the one thing the section exists to tell him in one.

options.text: Four more things — a statement that management is responsible for the other information; an identification of the other information obtained before the date of the report and, for a listed entity, of the other information expected to be obtained after that date; a statement that the auditor's opinion does not cover the other information and that accordingly he does not and will not express an audit opinion or any form of assurance conclusion on it; and a description of the auditor's responsibilities relating to reading, considering and reporting on it
options.why: The nothing-to-report sentence is the fifth of the five contents, not the section. SA 720 (Revised) requires the section to include a statement that management is responsible for the other information; an identification of the other information, if any, obtained prior to the date of the auditor's report and, for a listed entity, of the other information, if any, expected to be obtained after that date; a statement that the auditor's opinion does not cover the other information and that accordingly he does not express, or will not express, an audit opinion or any form of assurance conclusion on it; a description of his responsibilities relating to reading, considering and reporting on it; and, where other information was obtained before the date of the report, either the statement that he has nothing to report or a statement describing an uncorrected material misstatement of it.
keywords: management is responsible for the other information
does not cover the other information

options.text: The three other statements, but not the identification of information expected after the date of the report, which cannot be identified before it exists
options.misconception: reads the identification requirement as needing the document in hand, when for a listed entity the section identifies the other information expected to be obtained after the date of the report
options.why: The standard asks for the document to be identified, not read. For an audit of a listed entity the section identifies the other information, if any, expected to be obtained after the date of the auditor's report — which is why the auditor first determines through discussion with management which documents comprise the annual report.

options.text: Nothing more — the conclusion is the point of the section, and the rest is standing wording that adds length without adding meaning
options.misconception: keeps the conclusion and drops the four elements that tell the reader what the conclusion is about and what it is worth
options.why: A reader who is told only that there is nothing to report does not know which documents were read, who is responsible for them, or that the opinion does not cover them. Each of the four is a separate requirement of the standard and each answers one of those questions.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 720 (Revised): the Other Information section shall include a statement that management is responsible for the other information, an identification of the other information obtained before the date of the report and, for a listed entity, expected after it, a statement that the auditor's opinion does not cover the other information, a description of the auditor's responsibilities, and either a statement that the auditor has nothing to report or one describing an uncorrected material misstatement

items.scenario: The draft report on a listed company carries a section headed Other Information containing one sentence: that the auditor has read the other information and has nothing to report. The directors' report and the business responsibility statement were obtained before the date of the report; the shareholders' information section will only be available afterwards.

items.stem: What does SA 720 (Revised) allow?

options.text: Yes, but only the statement that the auditor's opinion does not cover the other information is indispensable, the rest being detail
options.misconception: picks one statement out of the ordinary section and calls it the minimum, when the standard names three different elements for a prescribed wording
options.why: That statement belongs to the ordinary section's five contents and is not among the three the standard names here. The three for a prescribed wording are the identification of the other information obtained before the date of the report, the description of the auditor's responsibilities, and the explicit statement of the outcome of his work.

options.text: Yes — where law or regulation requires a specific layout or wording, the report may refer to the Standards on Auditing if it includes at a minimum three things: an identification of the other information obtained by the auditor prior to the date of his report, a description of his responsibilities with respect to the other information, and an explicit statement addressing the outcome of his work for this purpose
options.why: The prescribed wording carries all three and so the reference stands. SA 720 (Revised) sets its own floor for a prescribed form, and it is shorter than the ordinary section: an identification of the other information obtained prior to the date of the auditor's report, a description of the auditor's responsibilities with respect to the other information, and an explicit statement addressing the outcome of the auditor's work for this purpose. The statements about management's responsibility and about the opinion not covering the other information are required in the ordinary section and are not part of that minimum.

options.text: No condition arises — where the regulator has prescribed the wording, the report complies with the Standards on Auditing because the auditor has done what the law requires
options.misconception: treats obedience to the prescribed wording as compliance with the standard, when the reference to the Standards on Auditing is conditional on the three minimum elements
options.why: Following the prescribed wording settles what the auditor must write; it does not settle what he may claim about it. The reference to the Standards on Auditing is available only if the three minimum elements are present, and the auditor has to look for them.

options.text: No — a prescribed wording may refer to the Standards on Auditing only if it carries everything the ordinary Other Information section carries, and two of the five are missing
options.misconception: reads the minimum for a prescribed wording as the full list required of the ordinary section, when the standard states a shorter list of three for this case
options.why: The standard writes a separate and shorter list for a prescribed wording, and it names three elements. Requiring the full five would leave no case in which a prescribed wording could ever refer to the Standards on Auditing, which is not what the provision is for.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — SA 720 (Revised): where law or regulation requires the auditor to refer to other information using a specific layout or wording, the report may refer to the Standards on Auditing only if it includes at a minimum an identification of the other information obtained prior to the date of the report, a description of the auditor's responsibilities with respect to it, and an explicit statement addressing the outcome of the auditor's work

items.scenario: A sectoral regulator prescribes the wording an auditor must use when referring to other information in his report on the entities it supervises. The prescribed wording identifies the documents obtained before the date of the report, describes the auditor's responsibilities in respect of them and states expressly what the outcome of his work on them was. It carries no statement that management is responsible for the other information and no statement that the opinion does not cover it. The partner asks whether the report can still refer to the Standards on Auditing.

items.stem: What does SA 800 require?

options.text: Determine materiality under SA 320 regardless — the existence of an agreed threshold does not relieve the auditor of that requirement — and in an audit of special purpose financial statements make the judgements about what is material by reference to the financial information needs of the intended users rather than of a wide range of users; and determine afresh the appropriate person to communicate with, because those responsible for oversight of the special purpose financial statements may not be those charged with governance responsible for the general purpose statements
options.why: Both of the manager's shortcuts are answered in terms. Where management agrees with the intended users on a threshold below which misstatements identified during the audit will not be corrected or otherwise adjusted, the existence of such a threshold does not relieve the auditor from the requirement to determine materiality in accordance with SA 320 for the purpose of planning and performing the audit. And in a special purpose audit the judgements about matters material to users are based on a consideration of the financial information needs of the intended users, not of users as a group. On communication, SA 260 (Revised) requires the appropriate persons to be determined, and where the entity also prepares a complete set of general purpose financial statements those responsible for the oversight of the special purpose statements may not be the same people.
keywords: financial information needs of the intended users
may not be the same people

options.text: Determine materiality under SA 320 on the common financial information needs of a wide range of users, since SA 320 is applied unchanged whatever the framework
options.misconception: applies SA 320 without the adjustment SA 800 makes to it, which is to base the judgements on the intended users rather than on users as a group
options.why: SA 320 applies, and SA 800 says how. The judgements about matters material to users are ordinarily based on the common financial information needs of users as a group; in an audit of special purpose financial statements they are based on the financial information needs of the intended users.

options.text: Determine materiality under SA 320, and communicate with the board audit committee as proposed, since those charged with governance of the entity are the same people whatever statements are being audited
options.misconception: assumes one governance body for both sets of statements, when the standard says those responsible for oversight of the special purpose financial statements may be different
options.why: Half the answer is right. The other half is what the standard warns against: where a complete set of general purpose financial statements is also prepared, the persons responsible for the oversight of the special purpose financial statements may not be the same as those charged with governance responsible for the general purpose ones, so the appropriate person is determined for this engagement.

options.text: Adopt the agreed threshold as materiality — the intended users are the only readers, and a threshold they have themselves agreed is by definition the level at which a misstatement would influence them
options.misconception: lets an agreement about which misstatements will be corrected settle the auditor's own materiality, which the standard says it does not
options.why: The threshold governs what will be corrected; materiality governs how the audit is planned and performed and how uncorrected misstatements are evaluated. The standard says so directly: the existence of such a threshold does not relieve the auditor from determining materiality in accordance with SA 320.

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 800: materiality judgements based on the financial information needs of the intended users, an agreed correction threshold that does not relieve the auditor from determining materiality under SA 320, and the appropriate person to communicate with determined under SA 260 (Revised) where those overseeing the special purpose statements may not be those charged with governance for the general purpose ones

items.scenario: You are auditing financial statements prepared under the reporting clauses of a loan agreement between two companies. The borrower and the lender have agreed in the contract that misstatements below a stated figure identified during the audit will not be corrected. Your manager proposes to adopt that figure as the audit's materiality and to save time on the whole engagement, and to report significant findings to the same board audit committee that oversees the company's general purpose financial statements.

items.stem: What does SA 800 require of the report?

options.text: Nothing more — a note describing the basis of accounting, drawn attention to in the report, tells the reader everything about the framework that the standard asks for
options.misconception: treats the description of the basis of accounting as covering the purpose and the intended users, which the standard requires separately
options.why: The basis of accounting says how the statements were prepared. The standard also asks why and for whom: the report shall describe the purpose for which they are prepared and, if necessary, the intended users, or refer to a note that contains that information.

options.text: Restrict the distribution of the report instead of describing its purpose — a report nobody else may use cannot be misused, so the description adds nothing
options.misconception: substitutes the restriction on distribution for the description of the purpose and the intended users, when the standard requires both and treats the restriction as an addition to the alert
options.why: The restriction is an addition to the alert, not a replacement for the description. The standard says that in addition to the alert the auditor may consider it appropriate to indicate that his report is intended solely for the specific users, and the report still describes the purpose for which the statements were prepared.

options.text: It shall describe the purpose for which the financial statements are prepared and, if necessary, the intended users, or refer to a note containing that information; because management had a choice of frameworks, the explanation of management's responsibility shall also refer to its responsibility for determining that the applicable framework is acceptable in the circumstances; and the paragraph alerting readers may be expanded to indicate that the report is intended solely for the specific users, with the heading modified accordingly
options.why: Three separate requirements meet in this report. In an auditor's report on special purpose financial statements the report shall also describe the purpose for which the financial statements are prepared and, if necessary, the intended users, or refer to a note in the statements containing that information. Where management has a choice of financial reporting frameworks, the explanation of management's responsibility shall also make reference to its responsibility for determining that the applicable financial reporting framework is acceptable in the circumstances. And where the auditor considers it appropriate to indicate that the report is intended solely for the specific users, the paragraph alerting readers may be expanded to include those other matters and the heading modified accordingly.
keywords: purpose for which the financial statements are prepared

options.text: Put the purpose and the intended users in an Other Matter paragraph, which is where matters about the report rather than the financial statements belong
options.misconception: moves into a paragraph a description the standard makes part of the report's own account of the framework, and treats an addressable requirement as a matter of placement
options.why: The requirement is on the report as a whole and is met by describing the purpose and the intended users or by referring to a note that contains that information; it is not an Other Matter. What the standard does place in an added paragraph is the alert about the special purpose framework and, where used, the restriction on distribution or use.

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 800: the auditor's report on special purpose financial statements shall describe the purpose for which they are prepared and, if necessary, the intended users or refer to a note containing that information; where management has a choice of frameworks the explanation of its responsibility shall refer to its responsibility for determining that the framework is acceptable; and the alerting paragraph may be expanded to restrict distribution or use with the heading modified accordingly

items.scenario: X Ltd's financial statements are prepared under the reporting provisions of its contract with Y Ltd. Management could have used one of two permitted frameworks and chose this one. Your draft report gives an unmodified opinion and draws attention to note A, which describes the basis of accounting. It does not say why the statements were prepared or who they are for, and the responsibilities paragraph says only that management is responsible for their preparation. You also want the report used by nobody but X Ltd and Y Ltd.

items.stem: What does SA 805 require him to settle before he accepts?

options.text: Nothing — an audit of one element by someone who does not audit the complete set is not permitted, because the two opinions would be given on the same records by different firms
options.misconception: turns a question about practicability into a prohibition, when the standard contemplates the engagement and asks only whether compliance with the SAs is practicable
options.why: SA 805 provides for exactly this engagement. It applies the requirement to comply with all relevant SAs irrespective of whether the auditor is also engaged on the complete set, and where he is not, it asks him to determine whether such an audit in accordance with the SAs is practicable — a question, not a bar.

options.text: Nothing beyond obtaining the other firm's audit file, from which he can take the understanding of the entity and the evidence about the quality of the accounting records
options.misconception: borrows another auditor's work in place of the understanding and evidence the standard says he will be without, when the requirement is to obtain his own
options.why: The gap the standard describes is a gap in his own knowledge and his own evidence. Reading another firm's file does not give him the understanding of the entity and its internal control that comes from auditing the complete set, and he may still need further evidence to corroborate audit evidence acquired from the accounting records.

options.text: Nothing — he may accept and scale the Standards on Auditing down to the size of the element, adapting them as necessary being what the standard expressly permits
options.misconception: reads the instruction to adapt the SAs as necessary as permission to leave requirements out, when adaptation is about the circumstances of the engagement and not about the requirements
options.why: Adapting the SAs as necessary in the circumstances is how they are applied to an element; it is not a licence to drop them. That is why the standard asks a prior question — whether an audit in accordance with the SAs is practicable — and offers a different type of engagement as the answer where it is not.

options.text: Whether an audit of the element in accordance with the Standards on Auditing is practicable at all — because, not being engaged on the complete set, he does not have the same understanding of the entity and its environment including its internal control, has no audit evidence about the general quality of the accounting records, may need further evidence to corroborate what those records give him, and faces SAs whose requirements may be disproportionate to the element; and if he concludes it may not be practicable he may discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be
options.why: The requirement to comply with all SAs relevant to the audit applies whether or not he is also engaged to audit the complete set, so the question is not which SAs he may drop but whether he can meet them. Where he is not also engaged on the complete set he shall determine whether the audit of the specific element in accordance with the SAs is practicable, and the standard gives the reasons it may not be: he often does not have the same understanding of the entity and its environment including its internal control; he does not have audit evidence about the general quality of the accounting records or other accounting information; he may accordingly need further evidence to corroborate audit evidence acquired from the accounting records; and certain SAs require audit work that may be disproportionate to the element being audited. If he concludes it may not be practicable he may discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable.
keywords: general quality of the accounting records

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 805: where the auditor is not also engaged to audit the entity's complete set of financial statements he shall determine whether an audit of the single financial statement or of the specific element in accordance with the SAs is practicable, the standard naming the absence of the same understanding of the entity and its internal control, the absence of evidence about the general quality of the accounting records, the need for further corroborating evidence and the disproportionate audit work certain SAs would require

items.scenario: CA G is offered the audit of the trade payables balance of a company whose financial statements under the Companies Act, 2013 are audited by another firm. He has no other engagement with the company. He proposes to accept and to confine his work to circularising the suppliers and agreeing the balances to the ledger.

items.stem: What does SA 805 require?

options.text: The element can properly be considered in isolation, that being the point of an engagement on one element, so sales, cash and the allowance are outside the scope
options.misconception: reads the narrow subject of the engagement as a narrow field of work, when the standard says the interrelation of the items may require procedures beyond the element itself
options.why: The subject of the opinion is narrow; the work needed to support it is not necessarily. The individual statements and many of the elements, including their notes, are interrelated, so the auditor may not be able to consider the element in isolation and may need to perform procedures in relation to the interrelated items.

options.text: The materiality determined for the specific element may be lower than that for the complete set, which affects the nature, timing and extent of the procedures and the evaluation of uncorrected misstatements; evidence obtained in the audit of the complete set may be used, but the SAs still require the audit of the element to be planned and performed to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on it; and because the items are interrelated, procedures may be needed on the interrelated items
options.why: All three of the proposals are answered. The materiality determined for a specific element may be lower than the materiality determined for the complete set, and this will affect the nature, timing and extent of the audit procedures and the evaluation of uncorrected misstatements. When auditing an element alongside the complete set the auditor may be able to use audit evidence obtained in that audit, but the SAs require him to plan and perform the audit of the element to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on it. And because the statements and many of their elements, including the related notes, are interrelated, he may not be able to consider the element in isolation and may need to perform procedures in relation to the interrelated items.

options.text: The complete set's materiality governs both engagements, one entity having one materiality, and the receivables work in the main audit is the evidence for both opinions
options.misconception: carries one materiality and one body of work across two engagements, when the standard says the element's materiality may be lower and requires evidence sufficient for the opinion on the element
options.why: Two opinions are being expressed and the second is on a much smaller subject, which is why the standard says the materiality determined for the element may be lower than that for the complete set. The evidence gathered in the main audit may be used, but it is not by itself the basis for the opinion on the element.

options.text: Evidence from the audit of the complete set cannot be used at all, each engagement standing on its own evidence, so the receivables work must be performed again for the element
options.misconception: separates the two engagements completely, when the standard expressly allows the auditor to use evidence obtained in the audit of the complete set
options.why: The standard says the opposite: when auditing an element in conjunction with the audit of the complete set, the auditor may be able to use audit evidence obtained in that audit. What it does not allow is stopping there, because the SAs still require sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the element.

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 805: audit evidence obtained in the audit of the complete set may be used but the SAs require the audit of the element to be planned and performed to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence for the opinion on it, procedures may be needed on interrelated items, and the materiality determined for the element may be lower than that determined for the complete set

items.scenario: You audit a company's complete set of financial statements and have also been engaged to audit its schedule of trade receivables. Your senior proposes to carry the materiality determined for the complete set across to the schedule, to rest the opinion on the schedule entirely on the receivables work already done in the main audit, and to look at the schedule on its own without touching sales, cash or the allowance for doubtful debts.

items.stem: What does SA 805 require?

options.text: Nothing follows — the standard speaks only to an adverse opinion or a disclaimer, so a qualified opinion on the complete set leaves the report on the schedule untouched
options.misconception: reads the rule about a contradictory unmodified opinion as the whole of the standard's treatment of a modification, when a qualified opinion and either paragraph each require the auditor to determine the effect on the report on the element
options.why: The adverse-or-disclaimer rule exists because an unmodified opinion would contradict it. A separate requirement runs ahead of it: where the report on the complete set is modified or carries an Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph, the auditor shall determine the effect on the report on the element and act where he deems it appropriate.

options.text: The opinion on the schedule must be qualified in the same terms, the two reports being drawn from the same accounting records and the same audit
options.misconception: makes the modification automatic, when the standard requires the auditor to determine the effect and to act only when he deems it appropriate
options.why: Nothing is carried across automatically. The auditor determines the effect that the modification may have on the report on the element, and modifies the opinion on the element or adds a paragraph when deemed appropriate — which on facts touching neither the schedule nor its measurement may mean a paragraph rather than a modification.

options.text: Determine the effect that the qualified opinion and the Emphasis of Matter may have on the report on the schedule and, when deemed appropriate, modify the opinion on the schedule or include an Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph in that report — and even where the matters do not relate to the schedule, refer to the modification in an Other Matter paragraph if you judge it relevant to users' understanding of the audited element or of the related report
options.why: The contradiction rule is only one part of SA 805's treatment of a modification. Where the opinion in the auditor's report on the complete set is modified, or that report includes an Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph, the auditor shall determine the effect that this may have on the report on the single financial statement or on the specific element, and when deemed appropriate shall modify the opinion on the element or include an Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph accordingly. The standard then deals with this very case: even when the modification, Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph does not relate to the audited element, the auditor may still deem it appropriate to refer to it in an Other Matter paragraph because he judges it relevant to users' understanding of the audited element or of the related report.
keywords: does not relate to the audited element

options.text: A reference may be made only where the modification relates to the audited element; an unrelated matter has no place in a report on one schedule
options.misconception: excludes the very case the standard provides for, which is a modification that does not relate to the element but is still relevant to users' understanding of it or of the report
options.why: The standard names that case in terms. Even when the modification, the Emphasis of Matter or the Other Matter paragraph does not relate to the audited financial statement or element, the auditor may still deem it appropriate to refer to it in an Other Matter paragraph because he judges it relevant to users' understanding.

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 805: where the opinion on the complete set is modified or the report includes an Emphasis of Matter or Other Matter paragraph the auditor shall determine the effect on the report on the single financial statement or specific element and, when deemed appropriate, modify the opinion or include such a paragraph, and he may refer to the modification in an Other Matter paragraph even where it does not relate to the audited element

items.scenario: You have qualified your opinion on a company's complete set of financial statements over a disputed tax provision, and your report also carries an Emphasis of Matter about a fire at a warehouse. You are separately engaged on, and about to report on, a schedule of net tangible assets. Neither the tax provision nor the fire touches that schedule. Your manager says the two reports are now unrelated, since the bar in SA 705 (Revised) bites only on an adverse opinion or a disclaimer.

items.stem: What does SA 810 require?

options.text: A qualified opinion on the summary financial statements, the aggregation of two segments being material but not pervasive to the summary as a whole
options.misconception: imports the audit modification grid into an opinion which asks only whether the summary is consistent with or a fair summary of the audited financial statements, and which the standard answers with an adverse opinion when it is not
options.why: The material-but-not-pervasive grid belongs to an opinion on financial statements. The opinion here answers a single question — consistency with, or fair summary of, the audited financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria — and where the answer is no and management will not change it, the standard prescribes an adverse opinion.

options.text: The unmodified consistency opinion, with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph describing the aggregation and its effect on the segment result
options.misconception: uses a paragraph to carry a defect that makes the summary not a fair summary, which the standard answers in the opinion itself
options.why: A paragraph beside a clean opinion says the summary is a fair summary and then explains why it is not. Where the summary is not a fair summary and management will not change it, the standard requires an adverse opinion on the summary financial statements.

options.text: An adverse opinion on the summary financial statements, because they are not a fair summary of the audited financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria and management does not agree to make the necessary changes — and a similar restriction or alert must go into the report on the summary, because the report on the audited financial statements restricted distribution and alerted readers to the special purpose framework
options.why: The standard gives one answer for a summary that does not hold up and it is not a qualification. If the summary financial statements are not consistent, in all material respects, with or are not a fair summary of the audited financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria, and management does not agree to make the necessary changes, the auditor shall express an adverse opinion on the summary financial statements. Separately, where distribution or use of the report on the audited financial statements is restricted, or that report alerts readers that the statements are prepared in accordance with a special purpose framework, the auditor shall include a similar restriction or alert in the report on the summary.

options.text: Withdraw from the engagement, since a summary management refuses to correct cannot be reported on at all
options.misconception: leaves an engagement the standard tells the auditor how to finish, replacing a prescribed opinion with silence
options.why: The standard does not send the auditor away; it gives him the opinion to express. An adverse opinion on the summary tells the intended users exactly what withdrawal would leave them guessing at, which is that the summary is not a fair summary of the statements it claims to come from.

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 810: where the summary financial statements are not consistent with or are not a fair summary of the audited financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria and management does not agree to make the necessary changes, the auditor shall express an adverse opinion on the summary financial statements; and where distribution of the report on the audited financial statements is restricted or that report alerts readers to a special purpose framework, a similar restriction or alert is included in the report on the summary

items.scenario: You audited a company's financial statements under the accounting provisions of a regulator's framework; your report on them alerted readers to the special purpose framework and restricted its distribution to the regulator and the members. You are now reporting on summary financial statements derived from them. The summary aggregates two segments in a way that hides a loss in one of them, and management will not change it. The draft report on the summary says the summary is consistent in all material respects with the audited financial statements, and carries no alert or restriction of its own.

items.stem: What does the later date require the report on the summary financial statements to say?

options.text: Nothing — the auditor is not required to obtain additional evidence on the audited financial statements or to report on subsequent events, so the gap between the two dates has no reporting consequence
options.misconception: reads the rule that no additional evidence is required as removing the statement the standard requires precisely because the later date opens a gap
options.why: The two rules sit side by side and the second exists because of the first. The auditor need not go back over the audited financial statements, and for that reason the report on the summary must tell the reader that neither document reflects events after the date of the report on the audited financial statements.

options.text: That the summary financial statements and the audited financial statements do not reflect the effects of events that occurred subsequent to the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements — and the introductory paragraph must also refer to that report and its date and to the fact that an unmodified opinion was expressed, and state that the summary does not contain all the disclosures required by the framework applied in preparing the audited financial statements and that reading it is not a substitute for reading them
options.why: The colleague is right about the evidence and wrong about the consequence. Because the auditor is not required to obtain additional audit evidence on the audited financial statements or to report on the effects of events occurring after the date of his report on them, there is a month in which something could have happened and neither document would show it — so where the report on the summary is dated later, it states that the summary financial statements and the audited financial statements do not reflect the effects of events that occurred subsequent to the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements. The introductory paragraph also refers to that report, its date and the unmodified opinion, and states that the summary does not contain all the disclosures required by the framework applied in preparing the audited financial statements and that reading it is not a substitute for reading them.
keywords: do not reflect the effects of events

options.text: That subsequent events to 15 July have been examined and their effects reported, the report on the summary being dated on that day
options.misconception: reads the later date as extending the subsequent events work, when the standard says no additional evidence on the audited financial statements is required and answers the gap with a statement instead
options.why: The date of a report is not a warranty that work was done up to it. When the auditor reports on the summary after completing the audit, he is not required to obtain additional audit evidence on the audited financial statements or to report on the effects of events after the date of his report on them.

options.text: Nothing, provided the report on the summary is dated 15 June to match the report on the audited financial statements and close the gap
options.misconception: back-dates a report to avoid a statement, when the report on the summary may be dated no earlier than the date the auditor obtained sufficient appropriate evidence on the summary
options.why: The date is not the auditor's to choose. The report on the summary financial statements is dated no earlier than the date on which he obtained sufficient appropriate evidence on which to base the opinion, including evidence that the summary has been prepared and that those with the recognised authority have taken responsibility for it, and no earlier than the date of the report on the audited financial statements.

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 810: where the date of the report on the summary financial statements is later than the date of the report on the audited financial statements, the report states that the summary and the audited financial statements do not reflect the effects of events occurring subsequent to the date of that report; the introductory paragraph refers to that report, its date and the unmodified opinion and states that the summary does not contain all the disclosures required and that reading it is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements; and the report is dated no earlier than the later of the two dates

items.scenario: CA Madhur signed his report on a company's audited financial statements on 15 June, with an unmodified opinion. His report on the summary financial statements derived from them is dated 15 July. His draft identifies the summary statements, identifies the audited financial statements and expresses the consistency opinion. A colleague says the later date raises nothing, because the auditor is not required to obtain additional audit evidence on the audited financial statements or to report on the effects of events after 15 June.

items.stem: What does SA 810 require in each case?

options.text: In the first, request management to include your report in the document, and if it does not, determine and carry out other appropriate actions designed to prevent management from inappropriately associating you with the summary financial statements in that document; in the second, be satisfied that the reference to you is made in the context of your report on the audited financial statements and that the statement does not give the impression that you have reported on the summary, and if not, request management to change it or not to refer to you at all
options.why: The standard covers both directions of association. Where the auditor becomes aware that the entity plans to state that he has reported on summary financial statements in a document containing them but does not plan to include his report, he shall request management to include it, and if management does not, he shall determine and carry out other appropriate actions designed to prevent management from inappropriately associating him with the summary financial statements in that document. Where he was engaged on the financial statements but not on the summary, and the entity plans to refer to him and to the fact that the summary is derived from statements he audited, he shall be satisfied that the reference is made in the context of his report on the audited financial statements and that the statement does not give the impression that he has reported on the summary; if either is not met he requests management to change the statement or not to refer to him.

options.text: In both, withdraw the report on the audited financial statements, since the auditor cannot control how the entity refers to him
options.misconception: answers a misdescription by withdrawing an unrelated report, when the standard gives a graded set of steps ending in other appropriate actions
options.why: The report on the audited financial statements is not the problem and withdrawing it would take away information the users are entitled to. The standard asks for the report on the summary to be included, or for the statement to be changed or the reference removed, and failing those, for other appropriate actions.

options.text: In the first, issue a fresh report on the summary addressed to the readers of the booklet; in the second, accept an engagement on the summary so that the statement becomes accurate
options.misconception: reaches for a new engagement as the only remedy, when the standard's first step is to have the existing report included or the statement corrected
options.why: Engaging the auditor to report on the summary and including that report is offered by the standard as an alternative the entity may choose, not as the auditor's remedy. His steps are to request that the report be included, or that the statement be changed or the reference deleted, and then to carry out other appropriate actions.

options.text: In the first, nothing — the company may describe its own documents as it pleases, and the auditor's report exists whether or not it is reprinted; in the second, nothing either, since the statement is true
options.misconception: treats a true sentence about the auditor as harmless, when the standard is concerned with the impression the document leaves about what the auditor reported on
options.why: Each sentence may be true and still leave a reader believing the auditor gave an opinion he did not give. That is what the association requirements are for: the report goes in the document, or the reference is put in the context of the report actually given, or the reference goes.

citation.ref: Ch. Specialised Areas — SA 810: where the entity plans to state that the auditor has reported on summary financial statements without including his report, he requests management to include it and otherwise carries out actions to prevent management inappropriately associating him with them; and where he is not engaged on the summary he must be satisfied that a reference to him is made in the context of his report on the audited financial statements and does not give the impression that he has reported on the summary

items.scenario: Two things reach you about the same client. In its investor booklet the company has printed a set of summary financial statements above the line "reported on by our auditors", and it does not intend to print your report on the summary. In a second document for a different year, in which you audited the financial statements but were never engaged on any summary, the company writes that the summary figures are derived from statements audited by you, in a way that reads as though you had reported on the summary itself.

items.stem: What does SRS 4400 require?

options.text: Accept without any restriction on distribution, since a report that must be laid before a public authority is a public document and the restriction adds nothing
