A referral commission measured as a percentage of the professional fee, paid to a person who is neither a member of the Institute nor a member of any prescribed professional body, falls outside every exception the clause allows, and the fact that the referral produced genuine work does not save it.

citation.ref: First Schedule Part I, Clause (2) — commission to a person outside the permitted classes

points.text: The payments to CA Bhoomi and to the widow of the deceased partner are both permitted. The first is to a member of the Institute and the second is to the legal representative of a deceased partner, and each is named in the clause as an exception.

citation.ref: First Schedule Part I, Clause (2) — permitted payments to a member of the Institute and to the legal representative of a deceased partner

keywords: legal representative of a deceased partner

points.text: The office manager's bonus is misconduct as computed. A bonus fixed as a percentage of gross professional fees is a share in the profits of professional business allowed to a non-member; the same amount paid as salary or as a bonus not linked to the fees or profits of the practice would not offend the clause.

citation.ref: First Schedule Part I, Clause (2) — a share in the profits of professional business allowed to a non-member employee

points.text: State the consequence. A finding under a clause of Part I of the First Schedule goes before the Board of Discipline, which on holding the member guilty may reprimand him, remove his name from the Register of Members for a period not exceeding three months, or impose a fine up to the prescribed limit.

citation.ref: Section 21A — Board of Discipline and the actions open to it on a finding under the First Schedule

keywords: Part I of the First Schedule

written.scenario: Ferozepur Foods Ltd is a listed company. The engagement partner signed and dated the audit report on 26 May 2026 and released it to the company the same day. The engagement quality control reviewer completed his review on 30 May 2026 and recorded that he does not agree with the engagement team's conclusion on a ₹22 crore revenue cut-off matter; the difference is still unresolved. The reviewer had been the audit manager on this same engagement until March 2026 and was moved into the reviewer's role in April. The firm's internal manual states that the engagement quality control review "shall be completed within seven days of the signing of the report". The company's profit grew 12% during the year.
written.question: State what SQC 1 requires in these circumstances and identify each departure from it, including what should now happen to the report.

points.text: For an audit of the financial statements of a listed entity, the firm's policies and procedures must require an engagement quality control review — an objective evaluation of the significant judgements made by the engagement team and of the conclusions reached in formulating the report.

citation.ref: Engagement quality control review required for audits of the financial statements of listed entities

points.text: The review must be completed before the report is dated. Dating the report on 26 May with the review completed on 30 May reverses that order, and the firm's own manual is itself non-compliant because a policy permitting review within seven days after signing can never produce a compliant engagement.

citation.ref: Completion of the engagement quality control review before the report is dated

keywords: completed before the report is dated

points.text: The reviewer is not eligible. The reviewer must have sufficient and appropriate technical expertise and authority and must be objective, and a member of the engagement team for the period under review cannot supply that objectivity — he would be reviewing his own judgements. Moving the manager into the role in April does not cure his work on the engagement up to March.

citation.ref: Eligibility and objectivity of the engagement quality control reviewer

points.text: State the consequence. The report should not have been issued, and cannot stand on an unresolved difference — the firm's policies must require that the report is not released until the review is complete and any difference of opinion between the engagement partner and the reviewer is resolved through the firm's procedures for dealing with differences.

citation.ref: Report not to be released until the engagement quality control review is complete and differences of opinion are resolved

written.scenario: Ravindra Pharma Ltd is a listed company with revenue of ₹900 crore. Its distributors hold a contractual right to return unsold stock, and you find that the company's controls over revenue recognition are not designed to capture returns claimed after the year end at all — ₹18 crore of such returns relating to the year came to light only because you asked for the post-year-end credit notes. Management accepted the point in full and corrected the financial statements, so the financial statements as they now stand are free from material misstatement. The finance head tells you that with the numbers corrected there is nothing left for you to report, and adds that in any case the company's borrowings fell below ₹1 crore during the year, so the small company exemption from internal financial controls reporting should apply.
written.question: State your reporting obligation, the opinion you would express on internal financial controls, and how it sits alongside your opinion on the financial statements.

points.text: Identify the obligation. Under section 143(3)(i) the auditor's report must state whether the company has an adequate internal financial controls system with reference to financial statements in place and whether such controls were operating effectively. This is a separate opinion, reported alongside but distinct from the opinion on the financial statements.

citation.ref: Section 143(3)(i) — reporting on the adequacy and operating effectiveness of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements

points.text: Dispose of the exemption argument. The exemption from this reporting reaches one-person companies, small companies and private companies satisfying the prescribed turnover and borrowing thresholds. Ravindra Pharma is a listed public company and is outside the exemption altogether, so the level of its borrowings is beside the point.

citation.ref: Notification exempting one-person companies, small companies and specified private companies from reporting under section 143(3)(i)

points.text: Define a material weakness — a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal financial controls such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the company's annual financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.

citation.source: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting
citation.ref: Definition of a material weakness in internal financial controls

keywords: prevented or detected on a timely basis

points.text: Apply it. The absence of any control designed to capture post-year-end sales returns is a material weakness — an ₹18 crore misstatement of revenue was neither prevented nor detected by the company's own controls and surfaced only through the auditor's procedures, which is the very possibility the definition describes.

citation.source: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting
citation.ref: Evaluating identified control deficiencies and classifying them as material weaknesses

points.text: Answer the finance head. Correcting the numbers does not cure the control. Adequacy and operating effectiveness are assessed as at the balance sheet date, and a weakness existing on that date must be reported however completely the resulting misstatement was subsequently corrected — indeed, the correction is evidence that the control failed.

citation.source: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting
citation.ref: Assessment of internal financial controls as at the balance sheet date, notwithstanding correction of the misstatement

keywords: as at the balance sheet date

points.text: State the consequence. Where a material weakness exists as at the balance sheet date the auditor expresses an adverse opinion on internal financial controls with reference to financial statements, describing the material weakness identified, while the opinion on the financial statements themselves may remain unmodified because the misstatement was corrected. Both opinions stand independently in the same report, and the adverse controls opinion is not softened by the clean opinion beside it.

citation.source: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting
citation.ref: Adverse opinion on internal financial controls where a material weakness exists, and its independence from the opinion on the financial statements

keywords: adverse opinion on internal financial controls

written.scenario: Three weeks before the year end, Gokuldas Polymers Ltd sold a parcel of surplus land carried at ₹2 crore to a firm owned by the son-in-law of Mr Gokuldas, the managing director, for ₹2.05 crore. The consideration is receivable over thirty-six months, interest free and unsecured. The company has never sold land before and holds no other real estate for sale. The transaction is recorded in the books, and management has given you a written representation that all related party relationships and transactions have been disclosed to you. The audit committee minutes for the year record no discussion of the sale. Management says that as the price exceeds book value you should be satisfied. The company's revenue for the year was ₹610 crore.
written.question: State how you would treat this transaction in your audit, and what the absence of audit committee approval means for your reporting.

points.text: Characterise the transaction. A significant related party transaction outside the entity's normal course of business gives rise to a significant risk, and this one is outside the normal course on its face — the company has never sold land, and the counterparty is a firm owned by a close relative of the managing director.

citation.ref: Significant related party transactions outside the normal course of business treated as giving rise to a significant risk

points.text: Perform the required procedures. For an identified significant related party transaction outside the normal course of business, inspect the underlying contracts or agreements and evaluate whether the business rationale, or the absence of one, suggests the transaction was entered into to engage in fraudulent financial reporting or to conceal a misappropriation of assets.

citation.ref: Inspecting the underlying contracts and evaluating the business rationale of a significant related party transaction outside the normal course of business

keywords: outside the normal course of business

points.text: Answer management's argument. Also evaluate whether the terms are consistent with management's explanations and whether the transaction has been appropriately accounted for and disclosed. A headline price ₹5 lakh above book value does not answer the terms — the value has moved in the thirty-six months of interest-free unsecured credit, which is where the substance of the transaction sits.

citation.ref: Evaluating whether the terms of a related party transaction are consistent with management's explanations, and its accounting and disclosure

keywords: terms are consistent with management's explanations

points.text: Do not stop at the representation. A written representation from management on the completeness of related party relationships and transactions is a necessary but not a sufficient source — it does not by itself provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the matter it addresses.

citation.ref: Written representations are not by themselves sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the matters they address

keywords: completeness of related party relationships and transactions

points.text: Identify the statutory breach. A related party transaction that is not in the ordinary course of business, or not on an arm's length basis, requires the prior approval of the audit committee and of the Board, and disclosure in the Board's report together with the justification for entering into it. None of that has happened here.

citation.ref: Section 188 read with section 177(4)(iv) — approval of related party transactions by the audit committee and the Board, and disclosure in the Board's report

keywords: prior approval of the audit committee

points.text: State the consequence. The want of approval is an identified non-compliance with law — communicate it to those charged with governance, consider its effect on the financial statements and on the risk assessment, and modify the opinion where the related party transaction and its terms are not adequately disclosed in the financial statements.

citation.ref: Reporting identified non-compliance to those charged with governance and considering its effect on the auditor's report

written.scenario: Bharat Hydel Ltd is an unlisted company in which the Central Government holds 62% of the paid-up share capital. Its board proposes to appoint Mehta & Associates as statutory auditors by a resolution at the annual general meeting, and its finance director says the Comptroller and Auditor General "has no role once a chartered accountant firm is signing the report". After the audit report is issued, a team from the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General visits and raises a finding that a township was built beside a dam site at a cost of ₹48 crore, with every tender and sanction in order, but stands empty two years after completion because the plant was commissioned elsewhere.
written.question: Comment on the finance director's view, state what the Comptroller and Auditor General may do before and after Mehta & Associates report, and identify the kind of audit the township finding belongs to and why.

points.text: Bharat Hydel Ltd is a government company under section 2(45): not less than 51% of its paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, and listing or the lack of it is irrelevant. Its statutory auditor is therefore appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General under section 139(5), not by the members at the annual general meeting, so the board's proposal is not the road.

citation.ref: Section 2(45) — government company at 51%; section 139(5) — auditor appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General

points.text: The finance director is wrong. Under section 143(5) the Comptroller and Auditor General directs the manner in which the accounts are to be audited, and the auditor's report must include those directions, the action taken on them and their impact on the accounts and financial statements.

citation.ref: Section 143(5) — directions of the Comptroller and Auditor General and their reporting by the statutory auditor

points.text: After the report is issued, the Comptroller and Auditor General may comment upon or supplement the statutory auditor's report, conduct a supplementary audit of the company's financial statements, and order a test audit of its accounts where considered necessary; the comments are placed before the annual general meeting with the audit report.

citation.ref: Section 143(6) and 143(7) — supplementary audit, comment upon the report, and test audit

points.text: The township finding is propriety audit: verification of transactions on the tests of public interest, commonly accepted customs and standards of conduct, which brings out improper, avoidable or infructuous expenditure even though the expenditure conformed to every rule and regulation — the module's own example is a building constructed and not used for its purpose. Regularity audit would have passed it; propriety audit asks whether an officer showed the vigilance a person of ordinary prudence shows with his own money.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings
citation.ref: Propriety audit — tests of public interest and standards of conduct; wasteful expenditure within the rules

points.text: Such a finding typically arises from a comprehensive audit, the efficiency-cum- performance appraisal the Comptroller and Auditor General conducts through Audit Boards over areas the professional auditors do not cover — investment decisions, project formulation, capacity utilisation and capital cost against approved cost — and it is reported to the legislature, not to the shareholders.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings
citation.ref: Comprehensive audit through Audit Boards — project cost, capacity utilisation and investment decisions

written.scenario: Rao & Rao are auditors of Cascade Foods Ltd, which acquired 70% of Nimbus Snacks Ltd on 1 October 2025 and holds 40% of a joint venture in Dubai that reports under IFRS and is audited by a Dubai firm. Nimbus is audited by another Indian firm and accounts for 35% of group assets and 28% of group revenue. Cascade's chief financial officer proposes to skip consolidation this year because "the Nimbus stake may be sold within eighteen months", and asks Rao & Rao to accept the Dubai firm's IFRS numbers as they stand. Nimbus sold goods to Cascade during the year at a margin, and a third of them remain in Cascade's closing stock.
written.question: Advise Rao & Rao on whether consolidation can be skipped, how they set materiality and deal with the two components, what they verify on the acquisition and the stock, and how their report refers to work done by the other auditors.

points.text: Consolidation cannot be skipped. Under section 129(3) a company with one or more subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures prepares consolidated financial statements in addition to its own, in the same form and manner, lays them before the annual general meeting with the standalone statements and attaches the salient features of each subsidiary in Form AOC-1; the Ind AS framework gives no exemption for control that is intended to be temporary.

citation.ref: Section 129(3) and 129(4) with Form AOC-1 — consolidation is mandatory; no temporary-control exemption under Ind AS 110

points.text: Rao & Rao compute materiality for the group as a whole and use it to assess the consolidation adjustments and to decide whether Nimbus and the Dubai venture are material to the group; they also compute component materiality and communicate it to the component auditors where needed for a true and fair view of the consolidated statements, and obtain confirmations from them on independence and the information needed for consolidation.

citation.source: SA 600 with ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Materiality for the group as a whole; component materiality communicated to component auditors

points.text: The Dubai numbers cannot be taken as they stand: where a component reports under a framework different from the parent's, management converts the component's audited statements to the group framework, and the conversion adjustments are audited by the principal auditor to ensure the component's information is suitable for consolidation.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Component reporting under a framework different from the parent's — conversion adjustments audited by the principal auditor

points.text: The Nimbus acquisition gives rise to permanent consolidation adjustments, made on the first occasion and when the shareholding changes: goodwill or capital reserve and the equity attributable to non-controlling interests, with attention to pre-acquisition reserves. The unsold stock gives rise to a current period consolidation adjustment: elimination of intra-group sales and of the unrealised profit in the third still held, with the related deferred tax.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Permanent consolidation adjustments on acquisition; current period adjustments eliminating intra-group profit

points.text: Where Rao & Rao rely on the other auditors, the report on the consolidated statements discloses the magnitude of the portion audited by others — the aggregate amounts or percentages of total assets, revenues and cash flows of those components, stated before consolidation adjustments — in an Other Matter paragraph; the reference is a statement of divided responsibility, not a qualification.

citation.source: SA 600 and SA 706 with ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Reference to other auditors — magnitude of assets, revenues and cash flows before consolidation adjustments; divided responsibility, not a qualification

written.scenario: Pallavi, a practising chartered accountant, is asked by Trident Logistics Pvt Ltd to "review" its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 for submission to a bank, which has written that it requires audited financial statements. Trident's management also says the vehicle-fleet ledger will not be made available "as it is with the transport consultant". Pallavi is separately engaged to review a sister company, Trident Warehousing Pvt Ltd, where her inquiries and analytical procedures show that rentals from a warehouse sold in December 2025 have been recognised for the full year, an overstatement she considers material but confined to one line, and where the company's bank has recalled its term loan.
written.question: Should Pallavi accept the Trident Logistics engagement? For Trident Warehousing, state the nature of the assurance she gives, what she must do about the loan recall, and how her conclusion is worded.

points.text: Pallavi should decline Trident Logistics. SRE 2400 bars accepting a review where there is no rational purpose — a review intended to meet a requirement of law or a lender that calls for audited statements has none — and where management imposes a limitation on scope, here the withheld fleet ledger, such that a disclaimer of conclusion is likely. She may recommend an audit instead.

citation.ref: Acceptance of a review engagement — no rational purpose, and a scope limitation likely to lead to a disclaimer of conclusion

points.text: A review is a limited assurance engagement: Pallavi obtains assurance lower than an audit, primarily by inquiry and analytical procedures, and her conclusion is expressed negatively — whether anything has come to her attention that causes her to believe the financial statements are not prepared in accordance with the framework.

citation.ref: Limited assurance through inquiry and analytical procedures; negative form of conclusion

points.text: The loan recall is an event that may cast significant doubt on going concern, so she must inquire of management about its plans, their feasibility and whether management believes they will improve the position, evaluate the responses as a basis for continuing the going concern presentation or for concluding the statements are misstated or misleading, and consider them against everything else the review has told her.

citation.ref: Going concern in a review — inquiry into management's plans, their feasibility, and evaluation of the responses

points.text: The rental overstatement is a material misstatement that is not pervasive, so she gives a qualified conclusion under the heading "Qualified Conclusion" with a "Basis for Qualified Conclusion" paragraph: "except for the effects of the matter described", nothing has come to her attention. An adverse conclusion is reserved for a misstatement that is both material and pervasive.

citation.ref: Modified conclusions — qualified when material but not pervasive, adverse when material and pervasive; required headings and wording

written.scenario: A private equity investor engages Kabir, a practising chartered accountant, to check whether the trade receivables of Sunbeam Retail Pvt Ltd at 31 March 2026 agree to confirmations from its twenty largest customers and to report the differences. Kabir's firm has been Sunbeam's internal auditor for three years. The investor's covering letter says it will "rely on Kabir's assurance that the receivables are fairly stated" and will circulate the report to its co-investors. Separately, Kabir compiles the financial statements of a partnership, Sunbeam Traders, from its records; on reading the compiled statements he sees that a ₹1.2 crore loan repayable in six months is shown as a long-term liability, and the partners refuse to change it.
written.question: Explain what Kabir's receivables engagement is, what he must settle in its terms and say in his report, and what he does about the loan classification in the compilation.

points.text: The receivables engagement is an agreed-upon procedures engagement under SRS 4400: Kabir performs the procedures the investor has agreed and reports his factual findings, and no assurance is expressed — the users draw their own conclusions from the findings. He must correct the investor's letter before accepting, because the engagement cannot be relied on as assurance that the receivables are fairly stated.

citation.ref: Agreed-upon procedures — a report of factual findings, no assurance expressed, users draw their own conclusions

points.text: Independence is not a requirement of an agreed-upon procedures engagement, so the internal audit relationship does not bar Kabir; but where the auditor is not independent, a statement to that effect is made in the report of factual findings. The terms must record that the procedures do not constitute an audit or a review and that no assurance will be expressed, and the limitation on distribution of the report, which the investor's plan to circulate it to co-investors makes essential to settle in advance.

citation.ref: Independence not required but disclosed; terms record no assurance and any restriction on distribution

points.text: The report of factual findings identifies the information the procedures were applied to and the purpose, states that the procedures were those agreed with the recipient and performed under the Standard, lists the procedures, describes the findings with sufficient detail of errors and exceptions, states that the procedures do not constitute an audit or review and no assurance is expressed, and that had additional procedures, an audit or a review been performed other matters might have come to light.

citation.ref: Contents of the report of factual findings

keywords: other matters might have come to light

points.text: In the compilation under SRS 4410, on reading the compiled statements Kabir has become aware that amendments are required for them not to be materially misstated, so he proposes the reclassification; when the partners decline, he withdraws from the engagement and informs management and those charged with governance of the reasons — the compiled information must not go out misleading under his name.

citation.ref: Compilation — proposing amendments, and withdrawal when management declines them

written.scenario: Three companies ask whether they must appoint an internal auditor for the financial year 2026-27. Orchid Textiles Pvt Ltd had a turnover of ₹185 crore in 2025-26 and outstanding bank borrowings that touched ₹104 crore for one week in November 2025 before being repaid. Lotus Foods Ltd, an unlisted public company, has paid-up capital of ₹22 crore, turnover of ₹150 crore and accepted deposits of ₹26 crore at one point during 2025-26. Marigold Pvt Ltd had a turnover of ₹140 crore and borrowings of ₹60 crore. Lotus Foods also asks what its internal auditor does about findings from last year's audits that management has not acted on.
written.question: Advise each company under section 138 read with Rule 13, state the time allowed to comply, and describe the internal auditor's responsibility for prior audit issues.

points.text: Orchid Textiles Pvt Ltd must appoint an internal auditor: a private company is covered where turnover is ₹200 crore or more in the preceding financial year, or outstanding loans or borrowings from banks or public financial institutions exceed ₹100 crore at any point of time during that year — and one week at ₹104 crore is a point of time.

citation.ref: Section 138 and Rule 13(1)(c) — private company, borrowings exceeding ₹100 crore at any point of time

points.text: Lotus Foods Ltd must appoint one: an unlisted public company is covered where paid-up capital is ₹50 crore or more, or turnover ₹200 crore or more, or borrowings exceed ₹100 crore, or outstanding deposits are ₹25 crore or more at any point of time during the preceding year, and deposits of ₹26 crore meet the last test though the other three fail. Marigold Pvt Ltd is outside every threshold and need not appoint one.

citation.ref: Section 138 and Rule 13(1)(b) — unlisted public company thresholds; each test stands alone

points.text: The internal auditor may be an individual, a partnership firm or a body corporate, and an existing company that comes within the criteria must comply within six months of the applicability commencing.

citation.ref: Rule 13 — who may be internal auditor and the six-month period to comply

points.text: Under SIA 390 the Chief Internal Auditor continuously monitors the closure of prior audit issues through a formal monitoring process agreed with management and those charged with governance, reports open and pending matters in an Action Taken Report, and where management has not acted within a reasonable time draws its attention to it and ascertains the reasons; implementing the action plans remains management's responsibility.

citation.source: SIA 390 — Monitoring and Reporting of Prior Audit Issues
citation.ref: The Chief Internal Auditor's monitoring, the Action Taken Report, and management's responsibility to implement

written.scenario: Iyer & Co are the statutory auditors of Meridian Polymers Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026. Because the company could not produce records for a fire-damaged plant that holds most of its operations, Iyer & Co have disclaimed an opinion on the complete set of financial statements. The company's lender now asks Iyer & Co, under a separate engagement, for an audit report on the balance sheet alone, and a bank guarantee counterparty asks for an audit report on the schedule of trade receivables, which is a small part of the statements and was fully verified. The company also wants Iyer & Co to report on summary financial statements it intends to publish in a newspaper, prepared on criteria the finance team has devised, with a statement that the summary "has been audited in accordance with the Standards on Auditing".
written.question: Advise Iyer & Co on each of the three requests, stating what they may report and what each report must say.

points.text: The balance sheet alone: Iyer & Co cannot express an unmodified opinion on a single financial statement of a complete set on which they have disclaimed an opinion, even in a report that is not published with the disclaimer, because a single financial statement is deemed to constitute a major portion of the complete set and an unmodified opinion would contradict the disclaimer.

citation.ref: No unmodified opinion on a single financial statement where the complete set carries an adverse opinion or disclaimer

points.text: The receivables schedule: an unmodified opinion on a specific element may be given despite the disclaimer on the whole only if law or regulation does not prohibit it, the opinion is expressed in a report not published together with the report containing the disclaimer, and the element does not constitute a major portion of the complete set — a small, fully verified receivables schedule meets the third test, so Iyer & Co may report on it in a separate report.

citation.ref: The three conditions for an unmodified opinion on a specific element when the complete set is adverse or disclaimed

points.text: Each engagement gets a separate opinion, and where the element report is published with the complete set the presentation must differentiate the element sufficiently and the opinion must be differentiated from the opinion on the complete set; Iyer & Co do not issue the element report until satisfied with the differentiation, and they consider whether to refer to the disclaimer in an Other Matter paragraph because it is relevant to users of the element report.

citation.ref: Separate opinion for each engagement; differentiation of presentation and opinion; Other Matter reference to the modification

points.text: The summary statements: before accepting, Iyer & Co determine whether the applied criteria are acceptable — criteria devised by management are judged by the nature of the entity, the purpose, the users' needs and whether the summary would be misleading — and obtain management's acknowledgement of its responsibility; if the criteria are unacceptable they do not accept the engagement unless law requires it, and even then the report must not say the engagement was conducted under SA 810.

citation.ref: Acceptance — acceptability of the applied criteria and management's acknowledgement; refusal where unacceptable

points.text: Because the report on the audited statements is a disclaimer, any report on the summary must state that the audit report contains a disclaimer of opinion, describe the basis for it, and state that as a result it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the summary financial statements; the proposed line that the summary "has been audited" cannot stand, since summary statements are reported on for consistency with the audited statements, not audited.

citation.ref: Report on summary financial statements when the audit report is adverse or a disclaimer — the three additional statements

written.scenario: Solaris Cold Chain Pvt Ltd asks Nair & Nair to examine a five-year statement of profits and cash flows for a bank loan. Years one and two are built on management's expectations of current contracts; years three to five assume a government subsidy that has not been announced and a doubling of warehouse capacity for which no land has been identified. The statement does not say which assumptions are which. Management also proposes that the report describe the figures as "verified and certain". Separately, Solaris outsources its entire payroll to a service organisation and its auditor asks whether a report describing the service organisation's controls as at 31 March 2026 is enough to rely on for the whole year.
written.question: Explain how Nair & Nair classify the information, what they must obtain evidence on, when they refuse or withdraw, how their opinion is worded and modified, and which service auditor's report Solaris's auditor should ask for.

points.text: Years one and two are a forecast — prospective financial information on best-estimate assumptions about events management expects to occur — while years three to five are a projection built on hypothetical assumptions about events not necessarily expected to occur; the statement is a combination, and SAE 3400 requires a clear indication of which assumptions are best-estimate and which are hypothetical, which is missing.

citation.ref: Forecast on best-estimate assumptions; projection on hypothetical assumptions; disclosure of which is which

points.text: Nair & Nair obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that the best-estimate assumptions are not unreasonable and the hypothetical assumptions are consistent with the purpose, that the information is properly prepared on the basis of the assumptions, that it is properly presented with all material assumptions adequately disclosed, and that it is prepared on a basis consistent with the historical financial statements using appropriate accounting principles.

citation.ref: The four matters on which evidence is obtained in an examination of prospective financial information

points.text: They should not accept, or should withdraw from, the engagement where the assumptions are clearly unrealistic or the information will be inappropriate for its intended use; an unannounced subsidy and capacity with no land are to be tested against that bar. The report can never say "verified and certain": it gives an opinion on whether the information is properly prepared on the basis of the assumptions and presented under the framework, with caveats on achievability, and the auditor does not vouch for the accuracy of a forecast.

citation.ref: Refusal or withdrawal where assumptions are clearly unrealistic; opinion on preparation and presentation with caveats on achievability

keywords: properly prepared on the basis of the assumptions

points.text: Where presentation or disclosure is inadequate, a qualified or adverse opinion or withdrawal; where a significant assumption gives no reasonable basis, an adverse opinion setting out the reasons or withdrawal; where conditions preclude a necessary procedure, withdrawal or a disclaimer describing the scope limitation.

citation.ref: Modified reports — inadequate disclosure, unreasonable assumptions, scope limitation

points.text: A report on the description and design of controls as at a date is a type 1 report; to rely on the payroll controls for the year Solaris's auditor should ask for a type 2 report, which adds the service organisation's assertion and the service auditor's reasonable assurance that the controls operated effectively throughout the specified period, with a description of the tests of controls and their results — and it must consider the complementary user entity controls the report says Solaris itself must operate for the control objectives to be met.

citation.ref: Type 1 against type 2 reports; operating effectiveness throughout the period; complementary user entity controls

written.scenario: Verma & Associates are auditing Quantum Retail Ltd, whose enterprise system approves purchase orders through a workflow, computes straight-line depreciation, posts a nightly interface from the point-of-sale sub-ledger to the general ledger, and produces the customer ageing report the credit team uses for its monthly review. During the year the IT head, who also writes program changes, moved changes straight into production, and three employees who left in October 2025 still had live system access in March 2026. The audit is being conducted remotely, and a junior proposes to take screenshots of the auditee's screens during video calls as evidence.
written.question: Identify the IT dependencies in this system, state how Verma & Associates respond to the two control failures, and advise on the screenshot proposal and the other safeguards a remote audit needs.

points.text: IT dependencies arise where IT initiates, authorises, records, processes or reports financial data, and the module names five types, all present here: an automated control (workflow approval of purchase orders), a calculation (straight-line depreciation), an interface (point-of-sale sub-ledger to general ledger), a system-generated report (the customer ageing used in a manual control), and security including segregation of duties enforced by the system.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: The five types of IT dependency — automated controls, reports, calculations, security, interfaces

points.text: Because dependencies exist, Verma & Associates scope in the general IT controls: access security, program change and data centre and network operations. The IT head moving his own changes to production breaks the program change objective — segregated development, testing and production, changes tested and approved before migration, developer and implementer separated — and the live access of leavers breaks the access security objective that access of terminated users is removed on a timely basis.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: General IT controls — access security, program change, data centre and network operations, and their control objectives

points.text: Where general IT controls are not implemented or not operating effectively they cannot be relied on, which means the IT dependencies cannot be relied on: the automated approval, the depreciation calculation, the interface and the ageing report must then be addressed by other means — direct testing of the report's completeness and accuracy and substantive procedures over the affected balances — rather than by reliance on the system.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: Ineffective general IT controls mean the IT dependencies cannot be relied upon

points.text: The screenshot proposal is refused: auditors should not take screenshots of auditees as evidence, and screenshots of documents or records need the audited organisation's prior authorisation. The remote audit also needs a restricted, encrypted document sharing platform with material removed after review and archived, a VPN for any access to the auditee's system, agreements on recording, and a documented assessment for each audit that remote means are sufficient to achieve the audit objectives.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: Remote audit — confidentiality, security and data protection, and the risk assessment of whether remote means suffice

written.scenario: Aurora Textiles Ltd, a listed company within the top 1000 by market capitalisation, is preparing its first Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report. Its sustainability head proposes to report only the disclosures marked leadership, "since those show us in the best light", to leave out anything about the dyeing contractors in its supply chain, and to describe the report as "audited" on the strength of an internal review. The board asks the statutory auditor, Sen & Sen, whether they can give assurance on the report and under which standard.
written.question: Advise Aurora on the structure and content of the report, the treatment of the contractors, the word "audited", and the standard and level of assurance Sen & Sen can provide.

points.text: The BRSR seeks disclosures on performance against the nine principles of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct, categorised two in environment, three in social and four in governance; under each principle the essential indicators are mandatory and the leadership indicators voluntary, so the proposal to report only leadership indicators inverts the rule — the essentials must be reported and the leadership indicators are what the company should endeavour to add.

citation.source: SEBI Listing Regulations with ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — SDGs and ESG Assurance
citation.ref: BRSR — nine NGRBC principles, two-three-four across E, S and G; essential indicators mandatory, leadership voluntary

points.text: The contractors cannot be left out: the principles reach the value chain — the governing structure should encourage entities in the value chain to adopt them, the company responds to outside entities such as suppliers and sub-contractors that violate them, and the well-being principle covers employees including those in the value chain — so the dyeing contractors' conditions belong in the report.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — SDGs and ESG Assurance
citation.ref: Principle 1 core elements and Principle 3 — the value chain, suppliers and sub-contractors

points.text: An internal review is not an audit and the report cannot be called audited on its strength; assurance on sustainability information is an engagement under ICAI's Standard on Sustainability Assurance Engagements, SSAE 3000, which provides reasonable or limited assurance, and the level obtained is what the report may claim.

citation.source: SSAE 3000 — Assurance Engagements on Sustainability Information
citation.ref: Assurance on sustainability information at reasonable or limited level; an internal review is neither

points.text: SSAE 3000 applied voluntarily to assurance reports covering periods ending 31 March 2023 and is mandatory for periods ending on or after 31 March 2024, so Sen & Sen's engagement for 2025-26 is under it, with SSAE 3410 for any greenhouse gas statement; the engagement follows a methodology of reviewing responses, an on-site assessment, submission of findings and an assessment report, and Sen & Sen must first consider independence and competence for a subject matter outside financial reporting.

citation.ref: Effective dates — voluntary for periods ending 31 March 2023, mandatory on or after 31 March 2024; greenhouse gas statements under SSAE 3410

written.scenario: Lalita & Co are the statutory auditors of Kaveri Agro Ltd. The company's lender, under a loan agreement, requires a separate set of financial statements for the same year prepared on the accounting provisions written into the agreement, which among other things require receivables to be provided for at 50% once ninety days overdue, far more prudently than Ind AS would. The agreement also states that misstatements below ₹10 lakh need not be corrected. The finance director asks Lalita & Co to audit these statements, says that materiality "is settled by the ₹10 lakh clause", and expects a standard audit report. CA Lalita plans to mention in an Other Matter paragraph that the statements follow the loan agreement.
written.question: Advise Lalita & Co on accepting the engagement, on materiality, and on what their report must contain that a general purpose report would not, and say whether CA Lalita's Other Matter plan is right.

points.text: The statements are prepared under a special purpose framework: the financial reporting provisions of a contract, one of SA 800's three examples, designed to meet the financial information needs of specific users, here the lender. Acceptance turns on whether the framework is acceptable under SA 210, judged by whether it exhibits the attributes normally exhibited by acceptable frameworks, with the relative importance of each attribute a matter of professional judgment. A framework that is not neutral, like very prudent provisions agreed between the parties for their own needs, can still be acceptable for the specific users' purpose.

citation.ref: Definition of special purpose framework; considerations when accepting the engagement, with SA 210

points.text: Materiality is judged by the financial information needs of the intended users, not the common needs of users as a group as in a general purpose audit. The ₹10 lakh clause is a threshold management has agreed with the intended users below which identified misstatements will not be corrected; the existence of such a threshold does not relieve the auditor from the requirement to determine materiality in accordance with SA 320 for planning and performing the audit. The finance director is wrong to say materiality is settled by the clause.

citation.ref: Considerations when planning and performing the audit — SA 320 and an agreed correction threshold

points.text: The report applies SA 700 (Revised) with additions. It must describe the purpose for which the financial statements are prepared and, if necessary, the intended users, or refer to a note that does, and evaluate whether the statements adequately describe any significant interpretations of the contract on which they are based. Where management had a choice of frameworks, the description of management's responsibility must also refer to its responsibility for determining that the applicable framework is acceptable in the circumstances.

citation.ref: Description of the applicable financial reporting framework; the auditor's report on special purpose financial statements

keywords: purpose for which the financial statements are prepared
responsibility for determining that the applicable framework is acceptable

points.text: The report must alert readers that the statements are prepared in accordance with a special purpose framework and, as a result, may not be suitable for another purpose; that alert is an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, not an Other Matter paragraph, because it draws attention to the basis of accounting disclosed in the statements. CA Lalita's plan is therefore wrong in form. She may go further and restrict the distribution or use of the report to the specific users, by expanding that paragraph and modifying its heading, which is what a report on loan-agreement statements needs so that it is not relied on by anyone else.

citation.ref: Alerting readers that the financial statements are prepared in accordance with a special purpose framework; restriction on distribution or use

keywords: may not be suitable for another purpose

written.scenario: CA Kabir is engaged by Meghdoot Traders, a partnership, to compile its financial statements from the ledgers its accountant keeps. He also acts as the firm's tax adviser and holds a small loan from one partner. Midway, he finds that the sales ledger does not reconcile to the bank statements by ₹18 lakh, asks for the missing invoices and receives none. The compiled figures also carry a loan from a partner described as a bank overdraft, and the partners refuse to relabel it, saying "nobody reads the notes". They then ask Kabir to state in his report that the statements are "free of material misstatement".
written.question: State whether Kabir may accept the engagement given his other roles, what he must do about the ₹18 lakh and the mislabelled loan, and what his report may and may not say.

points.text: Kabir may accept. A compilation engagement is a non-assurance engagement, so independence requirements do not apply to it, though he must still comply with the relevant ethical requirements of the Code and identify and address threats to that compliance, and any law or regulation that requires disclosure of the relationship. He must first agree the terms in an engagement letter, covering the intended use and distribution, the applicable framework, the scope, his and management's responsibilities, and the expected form of his report.

citation.ref: Ethical requirements — independence not required in a non-assurance engagement; engagement acceptance and the terms of engagement

points.text: On the ₹18 lakh, the information provided is incomplete or inaccurate. Kabir must bring that to management's attention and request the additional or corrected information; if he is unable to complete the engagement because management has failed to provide the records, documents or explanations requested, he must withdraw and inform management and those charged with governance of the reasons.

citation.ref: Performing the engagement — incomplete, inaccurate or unsatisfactory information; withdrawal where management fails to provide information

keywords: request the additional or corrected information
inform management and those charged with governance

points.text: On the mislabelled loan, having read the compiled information in the light of his understanding of the business and the framework, Kabir must propose the amendment needed for the information not to be misleading. If management declines or does not permit the amendment, he must withdraw from the engagement and inform management and those charged with governance why; if withdrawal is not possible, he determines his professional and legal responsibilities. He must also obtain an acknowledgement that management has taken responsibility for the final version of the compiled information.

citation.ref: Performing the engagement — proposing amendments, withdrawal where management declines, acknowledgement of responsibility

points.text: The report is not a vehicle to express an opinion or conclusion in any form, so Kabir cannot state that the statements are free of material misstatement. It must state that he compiled the information based on information provided by management, describe management's and his own responsibilities, identify the framework and the information, and explain that because a compilation is not an assurance engagement he was not required to verify the accuracy or completeness of the information and accordingly expresses no audit opinion or review conclusion.

citation.ref: The practitioner's report — elements, and the explanation that no opinion or conclusion is expressed

keywords: not a vehicle to express an opinion
not required to verify the accuracy or completeness
no audit opinion or review conclusion

written.scenario: Pallavi & Associates are the statutory auditors of Trident Warehousing Ltd, a listed company, and are engaged to review its half-yearly results under SRE 2410. The junior proposes confirming the top twenty receivables "to be safe". Management declines to give access to the minutes of the last two board meetings, saying they concern a confidential acquisition. Separately, a lender has recalled a ₹40 crore loan since the year end and the draft results say nothing about it. Management later publishes the results in the newspaper with the words "reviewed by the auditors" but leaves the review report out.
written.question: State the assurance Pallavi & Associates give and whether the junior's proposal fits it, what they do about the minutes, how the loan recall is reported if disclosed and if not, and what they do about the newspaper publication.

points.text: A review of interim financial information gives a conclusion whether anything has come to the auditor's attention that causes the auditor to believe the information is not prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the framework, reducing to a moderate level the risk of an inappropriate conclusion. It consists of inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters, and analytical and other review procedures; it ordinarily does not require tests of the accounting records through inspection, observation or confirmation. The junior's confirmations are audit procedures, not review procedures, and are not required.

citation.ref: Objective of an engagement to review interim financial information; inquiries, analytical and other review procedures

keywords: does not require tests of the accounting records

points.text: Reading the minutes of meetings of those charged with governance is one of the procedures the auditor ordinarily performs. Refusing access is a limitation on scope imposed by management; Pallavi & Associates request its removal, and if management refuses they are unable to complete the review and express a conclusion, and communicate in writing to management and those charged with governance why. Because a listed company's results require a review report, they issue one that disclaims a conclusion and gives the reason the review could not be completed, still communicating any matter that indicates a material adjustment is necessary.

citation.ref: Limitation on scope imposed by management; disclaiming a conclusion where a report is required

keywords: limitation on scope imposed by management

points.text: The loan recall is an event that may cast significant doubt on going concern. If management makes adequate disclosure of the material uncertainty in the interim information, the review report is modified by adding an emphasis of matter paragraph. If the uncertainty is not adequately disclosed, Pallavi & Associates express a qualified or adverse conclusion as appropriate, and the report refers specifically to the material uncertainty. Their written representations must also cover subsequent events and management's belief that uncorrected misstatements are immaterial.

citation.ref: Going concern and significant uncertainties; departure from the applicable framework; management representations

points.text: The terms of engagement include management's agreement that a document stating the interim information has been reviewed will also include the review report. Where management publishes without it, and especially where the report was modified, Pallavi & Associates consider seeking legal advice on the appropriate course of action and the possibility of resigning from the appointment to audit the annual financial statements. Their review report itself carries a UDIN, since a review is an assurance engagement.

citation.ref: Other considerations — document omitting the review report; reporting, including UDIN

written.scenario: Bansi Retail Ltd has outsourced its payroll and the remittance of statutory dues to Payline Services, which processes payroll for two hundred companies. Bansi's auditors want assurance on the design and operating effectiveness of Payline's controls over the year, not merely as at a date. Payline engages CA Nair, who has never reported on a service organisation, to give the report. Payline proposes to write the description of its system on criteria it has devised and not shared, to leave out the controls over remittance because "that is only a compliance matter", and to have its internal audit team do the testing. Separately, Bansi is issuing a prospectus and asks Nair to compile the pro forma information showing the effect of a recent acquisition.
written.question: State which type of report Bansi's auditors need and what it contains, what Nair must settle before accepting and on the three proposals, and what her responsibility is on the pro forma information.

points.text: Bansi's auditors need a type 2 report: a report on the description, design and operating effectiveness of controls throughout the specified period. It comprises the service organisation's description of its system, its written assertion that the description fairly presents the system as designed and implemented throughout the period, that the controls were suitably designed and that they operated effectively throughout the period, and the service auditor's assurance report conveying reasonable assurance on those matters and including a description of the tests of controls and their results. A type 1 report speaks only as at a specified date and says nothing about operating effectiveness.

citation.ref: Type 1 and type 2 reports — contents; objectives of the service auditor

points.text: Before accepting, Nair must ensure she has the capabilities and competence for the engagement; her inexperience is a matter to address, not a bar. She must be satisfied that the criteria the service organisation will use to prepare its description will be suitable and available to user entities and their auditors, so undisclosed home-made criteria are not acceptable; and that the scope and the description will not be so limited that they are unlikely to be useful to user entities. Controls over remittance of statutory dues are relevant to Bansi's financial reporting, since late remittance creates interest and penalty liabilities, so leaving them out limits the description in exactly that way.

citation.ref: Acceptance — capabilities and competence, suitable criteria available to user entities, scope not so limited as to be useless; why service organisation controls matter to a user entity

keywords: suitable and available to user entities

points.text: Nair, not Payline's internal audit, tests the controls. For a type 2 report she must test those controls she determines are necessary to achieve the control objectives and assess their operating effectiveness throughout the period. Where the service organisation has an internal audit function she obtains an understanding of its responsibilities and activities to decide whether its specific work can be used, but the assessment and the report remain hers. She also requests written representations that reaffirm the assertion, confirm that all relevant information and access were provided, and disclose any non-compliance, fraud or uncorrected deviations that may affect user entities.

citation.ref: Obtaining evidence regarding operating effectiveness; understanding the internal audit function; written representations

points.text: On the pro forma information Nair does not compile anything; that responsibility rests with the responsible party. Under SAE 3420 her sole responsibility is to report, with reasonable assurance, on whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, by the responsible party on the basis of the applicable criteria, after satisfying herself that the criteria are suitable and that the information is unlikely to be misleading for its purpose.

citation.ref: Nature of the practitioner's responsibility; engagement acceptance

written.scenario: Verma & Associates audit Nimbus Logistics Ltd, whose general ledger holds twelve million lines, more than a spreadsheet can open. Freight revenue is computed by the system from rate cards; the auditors suspect the rates were not updated when a customer addendum was signed. Sales are booked round the clock through an online portal. The company has also begun using an artificial intelligence model to approve customer credit limits and is piloting a blockchain-based consignment register shared with its partners. The engagement partner asks for a plan that uses CAATs, and for the audit implications of the two new technologies.
written.question: Set out how CAATs are used on the ledger, the revenue and the sales timing, naming the kind of tool for each, and state what the auditors must consider on the AI credit model and the blockchain register.

points.text: On the ledger, a data extraction and analysis tool such as ACL is used to check the complete data set: reconciling the general ledger dump to the system trial balance, proving completeness by record count, sum and pivot on a population that exceeds the capacity of a spreadsheet, and sampling for irregularities or patterns that could indicate control weaknesses or fraud.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: Emerging technologies in audit — data analytics and CAATs; ACL

points.text: On revenue, a workflow tool such as Alteryx is used to recompute every revenue entry from the rate cards and compare with the recorded figures, which is how the module's own logistics case found revenue understated because an addendum had not been revised in the system and old rates were used. Every step leaves a transparent audit trail in the workflow, and no coding is needed.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: Emerging technologies in audit — Alteryx and the logistics recomputation case

points.text: On sales timing, a visualisation tool such as Power BI is used to find outliers in the population and analyse trends, which in the module's apparel case surfaced sales transactions performed during non-business hours; the same dashboard serves to report findings interactively to management. A platform such as CaseWare then holds the audit, review and compilation workflow and links to client data consistently.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: Emerging technologies in audit — Power BI outliers and non-business-hours sales; CaseWare

points.text: On the AI credit model, because algorithms are invisible the audit focuses on the logical flow of the process: whether unintended bias has been added to the algorithm, whether its output is appropriately reviewed and approved, whether the AI is making decisions or management is using it as part of decision-making, how it affects the flows of transactions and reports management relies on, and, since AI is software, its cybersecurity, bugs and vulnerabilities. Where management has shifted its oversight onto the AI, the auditors understand what shifted and whether existing risks are getting less attention.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: Automated tools in audit — AI, auditor implications and common risks

points.text: On the blockchain register, the auditors consider governance and security around the transactions: the risks where the chain interacts with legacy systems and partners through insecure application programming interfaces, data confidentiality and privacy where data crosses geographic boundaries, weak application development protocols, and the strength that is also a weakness, that transactions cannot be reversed and data cannot be accessed without the keys, so the company needs protocols and contingency plans so that it is not locked out, and compliance managers who follow the evolving regulation.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Digital Auditing and Assurance
citation.ref: Automated tools in audit — blockchain, audit implications and common risks

written.scenario: CA Palash Shah is completing the audit of the consolidated Ind AS financial statements of YK Industries Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026. The group's memorandum consolidation records show eliminations of intra-group sales, interest and balances, but no deferred tax on the unrealised profit in inventory bought from a subsidiary, and the subsidiary's inventory is still valued on a policy different from the parent's. Goodwill of ₹50 crore arose on an acquisition in June 2025 and no impairment test was done. One foreign subsidiary's statements are drawn up to 31 December 2025 because local law requires it, and management says a March closing is impracticable. A small subsidiary acquired in February 2026 is unaudited and management says it is "too small to matter". The notes repeat every disclosure from the subsidiaries' separate statements, including MSME dues and the source of a bonus issue, and give no percentages of consolidated net assets or profit.
written.question: State what Palash verifies on the adjustments and the goodwill, what he does about the December closing and the unaudited subsidiary, and what the notes should and should not contain.

points.text: Current period adjustments are made in memorandum records kept by the parent, and Palash reviews those records to verify the entries. Beyond eliminating intra-group transactions and balances, he verifies that deferred tax has been recorded under Ind AS 12 on the temporary differences arising from elimination of unrealised intra-group profit, and that the consolidated statements use uniform accounting policies for like transactions: under Ind AS 110 the subsidiary's inventory figures must be adjusted to the group's policy, since impracticability is a disclosure route only under AS 21, not under Ind AS.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Current period consolidation adjustments; the auditor's verification of memorandum records, deferred tax on eliminations and uniform accounting policies

points.text: Goodwill arising on consolidation is carried at the value determined at the date of acquisition and tested for impairment at every balance sheet date. Palash examines whether the parent has determined any impairment loss, the procedure it followed and whether the amount is fair, and performs procedures to see whether intra-group losses indicate an impairment that needs recognition; "no test was done" is not an answer to the requirement. He also verifies that the June 2025 subsidiary's income and expenses are included only from the date control was gained, based on the amounts recognised at the acquisition date.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Impairment of goodwill arising on consolidation; inclusion of a subsidiary's results from the date of control

points.text: Components should be drawn up to the parent's reporting date; where that is not practicable, adjustments are made for significant transactions or events between the component's date and the parent's, and the gap may not exceed three months under Ind AS (six months under AS). A 31 December closing is within three months of 31 March, so it can be used, but Palash reviews the subsidiary's results between the two dates for significant transactions or events that must be reflected, and ensures any change in reporting period from the prior year is disclosed for consistency.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Components drawn up to a different reporting date — the three-month and six-month limits, and review of intervening events

points.text: An unaudited component is a limitation on the evidence available for the consolidated amounts. Palash evaluates both the quantitative and the qualitative effect of the amounts remaining unaudited, using SA 705, and decides whether his report on the consolidated statements needs modification; "too small" is management's assertion, and the evaluation is his.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: Components not audited — evaluation under SA 705

points.text: Under MCA Circular 39/2014 and section 129(4), consolidated statements carry only the disclosures relevant to consolidation and do not merely repeat the separate statements' notes, so the MSME disclosure and the source of the bonus issue come out. What must go in, under Schedule III's general instructions, is the information for the parent and each component: net assets as an amount and as a percentage of consolidated net assets, share in profit or loss as an amount and a percentage, and other comprehensive income as an amount and a percentage, with consolidation adjustments shown as a single line or adjusted into those figures.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Group Audits
citation.ref: MCA Circular 39/2014; Schedule III disclosures of net assets, profit or loss and OCI for the parent and each component

written.scenario: The Comptroller and Auditor General takes up a performance audit of a State-owned power distribution company's rural electrification programme, which was to connect two lakh households in three years. The field team proposes to start by checking whether tenders followed the procurement manual, and to stop there. The company's managing director says a performance audit is "just the statutory audit with more adjectives", asks whether the auditors intend to certify anything, and wants to know where the findings will go.
written.question: Explain what a performance audit examines that a compliance audit does not, how the team should plan it, whether it is an attestation or a direct reporting engagement, and where the report goes.

points.text: Checking tenders against the manual is compliance audit: regularity, adherence to the formal criteria from laws, regulations and agreements, together with propriety, the general principles of sound financial management and official conduct. A performance audit is an objective and systematic examination of the performance of a programme to improve public accountability, and it addresses the three Es: economy, minimising the cost of resources at the right quantity, quality and price; efficiency, the input-output ratio, whether output was maximised for the inputs; and effectiveness, the extent to which objectives were achieved and the relation between the intended and the actual impact — here, whether two lakh households were connected, at what cost per connection, and whether the connections changed anything. Compliance is one aspect of that examination, not the whole of it.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings
citation.ref: Compliance audit — regularity and propriety; performance audit — economy, efficiency and effectiveness

points.text: Planning follows the C&AG's steps: understanding the entity and programme from its own documents, legislative documents including Public Accounts Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings reports, policy documents, academic research, past audits, media coverage and special focus groups; defining the objectives crisply and the scope that confines the audit to significant issues; determining the audit criteria; deciding the approach; developing audit questions; assessing whether the team's skills suffice or outside expertise is needed; preparing an audit design matrix; fixing the timetable and resources; and intimating the programme to the audited entities. The responsibility for measurable objectives and performance indicators rests with the entity, so the auditors first ask what the company set itself to measure.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings
citation.ref: Planning for performance audit — the steps and the sources for understanding the entity; Regulations on Audit and Accounts

points.text: The managing director is wrong on both counts. A performance audit, like a compliance audit, is generally a direct reporting engagement: the auditors measure the subject matter against criteria and report their own findings, rather than attesting to an assertion prepared by management as in a financial audit. Nothing is certified; the output is findings and recommendations, with the entity's responses included.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings
citation.ref: Attestation engagements and direct reporting engagements in PSU audit

points.text: The findings go into the C&AG's report to the legislature, which is presented in parts: an introduction reviewing the working results of government companies and corporations, the results of comprehensive appraisals of selected undertakings by the Audit Board, a resume of the company auditors' reports under the C&AG's directions and the comments on accounts, and significant results of audit of undertakings not taken up by the Audit Board. For a State company the results appear in the separate commercial report or the commercial chapter of the State report, and are examined by the Committee on Public Undertakings.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings
citation.ref: Audit report of the Comptroller and Auditor General — its four parts; State commercial reports

keywords: resume of the company auditors' reports

written.scenario: Sagar Refineries Ltd, a listed company, wants to appoint Mr Parteek, a retired officer of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service with a law degree and no accountancy qualification, as Chief Internal Auditor reporting to the Chief Financial Officer. The board also wants the internal audit function to run the company's SEBI compliance-tracking system and to correspond with the regulator, since "compliance with laws" is in the audit scope. The first assignment is the procurement process. The audit committee asks what the engagement will involve, what the report will look like, and whether it may be issued straight to the committee without showing procurement first.
written.question: Advise on the appointment and the reporting line, on the compliance-tracking proposal, on the steps of the procurement engagement with the standards that govern them, and on the report.

points.text: Parteek may be appointed: section 138 read with Rule 13 allows a chartered accountant, a cost accountant or such other professional as the board decides, so an accountancy qualification is not a condition. Reporting to the CFO is the wrong line for a listed company: independence must exist in mind and in appearance, the position and reporting of the Chief Internal Auditor within the structure is what establishes it, and in a listed company the internal auditor may be required to report directly to those charged with governance, the audit committee, rather than the CEO or CFO.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Internal Audit
citation.ref: Basic principles — independence in mind and appearance, reporting to the audit committee; Rule 13 — who may be internal auditor

points.text: The compliance-tracking proposal is refused. Managing the system and corresponding with the regulator is an operating responsibility; an internal auditor must avoid conflicts of interest and should not review an activity for which he was responsible, so a function that runs compliance cannot then audit it. Having "compliance with laws" in the scope means reviewing the company's compliance, not performing it, and any actual or apparent conflict is brought immediately to the appropriate level of management.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Internal Audit
citation.ref: Basic principles — conflict of interest; the Test Your Understanding case on managing a compliance-tracking system

points.text: The engagement runs in five steps in sequence: obtain knowledge of the business and its environment, including the IT landscape and the regulatory landscape; plan under SIA 310 with the scope approved by the audit committee and board, an opening meeting, and a work plan built from the major risks in the process; gather information, as far as possible directly from the source; perform audit checks with analytical procedures under SIA 6, sampling under SIA 5, evidence under SIA 320, review and supervision under SIA 350 and documentation under SIA 330; and report the issues, communicating under SIA 360 and SIA 370.

citation.source: ICAI Study Material, Paper 3 — Internal Audit
citation.ref: Performing an internal audit engagement — the five steps and the Standards on Internal Audit at each

points.text: Under SIA 370 reporting is in two stages: an Internal Audit Report at the end of each assignment, issued to the auditee with copies to local and executive management, and a periodic, normally quarterly, comprehensive report by the Chief Internal Auditor to the audit committee; SIA 370 governs the first. The assignment report includes an overview of objectives, scope and approach, a statement that the audit was conducted in accordance with the Standards on Internal Audit, an executive summary of key observations, a summary of corrective actions required or agreed, and the nature of assurance if any — with findings rated, root causes and business impact explained, and management's action plan and timelines. No report may be issued in final form unless a written draft was previously shared with the auditee, so procurement sees it first; and actual or suspected fraud is brought to management immediately, not held for the report.

citation.ref: Reporting Results — the two stages, the elements of the Internal Audit Report, and the draft to the auditee

points.text: Afterwards, under SIA 390 the Chief Internal Auditor monitors closure of the agreed action plans through a formal process pre-agreed with management and those charged with governance, and reports open matters as an action taken report; implementation stays management's responsibility.

citation.ref: Monitoring and Reporting of Prior Audit Issues — the action taken report

written.scenario: Sahyadri Bank asks CA Mehra to investigate Tungabhadra Foods Ltd, which has applied for a ₹30 crore term loan to add a processing line, before the credit committee decides. The bank's letter says only "look at the company". The company's last balance sheet shows receivables of ₹22 crore with no ageing, inventory valued "at cost", and a recently revalued factory. Mehra's junior proposes to verify the whole of the last year's transactions, and to write the report as a list of everything found.
written.question: State how Mehra settles the scope and programme, what he collects for the bank, how he schedules the receivables and inventory, and how the report is written.
